Welding processes include Resistance Welding (Spot Welding), Arc Welding and Gas Welding (and cutting).

Resistance Welding (Spot Welding)

This process may cause particles of molten metal to be emitted at a high velocity, and the eyes and skin must be protected

Arc Welding

This process emits a high level of ultraviolet radiation which may cause arc-eye and skin bums to the operator and to other persons neary. Gas-shielded welding processes are particularly hazardous in'this respect. Personal protection must be wom, and screens used to shield other people.

CONTACT LENS WEARERS ARE ADVISED TO REVERT TO ORDINARY SPECTACLES WHEN ARC WELDING as the arC SpEctrum iS believed to emit microwaves which dry out the fluid between the lens and the eye. This may result in blindness when the len is removed from the eye.

Metal spatter will also occur, and appropriate eye and skin protection is necessary.

The heat of the welding arc will produce fumes and gases from the metals being welded, the rods and from any applied coatings or contamination on the surfaces being worked on.These gases and fumes may be toxic and inhalation of these should bevoidedThe use oextracion ventiti t remove the fumesrom the workig area may be eessary particulaly in cases where the general ventilation is poor or where considerable welding work isanticipated. In extreme cases or confined spaces where adequate ventilation cannot be provided, air-fed respirators may be necessary.

Gas Welding (and Cutting)

Oxy-acetylene torches may be used for welding and cutting and special care must be taken to prevent leakage of these gases with consequent risk of fire and explosion.

The process will produce metal spatter and eye and skin protection is necessary.

The flame is bright, and eye protection should be used, but the ultraviolet emissin is much lessthan that from ar welding, and lighter filters may be used.

The processitself produces few toxic fumes, but such fumes and gases may be produced from coatings on the work, particularly during cutting away of damaged body parts, and inhalation of the fumes should be avoided.

In brazing, toxic fumes may be produced from the metals in the brazing rod and a severe hazard may arise if brazing rods oaiing camim areusedthisent particularcare must e takent aidalati o fumesandexpert vicmay be required.

SPECIAL PRECAUTIONS MUST BE TAKEN BEFORE ANY WELDING OR CUTTING TAKES PLACE ON VESSELS WHICH HAVECONTAINED COMBUSTIBLE MATERIALS, E.G. BOILING OR STEAMING OUT OF FUEL TANKS.

Local regulations for the towing of vehicles must be follwed. In some countries the registration number of the towing vehicle and an 'On Tow' sign or warning triangle must be displayed at the rear of the towed vehicle. 24-80 km/h (15-50 miles/h): With light aceleration, a moaning noise is heard and possbly a vibration is felt in the front floor pan. It may also produce a moaning sound, depending on what component i causing i Refert Tip-In Moanin the Symptom Chart.

Accleration/deceleration: With slow acceleration and deceleration, a shake is sometimes noticed in the steering wheel/column, seats, front floor pan, front door trim panel or front end sheet metal. It is a low frequency vibration around 9- cycles per second. I may or may not e inreased by appling brakesghty. Refer to de Boom/Shake /Vibration in the Symptom Chart.

High speed: A vibration i felt in the front floor pan or seats with no visible shake, but with an accompanying sound or rumble, buzz, hum, drone or booming noise. Coast with the clutch pedal depressed or shift control selector lever in neutral and engine iding. If vibration is stillevident, it may be related to wheels, tires, front brake discs, whee hubs or front wheel bearings. Refer to High Speed Shake in the Symptom Chart.

Engine pm sensitive: A vibration is felt whenever the engine reaches a particular pm. It will disappear in neutral coasts. The vibration can be duplicated by operating the engine at the problem pm while the vehicle is stationary. It can be caused by any component, from the accessory drive belt to the torque converter which tums at engine speed when the vehicle is stopped. Refer to High Speed Shake in the Symptom Chart.

Noise/vibration while tuning: Clicking, popping, or grinding noises may be due to a wom, damaged, or incorectly installed front wheel bearin, rear drive half shaft or CV joint.

Noise/ibration that is road speed relative: This noise/vibration can be diagnosed independent of engine speed or gear selected (engine speed varies but torque and road speed remain constant). The cause may be a rear drive axle/differential whine.

EDC (engine drag-torque control) prevents wheel slip caused by any of the following:

A downshift using the Jauar sequential shift function on automatic transmission vehicles.

An active wheel speed sensori installed in each wheel hub to provide the AS module with a rotational speed signal from each road wheel. The head of each front wheel speed sensor is poitioned close to a magneti encoderring incororated into the iboard seal of the wheel bearing.The head of each rear wheel speed sensor is positined close to a magetic encoder rig icorporated into the rear wheel bearing assembly. Each encoder ring contains 46 north and south poles. A fly lead connects each sensor to the vehicle hamness.

The wheel speed sensors each have a signal and a retum connection with the ABS module. When the ignition is ON the ABS module supplies a signal feed to the wheel speed sensors and monitors the retum signals. Any rotation of the road wheels induces curent fluctations in the retum signals, which are converted into individual wheel speeds and overall vehile speed by the ABS module.

The ABS module broadcasts the individual wheel speeds and the vehicle speed on the high speed CAN bus for use by other systems, although vehicle speed information to the roof opening panel motor/module is  hardwired connection.

Ifa wheel speed sensor fault is deteted by the ABS module, ABS FAULT will be displaed in the instrument cluster message center and an amber warning indicator will illuminate.

As the wheel speed sensors are active devices, aretum signal is availale when the road wheel are not rtating. This enables the ABs module to check the condition of the speed sensors while the vehicle is stationary.

### Rear Crankshaft Oil Seal


The 3.0 liter dieselengine is a  coiguation unit with 2 banks of 3 cylinders aranged at 60 degrees to each other. There are 4 valves per cylinder, which are operated by 2 overhead camshafts per cylinder bank.

The cylinder block is cast in compacted graphite iron, which usesless material to produce compared to a coventional cast io block. This provides reduced weight and length with superior structural capabilities.A separate aluminum lader frame, bolted to the underside of the cylinder block, provies a lightweight, compact and very stiff bottom end of the engine.

The cylinder heads are cast luminum with a moulded plastic camshaft cover with an integral ir intake.The single-piece il afomedfrom stampedsteelThe exhaust manifold are cast from an iron al. moulded plasticacousticoverfitte over the upper engine to' absorb engine-generated noise.

A low compresson ratio of 16:1 contributes to improved emissions quality, quieter combustion and compatibility with the engine's unique forced induction system. For additional inforation refer to Intake Air distriution and iltering.

The low compression ratio also means less heat build-up in the piston bowl and more efficient fuel bum, resulting in the production of lower levels of pollutants. It also assists with cold starting allowing a faster cranking speed.

Operation of the engine is cntrolled by the EM (engine control module. Fordtionl ifomatio refert 303-14A Elctron Engine Controls.

![](images/_MISSING_a64afbf5c9dc4da1505fb662c18c6d6bb049a98d259e09ef245305049463c69f.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_1b75894083b43ff8c52e3ff6e5ffaac166f66f63c189bb7c09e2222fd27722ca.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_004d27fbf3d8b15884e289dc0957df6ea3baa68767d42d12c2b5fc5b14d1745b.jpg)

The cylinder block is a single cast construction with a hollow beam structure, cast from compact graphite iron. This type of construction provides outstanding strength and durability and uses lessmaterial than a conventional cast iron block, therefore reducing engine weight and length.

The use of compact graphite iron allows the cross sectional areas of the casting to be reduced, compared with a convention gray cast iron block. This ensures reduced engine weight and length, with highr structural capabilities.

To maintain the stiffessof the bottom end of the cylinder block and crankshaft system, the clinderblock has a deep skirt and bearing cap desig. Each of the main bearing caps is double bolted at each side of the crankshaft bearing and cross bolte back to the cylinder block.

The cylinder block assembly is further stiffened by couplig it to a separate die cast aluminium stiffening frame, which is bolted to the cylinder block skirt faces and to the bearing caps.

Lubricationilidistributed through the ylinderblock,via a main oil gally and channels bored n the blockto all ritial moving parts. These channels divert oil to the main and connecting rod bearings via holes machined into the crankshaft.

A tapping at the rear of the cylinderblock connects a pipe to the turochargers by means of banjo connections. il is supplied, under pressure via this tapping, from the oil pump to provide lubrication for the bearings of the turbochargers.

Cylinder cooling is achieved by coolant circulating through chambers in the cylinder block casting.

Two hollow metal dowels are used to locate the cylinder heads to the clinder block, 1 on each side at the rearof the unit.

A port is icluded at the RH (right-hand and (left-handside of the ylinder block, below each of the turbochargers, to connect the turbochargers oil rètur pipé to the oil pan.

Two coolant drin plugs are istalledin the clinderblock; one is fited in the rear RH side and the otherifited in the middle of the cylinder block on the LH side.

The cylinder head gasket i a layer aminated stee type and s ilable in diffrent thicknesses.The choice of gasket thickness is dependent on the maximum piston protrusion. Gasket thickness is identified by serations cut into the front end of the gasket.

The clinder head has4 ports machined at each cylinder loation, 2 exhaust ports and intake ports. One of the intake ports s helical and functions as a swirl port, the other is arranged laterally as a tangential port and functions as a charge port.

The camshafts are of a hollow steel tube construction, with pressed on sintered lobes. Each camshaft is retained by aluminum ally caps, 5 for theexhaust camshafts and 4 for the itake camshafts. The LH cylinder bank exhaust camshaft is machined to accept a rear camshaft gear. The rear camshaft gear provides drive fo the high-pressure fuel pump.   
Refer to: Fuel Charging and Controls (303-04C Fuel Charging and Controls - V8 5.0L Petrol, Description and Operation).   
The exhaust camshaft gear of the LH cylinder head also incorporates a trigger wheel, which is used in conjunction with the camshaft sensor to measure engine position.   
Refer To: Electronic Engine Controls (303-14A Electronic Engine Controls- TDV6 3.0L Diesel, Description and Operation).   
The RH cylinder head exhaust camshaft is machined at the rear end to provide a drive connection for the vacum pump.   
The fuel injection nozzles are centrally mounted above each cylinder.   
Refer to: Fuel Charging and Controls (303-04A Fuel Charging and Controls - TDV6 3.0L Diesel, Description and Operation).   
The glow plug are arranged centrally on the intake side of the ylinderheads, between the intake ports of each cylinder.   
Refer to: Glow Plug System (303-07B Glow Plug System - TDV6 3.0L Diesel, Description and Operation).   
The engine lifting eyes are bolted to the cylinder head, 1 at the front and 2 at the rear, 1 per cylinder head.

![](images/_MISSING_46edac5f899c5507b1c83f4821d64e63c4202dc879ff31678c2a725c5fdfdcbe.jpg)

16cAUTION: Make sure the seal is installed correctly.

Remove the special tool. Remove and discard the crankshaft pulley retaining bolt.

![](images/_MISSING_37a5ede2f1eff4cb77bc633c3f2d10ba6d246937669fab44d3bb57284570944f.jpg)

17. CAUTION: Make sure that a new crankshaft pulley bolt is installed.

NOTE: Before installing the crankshaft pulley retaining bolt, note the thread size of the bolt (there are two différent sized threads, M14 and M16). Failure to follow this instruction may result in damage to the vehicle.

Install the crankshaft pulley. Tighten the M14 retaining bolt in two stages: 1. Stage one: Tighten to 140 Nm. . Stage two: Tighten a further 90degrees. Tighten the M16 retaining bolt in three stages: 1. Stage one: Tighten to 150 Nm. 2. Stage two: Tighten to 300 Nm. 3. Stage three: Tighten a further 90 degrees.

The engine coling system maintains the engine within an optimum temperature range under changing ambient and engine operating conditions. It also provides:

Heating for the passenger compartment. For additional information refer to Heating and Ventilation 412-01.   
Cooling for: -The engine oil - The fuel - The EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) system - Refer to: Engine Emission Control (303-08A Engine Emission Control - TDV6 3.0L Diesel, Description and Operation. - The transmission fluid.

Whenthe engine is runing he colant i cirulatedaround the engine cooling system by the coolant pump. From the coolant pump,cooantfowsthrough the clinderblockand the clinderheadSome othe coolant ithe linderblck diverted through the engine oil cooler before returning to the 5-way connector via the water outlet.

From theway coector the majority of theoolant flows to the pressurelif therostat ither irectly or via the iator depending on the temperature of the coolant. Some of the coolant is also directed through the uxiliary cooling radiators returning the cooled coolant to the Pressure Relief Thermostat (PR) via the radiator bottom hose. From the outlet of the thermostat the coolant flows to the inlet of the coolant pump.

Aseparate hose from the radiatoallows extra-cooled coolant from the raiator to flow through the trasmission oil cooler.Th coolant from the cooler is retumed to the system via a branch in the bottom radiator hose.

Coolant from the wateroutlet also flows through the EGR (exhaust gas reirulation) coolers and then to the heater core. From he heater core outlet, the coolant flows to the outlet zone of the pressure relief thérmostat.

The expansion tank allows expansion of coolant due to temperature increases to pass excess coolant back to the expansion tank. A small hose is connected from the water outlet to the expansion tank for this purpose.As the coolant coos, the coolant is allowed back into the system from the tank via a hose from the expansion tank into the radiator bottom hose.

The 3.0L  dieselengine is equipped with a High Pressure (HP) common rail fuel injection system. With this fuel ijection process a HP pump dlivers a uniform level of pressure to the hared fuel lines (the common rails), which serve allfuel injectors. Pressure is controlled to the optimum level for smooth operation.

The common rail system supports a pre and pilot injection depending on engine operating conditions, which reduces combustion noise levels, more commonly referred tó as 'diesel knock'.

Fuel injection pressure is generated independently of engine speed and fuel injection events.

he ful injetiontiming and vlume ar calulated by the M (engine control module, which then energizes the appropriat iezo actuàted injector. The common rail fuel injection system has the following features:

High fuel ijection pressures of up to 2000 bar (29007 f/in² for greater atomization of fuel (increasing performance and lowering emissions).   
•Variable injection to optimize combustion in all engine operating conditions Low tolerances and high precision throughout the life of the system.

The fuel system is divided into two sub systems:

Low Pressure (LP) system HP system.

The LP system features the following components:

In-tank fuel pump   
Fuel pressure regulator (integral to the fuel delivery module) Fuel filter   
Return pipes   
Injector retumn pipes   
Fuel coolers engine and vehicle).

The LP system is regulated to 0.5 bar (7.25 Ibf/in²).

The HP system features the following components:

HP pump   
Fuel rails and diverter rail HP fuel pipes   
Injectors.

During starting, the fuel il pressure must beat least15 bar(2175 fn².Should the pressure be below thi figure, the injecs will not erateeti the eicle not saing.

To stop the engine the EM (engine control module) stops energiing the actators in the fuel ijectors, therefore, no fuel is injected and the engine speed drops to zero. Refer to: Electronic Engine Controls (303-14A Electronic Engine Controls - TDV6 3.0L Diesel, Description and Operation).

The 3.  desel eine uses thars; a ixed vane type (eoday) and  varleane (primay type.The ie aeaet teitandline an nd te arle a eite te (left-hand) cylinder bank.

Both turochargers are used in a parall sequential turocharging system which enables the engine to achieve quick throttle response at low engine speeds and efficient use of exhaust gas energy at high engine speeds.

The variable vane turchargerhas an EM (engine control module cotrolled electronic rotary actuatorThe rotary actuator adjusts the turine vanes to optimize the exhast gas flow and velocity onto the turbine whee to maintain the required boo pressure.

The parallel sequential turbocharging system comprises the two turbochargers and the EM. The primary variable nozzle turbine perates through the entire engine speed range but i at it most eficient at engine speeds of up to 2800 m. At engine speeds above 2800 rpm under load, the fixed vane secondary turbine comes into operation, with both of the turbochargers now running in a parallel bi-turbo mode.

The turbine wheel of the turocharger uses the engine's exhaust gasses to drive the compressor wheel. The compressor wheel draws in fresh air which is supplied to the engine cylinders in a compressed form.

The primary ariable vane turchargerallws the optimum ilet geometry inlet area and flow angle) to be used overa wide rage of engie perating conditionsThisllws  rapid speedof esponse and higher boost pressures at low engie speed. erleaedie  thee aelae ecl ee module.The variable vanes allow effient use of the exhaust gas energ which in tum improves trochargerand engine efficieny.

Principles of Variable Vane Operation

![](images/_MISSING_fd6ff7d7538b02c2835bf3c6603f7ade0268363fbfceef905a87614cc359d56f.jpg)

E107579

![](images/_MISSING_cb2baccf7f7eed99b9dbee5ec28f90d3e884c570877655b4aba018ba927e46b8.jpg)

The variable vanes in the primary turocharger are controlled by the EM. The ECM controls a rotary electronic actuator aached t the primary th wich iused to ajust the pitch angeof the vanes by rotatig the turineousig.he electronic rotary actator also providesthe  with a feedack signal to detemine the pitch ange of the vanes.

The variable vanes in the primary turocharger improve the exhaust gas power transfer to the turine wheel which in tum drives the compressor wheel At low engine speeds this greatly assists the increase in turbocharger boost pressure.

As engine speed, and therefore the exhaust gas velocity, increases, the vanes are opened. The amount of opening is determined by the ECM to ensure that the power transfer from the turbine wheel to the compressor wheel is within the turbocharger speed and boost pressure requirements.

At high engine speed and exhaust gas flow, the ECM increases the vane opening to avoid overspeed of the turbines and provie a smooth high speed operation. At this point the dual mode boosting system comes into affect by utilizing the secondary (fixed vane) turbocharger.

The dual mode boosting system comprises two turbochargers and software within the ECM. The two turbochargers can operat in two modes; mono turbocharger operation or bi-turbocharger operation.

When the engine operating parameters approach the limits (approximately 2800 rpm under load) of the primary turbocharger,

dual mode bosting control software within the ECM begins the switch to parall bi-turbocharger operation. The secondary turbocharger is brought into operation by the opening of the turine shutof valve which allows exhaust gasses to flow through the turbine.

Initially the seconday turocharger does not produce a boost pressureto equal that of the primary trchargerTherefre, the itial oost pressure from theseondary turhrgr fed vi the reiulati valvet the clean iriet fothe primary turochargerAs the seonday turchargerboost pressure output increases, the reiulation valve ithen cosed and the compressor shut-of valve opened to increase the boost pressure from the secondary trocharger which is directed into the charge air cooler.

The haessfor each bank conectinto a coecto block which attachest each of the ow plug forthat bank.The ow plugs are conected directly to the glow plug module which is controlled by glow plug software contined within the ECM (engine control module).

Pre heating Crank heating Post heating

Pre-heat is the length of time the glow plugs perate prior to engine cranking.The ECM controls the pre-heat time based on outut t ol te T esi e  willsehe Taeiees asa default value.The pre-eat duration is extended if the coolant temperature is low and the battery is not fully charged.

The ECM receives the corresponding temperature signal from the ECT sensor.

The EGR (exhaust gas reirulation) system is used to control the amount of exhaust gas being recirulated in order to reduce exhaust emissions and combustion noise. EGR is enabled when the engine is at normal operating temperature and under cruising conditions.

he crankcase ventilation system ensures that al gasses emitted from the crankcase during engine running are separated from any oil particles and recirculated via the clean air iñduction system.

Crankcase gasses are drawn into the oil separator unit from the crankcase and the cylinder head covers (both banks) by a vacuum created by a connection into the air induction system.

The crankcase gasses are ciulated around the oil separator where the as and oil are separated The gass retumed to the inet side ofthe idutio systempriorto the primartocarerThe collectedil dined dow to the ump i the cooler and filter housing on the cylinder block.

EGR System Control Components

![](images/_MISSING_96c783214a62e8bfe868e82ee25b61017032b081d0fbf3a8177d0eb57d738f7f.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_369475bf105e713c06c516c5aedc500434571bb063d82b87847cf0036f7189ba.jpg)

The EGR system comprises an EGR cooer and housing assembly which is bolted to the cylinder head, above the exhaust manifold Each EGRassembly comprises a EGR cooler, a by-pass housing a bypass alve motoranda by-pass valve vauum actuator.

A pipe is connected to the exhaust manifold and directs exhaust gasses into the by-passhousing. A second pipe from the by-pass housing connects to the throttle intake manifold and passes the cooled exhaust gasses into the intake manifold to mix with the clan air entering the engine from the air filter.

The EGR coler is attached to the by-pass housing with a gasket and 5 screws. The by-pass housing has an engine colant coection wich allws coolant to fw rom the engiei coolerintthe yass housing Engie coant fws fromthe bypass housing into a water jacket within the cooler which in cools the exhaust gasses by heat transfer within the cooler. The enine coolant flows from the coolerthrough an outlet pipe and i passed back into the cooling system via the heater core.

The by-pass housing contains the EGR valve motor, the EGR valve and the by-pass valve.

By-pass Housing Components

![](images/_MISSING_36e87a21c6648c18f2c0c3e62363ff79e8aa941e1bd36b07840f05c03fdad0ec.jpg)

E107585

![](images/_MISSING_82df691b9a1d58ce232c35d4274bcd8bc419f104ca5d81431ef79040be2ce614.jpg)

The crankcase ventilation system comprises an oil breather and separator. The breather receives crankcase directly from the crankcase and also from thé cylinder heads.

The breather is connected to the top of the cylinder block with two seals. wo scavenge pipes located on the top of the breather are coected to the cylinder head covers.A breather pipe is conected from the top of the breather to the cleana intake hose at a point prior to the primary turbocharger.

Clean air being daw into the egine when it s rnig creates  vauum in the breather pipe.This vacm i tum creates a vacum in the oil breather and separator which draws gasses from the crankcase and cylinder heads into the breather. These gasses are cirulatedaround the brather allwing l parties to be separated from the gas.The gasses are drawn into the breather pipe and are mixed with the clean air being drawn into the turbocharger.

he il particles separated from the gasses accumulate in the il separator and drain through a third coectin at the bottom of the oil breather and separator, through a connection on the oil cooler housing to the oil pan.

The 3.L V diesel engine has an ECM controlled engine management system. Multiple sensor inputs and precision control of actuators are used by the ECM to achieve optimum performance during áll driving conditions.

The ECM receives and processes information from the following input sources:

•Oil level sensor   
Secondary turbocharger shut-off sensor   
Secondary turbocharger boost pressure sensor   
• Alterator Differential pressure sensor Camshaft Position (CMP) sensor Crankshaft Position (CKP) sensor Fuel rail pressure sensor Fuel temperature sensor   
Air charge temperature sensor   
Engine oolant Temperature (ECT) sensor   
Throttle Position (TP) sensor   
Mass Air Flow (MA / Intake Air Temperature A) sensor   
Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor   
EGR sensors HO2S   
Catalyst and Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) temperature sensors   
Brake lamp switch

The Engine Control Module (ECM) outputs controling signals to the following sensors and actuators:

Air Conditioning (A/C) compressor clutch solenoid   
A/C compressor clutch   
Fuel injectors   
Glow plug module   
Fuel pressure control valve el olume control valve Fan control module Vacuum control valves (EGR cooler by-pass secondary turbocharger compressor shut-off secondary turbocharger turbine shut-off) ABS module Transmission Control Module (TCM) Instrument cluster Restraints Control Module (RCM) Primary turbocharger control module EGR recirculation valves Alternator Throttle actuator   
Secondary turbocharger compressor recirculation valve   
Active engine mount' solenoid valve.

The 3.L  diesel engine management system is contrld by an ECM (engine control module and is able to monitor adapt and precisely control the fuel ijection.The EM uses multiple sensoriputs and precision control of actuators to achieve optimum performance during all driving conditions.

The ECM uses the drive by wire principle for acceleration control. There are no control cables or physical connections between the accelerator pedal and the engine.Accelerator pedal demand is communicated to the EM by two potentiometers located in an APP(accelerator pedal position) sensor. The ECM uses the two signals to determine the position, rate of movement and direction of movement of the peda. The ECM then uses this data, along with other engine infomation from other sensors, to achieve the optimum engine response.

The ECM is located on a bracket on the passenger side of the engine compartment bulkhead.

The ECM connected to the vehicle hamesses via 2 connectors. The ECM contains data processors and memory microchips. The output signals to the actators are in the form of ground paths provided by driver ciruit within the EM. This avoids incorrect signals caused by voltage drop during cranking.

When a new ECM is fitted, it must also be synchronized to other system control modules using a Jaguar approved diagnostic system. ECM's cannot be 'swapped' between' vehicles as they must be 'matched' with security information to other system modules

The ECM is connected to the engine sensors which allw it to monitor the engine operating conditions. The ECM processes these signals and decides the actions necessary to maintain optimum engine performance in terms of drive ability, fuel efficiency andexhaust emissions. The CP (crankshaft position) sensor is located at the ear of the engine block on the  leftandside. The sensor lead passes through a coveri an aperture on the side ofthe engine block.The sensor is secured to a bracket on a plate which locates therear crankshaft oil seal. The sensortpis aligned with a maeti triggereluctor whee which i attached to the end ofthe akshaftThe tre wheel is a pressfit n the end of the kshafThergerwheel must e afullye to the crankshaft to ensure corect timing.The sensor produces a square wave signal, the frequency of which is proportionl to engine speed.

The ECM monitors the CKP sensor signal and can detect engine over-speed. The ECM counteracts engine over-speed by graduall fading out speed synchronized functions. The CP is a Halleffect sensor. The sensor measures the magneti field variation induced by the magnetized trigger wheel.

The trigger wheel has a 60 minus 2 tooth pattem. The missing teeth represent 12 of crankshaft rotation and provide a reference point for the angular position of the crankshaft at 2 BTDC (before top dead center) on cylinder 1.

When the space with the two missing teeth pass the sensor tip, a gap in the signal is produced which the ECM uses to determine the crankshaft position.The ir gap between the sensortip and the ring is important to ensure corect sigals are output to the ECM. The recommended air gp between the CKP and the trigger wheel is 0.4 mm- 1.5 mm.

The ECM uses the signal from the CKP sensor for the following functions:

Synchronization   
Determine fuel injection timing   
Produce an engine speed signal which is broadcast on the high speed CAN bus for use by other systems.

The T (enine coolant tmperture) sensoris located inthe LH EGR cooler coolant iet pipe, at the font of theengine.The ECT sensor provides the ECM and the instrument cluster with engine coolant temperature status.

The ECM uses the temperature information for the following functions:

Fuelling calculations

The instrument custer uses the temperature infomation for gneration ofengine temperature messages.The engine coolant temperature signal is also transmitted on the medium speed CAN bus by the instrument cluster for use by other systems.

The ECT sensor circuit consists of an intemal voltage divider circuit which incorporates an NTC thermistor As the coolant temperature rises the resistance through the sensor dereases and vice versa. The output from the sensor is the change in voltage as the thermistor allows more current to pass to ground relative to the temperature of the coolant.

The ECM compares the signal voltage to stored values and adjusts fuel delivery to ensure optimum drive ability at al times. The engine willequire more fuel when it cold to verome fuel condensing n the cold metal surfaesinside the combustior chamber. To achieve a richer air/fuel ratio, the ECM extends the ijector pening time. As the engine warms up the irfuel ratio is leaned off.

If the ECt sensor fails, the following symptoms may be observed:

Difficult cold start   
Difficult hot start   
Engine performance compromised   
Temperature gauge inoperative or inaccurate reading.

In the event of ECT sensor signal failure, the ECM applies a default value of 80°Celsius (176°F) coolant temperature for fuelling purposes. The ECM will lso permanently operate the cooling fan at all imes when the ignition is switched on, to protect the 'engine from overheating.

he secondary turbocharger boost pressure sensor is located on the steering pump mounting bracket on the RH side of the ngine. The sensor is conected via a hose to the charge air outlet pipe from the primary turbocharger compressor.

The boost pressure sensor uses a diaphragm transducer to measure pressure.The ECM uses the boost pressure sensor signa for the following functions:

To help smooth control of the mono to bi and bi to mono turbo transitions To aid the air path diagnostics.

The secondary turocharger turbine position sensor is located on the turbine vacum shut-offvalve. The sensor has three connections to the ECM; a 5V reference voltage, a ground and a signal return.

The engine management system provides accurately metered quantities of fuel to the combustion chambers to ensure the most effcient use of fuel and to minimise the exhaust emissions. To further reduce the carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons content of the exhaust gases, a catalytic converter is iterated into each front pipe of the ehaust system. In the catalyti converter the exhaust gases are passed through honeycombed ceramic elements coated with a special surface treatment called ahcoatThe washcat creases the surface area othe ceramiclements by a acto opproximately 00nto othe washcoat i a coating containing platinum and palladium, which are the active constituents for converting harful emissions into inert by-product. The platinum and palldium add oxygen to the carbon monoxide and the hydrocarbons in the exhaust gases, to convert them into carbon dioxide and water respectively.

Passive regeneration requires no special engine management intervention and occurs during normal engine operation. The passive reeneration involves a slow conversion of the particulate matter deposited in the F into carbon dioxide. This process occurs when the DPF temperature exceeds 250°C (482°F) and is a continuous process when the vehicle is being driven at higher engine loads and speeds.

During passive regeneration, only a portion of the particulate matter is converted into carbon dioxide. This is because the chemical eaction, which utilises nitrogen dioxide, is slower than the rate of engine production of particulate matter and is effective from 250°C (482°F).

Above 580C the conversion eficiency of the particulates into carbon dioxide rapidly increases. These temperatures are generally only be achieved using the active regeneration process.

The porous surfae of the filter consists of thousands of smallparall channels positioned in the longitudinal drection of the exhaust system. Adjacent channels i the filter are altemately plugged at the end. This design forces the ehaust gasses to flow through the porous fiter wall, which act as the fiter medium. There are two variants of speed control available, a standard system and an adaptive system. The standard system maintains aset speed selected by the driveruntil peration i suspended or canceld by a further iput from the driver and iscontrolled by the M (engine control module.The daptive system includes the same functionality asthe standard system, but also has the ability to:

Reduce vehicle speed, to less than the set speed, in order to maintain a selected distance behind a slower moving vehicle   
Acelerate the vehicle back to the set speed, once the way ahead is clear, after reducing the set speed because of a slower moving vehicle   
Alert the driver when the vehicle comes within a given distance of a slower moving vehicle.

The speed control system is integrated with the engine management system and uses fueling intervention to automatically maintain a set vehile speed. Once engaged, the system can also be used to accelerate the vehicle without using the accelerator pedal. The speed control system comprises the following components:

•'+' and '-' (set/accelerate and decelerate) steering wheel switches Resume switch   
Cancel switch   
Clock spring   
Speed control warning indicator.

The speed control system also uses inputs from the brake pedal switch, the APP (accelerator pedal position) sensor the ECl (engine control module) and the ABs (anti-lock brake system) module.

The speed control i operated by the driver using only the steering wheel witches. When speed control is active, the ECM reateheu it diiateeaueppaeaiit set speed.

During speed control operation, the ECM controls vehicle speed by adjusting fuel injection duration and timing. When the accelerator pedal is pressed with speed control ative, the M output a calulate throttle angleignal in placeof the actl throttle angle signals produced by the APP sensor. The calculated throttle angle is derived from fuel demand based on the torque required to overcome the rolling resistance (vehicle motion drag).

The minimum set speed for speed control is 20 mph (32 (km/h). Speed control is automatical suspended if the following conditions apply:

Vehicle speed falls below 20 mph (32 km/h).   
The brake pedal is pressed.   
The cancel button is pressed.   
Neutral, park or reverse gear is selected.   
The difference between actual speed and the set speed is too great.   
If the accelerator pedal is used to accelerate beyond the set speed for too long (more than 5 minutes).   
•Stability control system intervention System error causes shut-off.

There are 4 standard speed control switches:

Set speed + accelerate switch Decelerate - switch   
Cancel switch   
Resume switch.

The standard speed control witches are located on the RH (righthand side of the steering wheel. The switches are resistive ladder type switches which vary the resistance of a voltage signal sent to them. The PATS (passive anti-theft system) prevents the vehicle's engine from being started by unauthorized persons.

ngine starting is prevented by inibiting the fuel, engine (spark, injectors and crank) and ignition systems from operatin

his is achieved by using a uniquely coded Smart Key and an encoded data exchange between multiple control modules.

The system is automatic and requires no input from the driver.

The engine start system is initiated when the encoded data between the Smart Key and vehicle control modules is verified. The enine can then be started when the drive selectoris in the 'Park' poition, and the start/stop witch and the brake pedal are pressed simultaneously.

Ifthe vehicle has been unlocked using the emergency key blade or the Smart Key is not detected by the vehicle  will be necessary to use the keyless start bak-up system to disarm the alarm and start the engine. The following process must be followed in this event:

btain allthe data for the vehicle, including type, vehicle ientification number, trim code, engine identification letters, initial registration etc

Chemical Materials - Do's

Do carefull read and observe hazard and precaution warings given on material containers (labels) and in any accompanying leaflets, posters or other instructions. Material health and safety data sheets can be obtained from manufacturers Do remove chemical materials from the skin and clothing as soon as practical after soiling. Change heavily soiled clothing and have it cleaned Do orgnise work practices and protective clothing to avoid soiling of the skin and eyes, and the breathing in of vapors, aerosols, dusts or fumes Do wash before breaks, before eating, smoking, drinking or using toilet facilities when handing chemical materials   
Do keep work areas clean, uncluttered and free from spills   
Do store chemical materials according to national and local regulations   
Do keep chemical materials out of the reach of children

Chemical Materials - Do Nots

Do not mix chemical materials except under the manufacturer's instructions; some chemicals can form other toxic or harmful chemicals, give off toxic or harmful fumes or become explosive when mixed together   
Do not spray chemical materials, particularly those based on solvents, in confined spaces e.g when people are inside vehicle Do not apply heat or flame to chemical materials except under the manufacturer's instructions. Some are highly flammabie and some may release toxic or harmful fumes Do not leave containers open. Fumes given offcan build up to toxic, harmful or explosive concentrations. Some fumes are heavier than air and will accumulate in confined areas, pits etc. Do not transfer chemical materials to unlabeled containers Do not clean hands or clothing with chemicals. Chemicals, particularly solvents and fuels, willdry skin and may cause iritation leading to dermatitis or be absorbed through the skin in toxic or harmful quantities Do not use emptied containers for other materials except when they have been cleaned under supervised conditions   
Do not sniff or smel chemical materials. Brief exposure to high concentrations of fumes can be toxic or harmful

High concentrations wil cause eye, nose and throat iitation, nausea, headache depression and symptoms of drunkenness. Very high concentrations wil result in rapid loss of consciousness.

Ensure there is adequate ventilation when handling and using gasoline. Great care must be taken to avoid the serious consequences of inhalation in the event of vapor build up ariing from spillages in confined spaces.

Special precautions apply to cleaning and maintenance operations on gasoline storage tanks.

Carry out a road test to compare actual vehicle braking performance with the performance standards expected by the driver.   
he ability of the test driver to make valid comparisons and detect performance deficiencies will depend on experience.

he driver should have a thorough knowledge of brake system operation and accepted general performance guidelines to mak jood comparisons and detect performance concerns.

Once the route is established and consistently used, the road surface variable can be eliminated from the test results.

Before a road test, obtain a complete description of the customer concems or suspected condition. From the description, the technician's experience willlow the technician to match possible causes with symptoms.Certain components wilbe tagged as possible suspects while others willbe eliminated by the evidence. More importantly, the customer description can revel unsafe conditions which should be checked or corrected before the road test.The description willalso help form the basic approach to the road test by narowing the concern to specific components, vehicle speed or conditions.

Begin the road test with a general brake perfomance check. a concem exists, use the Symptom Chart in order to isolateit to a specific sub-system and condition description. Fromth escription, a list of possible sources can be used to further narrow the cause to a 'specific component or condition.

### PARKING BRAKE ACTUATOR


he parking brake is an electricall actuated system that perates on the rear brake calipers.Cables are connected to therear rake calipers, and act directly on the same pistons used for normal, hydraulic rear brake actuation.

The parking brake iscontrold by the E electronic parking brake module.n response to commands from the drivertrough thearking brakeitch the  module control perati othe parking brake acatorThe atatoadjustthe tesio the brake cables to apply and release the rear brake calipers. Features of the parking brake include:

Manual apply.   
Manual release.   
Automatic release.

A service routine to release cale tension, using Jaguarapproved diaosti equipment, must be perfomed prior to working on the EPB system. This decouples the components, to prevent damage to the actuator, and inhibits al parking brake switch functions. There is also a procedure for the emergency release of cable tension. Refer to: Parking Brake Cable Tensin Release (06- Parking Brake and Actuation, General Procedures).

The EPB module receives a vehicle speedsignal from theABS (anti-lock brake system) module n the high speed CAN bus. If the parking brake witch is puld to the apply position and veice speed i lessthan mph ( k/h), te  module will instigate the static apply mode and drive the actuator to apply full parking brake force to the rear wheels.

The EPB module monitors the current drawn by the actuator and compares this to information held within its configuration software to determine when full braking force 'has been applied.

There are two dynamic appy modes; low speed dynamic and high speed dynamic. The low speed dynamic mode operates at speeds between 2 and 20 mph  nd 32 km/h).The high speed dnamicmode perates a speeabove 20 mph (2 k.

fthe parking brake switch is pulled up to the apply position and vehicle speed is within the low speed dynamic range, the EP nodulé drives the actuator to apply full parking brake force to the rear wheels.

Ifthe parking brake switchis pulld up to the apply position and vehicle speed is within the high speed dynamic range, the E module will apply braking force t the ear wheel at aslower rate until full braking load  reached o the switch relsedhe ate iich bakig foapplie corolle be odule which o o cuent dy the actuator and positional information from the actuator hall sensor and compares this to information held within its configuration software.

The EPB module willinitiate the release from park function and automaticall release the parking brake if the gearselector s moved from P (park).

Before carring out any work on the parking brake system, use Jaguar approved daostic equipment to perform the seice routine t lesealtesion.The rutine cbe found ithe vice citi area, nderthe seup and ciuration menu. After any work has been caried out on the parking brake, the system will require resetting.

CAUTION: Do not use the emergency release tool to allow work to be caried out on the parking brake. Work can only be carried out on the parking brake systm after the service routine to release cable tension has been run.

The EP module will only perate the actator if the power supply rom the battey is between  and 6 At ny oltae within this range, the actuator is able to full tighten and release the brake cables. f the power supply falls outide of the range, a fault ode is stored in the EPB module and can be retrieved using Jaguar approved diagnostic equipment.

![](images/_MISSING_b6d98a0efa47df664aa7447023c699d51de07a204ee4e023afed7212c1efd926.jpg)

The parking brake switch is mounted in the floor console, rearward of the rotary gear selector. The switch has three states:

Apply: When the switch is pulled up to apply the parking brake.   
Release: When the switch is pushed down to release the parking brake.   
Neutral: The central default position. The switch returns to this position regardless of parking brake status.

he parking brake switch contains a pair of micro-switches for both the apply and release actions. The EPB module provides an ividul ardwirelectical eedt eachof theour miroihes plus inge goundcoeinllwingo costan nonitor switch status.

![](images/_MISSING_827c5a86405de569f278541d74c744925a862c1ac2160e6f44f475bdab21a0dc.jpg)

he parking brake actuator is mounted on the back of the rear subframe. Operation of the actuator i controlled by the EPB nodule in response to parking brake switch requests from the driver.

A Hallsensor is located within the actuator and provides positional information back to the EPB module. The principle functior of the Hl sensor is to ensurethe actator full rleases the parking brakewhen astati releaseequest is made.The sial provided by the Hallsensor is compared to configuration information contained within the EP module software to determine when a fuli release has been carried out.

The stoplamp witch is mounted on the brake pedal mounting bracket. One of the prerequisites for relasing the parking brake isthat the foot brake is applied.The E module is able to deterie the position of the foot brake by miting the status of the stoplamp switch vià a hardwired electrical connection.

The stoplamp switch also supplies status signals to the CIB and the ECM.

### Hydraulic Brake Actuation -


The instrument cluster contains a red waming indicator for the EP.The waming indicator is permanently illminated while th ≡PB is applied. If the warning indicator flashs, the EPB has an electrical fault.

Ifthere i anEP fault the message Cannot Apply Park Brake or Park Brake Fault pears in the istrument custermessae center. If the vehiceis moving with the parking brake applied, the message Caution Park Brake Applied appears in the message center accompanied by a chime from the instrument cluster. Refer to: Information and Message Center (413-08 Information and Message Center, Description and Operation).

For a detailed description of the Parking Brake operation, refer to the relevant Description and Operation section of the workshop manual. REFER to: Parking Brake (206-05 Parking Brake and Actuation, Description and Operation).

The parking brke system must be calibrated whenever the battery has been disconnected or has been in a state of discharge, or repairs have been carried out to the rear service or parking brake system.

NOTE: If new rear brake pads have been installed, pressure must be applied to the brake pedal a minimum of five times prior to calibration of the parking brake system.

To calibrate the parking brake system:

Place gear selector lever in 'P' Park position.   
Release parking brake cable tension to service position.   
Set the ignition status to 'ON'.   
Apply and hold the footbrake then pull up the parking brake switch.   
To release the parking brake, apply and hold the footbrake then release and press down the parking brake switch.

For a list of Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) that could be logged on this vehicle, please refer to Section 100-00. REFER t DiostiTroubleode() Inde-ElecriParking Brake(P) (100-00 Generaomatin Descriptin and Operation).

The ABs provides the following brake functions that are designed to assist the vehicle or aid the driver:

ABS. DSC, including Trac DSC. CBC (corner brake control). EBD (electronic brake force distribution). ETC (electronic traction control). EBA (emergency brake assist). EDC (engine drag-torque control). EUC (enhanced ündersteer control). Electronic brake prefill (vehicles with ACC only).

Al the brake functions listed are automatial active when the ignition i i power mode and theengine is running.The DS system can be selected to off using the DSC switch.

ABS controls the speed of allroad wheels to ensure optimum whee slip when braking at the adhesion limit. The wheels are orevented from locking to retain effective steering control of the vehicle.

SC(dynamic stability control) uses brakes and powertrain torque control to assist in maintaining the yaw stability of the ehice. While the ignition is nergized the DSC function is permanently enabled, unless selected off using the DS switch.

DSC enhances driving safety in abrupt maneuvers and in under-steer orover-steer sitations that may occur in a bend. nan over-steer situation initially powertrain torque i cotrolled then the outer front wheelis braked to counteract the yaw movement of the rear axle towards the outer edge of the bend.

The steering angle sensor measures the steering wheel angle and the rate of change of the steering wheel angle. These measurements are received by the ABS module and broadcast on the high speed CN bus for use by other systems.

The steering angle sensor is mounted on the steering column upper shroud mounting bracket, immediately behind the multifunction switches, and is secured by 2 screws.  fly lead connects the sensor to the passenger compartment wiring harness via a 4 pin multiplug.

he sensor is housed in a 'U' shaped plastic casing and contains two offset LEDs (light emittig diodes) facing two detectors.

An encoder ring is mounted on the iner steering column shaft and intersects the LEDs and detectors. The encoder ring contains 60 slots which break and restore the light beams between the LEDs and the detectors as the steering wheel is rotated. The ABS module is able to determine the direction of rotation of the steering wheel by moitoring when the light beams change state.The LEDs and detectors are mounted in such a way that only one beam willchange state, eitherto broken or restored, at any one time.

The center (straight ahead) position of the steering wheel has to be leamed by the ABS module every time the ignition is switched ON. The steering angle sensor is unable to determine the center position so inputs from the yaw rate and laterl acceleration sensor and wheel speed signals are also used by the AS module to help it perform this process. If extreme weather conditions are present, forexample ice causing extreme wheel spin or understerrster the As module may o eable t deteie the cnter piti of the steig whee.  thi itatin, STILTY ONTROL NOT LEDRE WITH CARE will be displayed in the instrument cluster message center and the amber waming indicator willuminate.

The message STABILITY CONTROL NOT AVAILABLE DRIVE WITH CARE willalso be displayed if the ABS module detects a steering angle sensor fault. The amber warning indicator willilluminate until the fault is rectified.

The stoplamp switch is mounted on the brake pedal box and is connected to the vehicle hamess via a four pin multiplug.

When the brake pedal is pressed, the switch contacts close.This allows a hard wired signal feed to be sent to the ECM. A stoplamp switch status messae is then sent from the EM to the ABS module on the high speed CAN bus. The ABS module is then able to control braking force accordingly in conjunction with the HCu.

The HCU is a four channel unit, secured to a mounting bracket located in the passenger side, rear engine bay. The HCU modulates the supply of hydraulic pressure to the brakes under the control of the ABS module.

To accomplish the transfer of heat, refrigerant is circulated around a sealed system, where it passes through two pressure/temperature regimes. In each of the regimes the refrigerant changes state, during which process maximum heat absorption or dissipation occurs.

The low pressure/temperature regime is from the therostatic expansion valve, through the evaporator to the compressor. Th refrigerant decreases in pressure and temperature at the thermostatic expansion valve, then changes state from a liquid to a vapor in the evaporator to absorb heat.

The high pressure/temperature regime is from the compressor, through the condenser and receiver drier assembly to the thermostatic expansion valve.The refrigerant increasesin pressure and temperature as it passes through the compresso, then releases heat and changes state from a vapor to a liquid in the condenser.

The front suspension is a full independent design assembled on a non-isolated subframe. Each front wheel knuckle attaches to unequal length wishbone-type upper and lower control arms, which minimize track and camber changes during articulation. A stilier arattached to the front of the sframe and coeted t each arlwercontro a with a link assmbly.A spring and damper assembly i installed between each rear lower control arm and the related front suspension housing.

Description and Operation

System Operation Component Description

![](images/_MISSING_33041e3ea2c5a7037cad4fc38acd524b25e332f89598ee896b34da2b7fb4eafa.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_0448195ca7c2af22dc99f2d165c5cb9eca5c8890d3521e75736881580f557139.jpg)

The forged-aluminum upper control arm is a wishbone design and connects to the vehicle body through two plain bushes, and links to the swan neck wheel knuckle by an ntegral balljoint.The upper control arm i inclined to provide anti-dive characteristics under heavy braking, while also controlling geometry for vehicle straight-line stability.

he forged aluminum lower control arms are of the wishbone design; the arms separate to allow for optimum bush tuning:

The rear lateral control arm is fitted with a bush at its iner end which locates between brackets on the subframe. The arm is secured with an eccentric bolt which provides the adjustment of the suspension camber geometry. The outer end of the control arm has a tapered hole which locates on a baljoint fited to the wheel knuckle. An integral clevis bracket on the forward face of the lateral control arm allows for the attachment of the forward control arm. A bush is fitted below the clevis bracket to provide for the attachment of the stabilizer bar link. A cross-axis joint is fited to a cross-hole in the control arm to provide the location for the clevis attachment of the spring and damper assembly. The forward control arm is fitted with a fluid-block rubber bush at its inner end which locates between brackets on the subframe. The arm i secured with an eccentric bolt which provides adjustment of the castor and camber geometry. The outer end of the control arm is fitted with a cross-axis joint and locates in the integral clevis bracket on the laterl control arm.

### Front Suspension - Front Shock Absorber Removal and Installation


The cast aluminum wheel knuckle is a swan neck design and attachesto the upper control arm and lower lateral control arm The lower lateral control arm locates on a non serviceble balljoint integral with the whee knuckle. The lower boss on the ear of the knuckle provides for the attachment of the steering gear tie-rod ball joint.

The wheel knuckle also provides the mounting locations for the:

•Wheel hub and bearing assembly.   
The wheel speed sensor (integral to the wheel hub and bearing assembly).   
Brake caliper and disc shield.

he spring and damper assemblies are located between the lower lateral arm and the front suspension housing. Each spring ind damper assembly incorporates:

An adaptive dynamics damper, which enables the damping characteristics of the suspension to be adjusted. Refer to: Vehicle Dynamic Suspension (204-05 Vehicle Dynamic Suspension, Description and Operation).   
conventional coil spring individually tuned to provide the required characteristics for the iffrent engine variants.

The spring rate of the coil spring differs between models and is color coded for identification.

The air suspension system provides a fuly automatic selfleveling function that ensures the vehicle maintains a constant attitude, irespective of load, by adjusting the rear ride height to match the front ride height.

The air suspension system comprises of:

An air spring in the spring and damper assembly of each rear wheel.   
An air compressor assembly.   
A valve block.   
•A reservoir.   
A silencer.   
A network of pipes to connect the individual components.   
Four suspension height sensors (one for each corner of the vehicle).   
An air suspension module.

Calibration or height seting is the process of adjusting the values stored in the air suspension module for the suspension height sensor offsets for each of the four comers. Each of the suspension height sensors measures the position of the associted wheel with respect to the vehice chassis and generates a coresponding voltae signal Each of these voltae sigals i read by the module and converted to a height lue in milimeters. Ideal this height vale would exactly match the actual value for ach wheel, however due to build and component tolerances there can be an offset between these two sets of values.

he caliration process sets the necessary value for this offset for each suspension height sensor so that the actual and calculated values are equal. System calibration is required in the following cases:

A suspension height sensor is removed or replaced.   
A replacement air suspension module is fitted.   
If the suspension on any comer is dismantled and rebuilt.

he calibration procedure is carred out using Jaguar approved diagnostic equipment and a suspension height measurement :00l.

The air suspension module contains a selftest function, that can be activated by Jaguar approved diagnostic equipment. The :est is primarily an electrical test. Checks for stuck valves or leaking valves etc. are not included.

The test routine activates each output (valves and compressor) in tum, and monitors electrical connections. The routine takes approximately 30 seconds to complete, but may be terminated immediately by switching the ignition off Operation of the valves during this test may causemal qantities of ir flw into or out of the irsprings. As result the veicle may make small changs in height.

The self test operates in the following sequence:

•Opens exhaust valve 100%, then closes valve.   
Turns compressor on and off.   
Opens rear left air spring valve 100%, then closes valve.   
Opens rear right air spring valve 100%, then closes valve.   
•Opens the reservoir valve 100% for 2 seconds, then closes valve.

To de-pressurize the system air is vented through the valve block, the air compressor assembly which regenerates the air drier), the filter and the silencer to atmosphere. The system is pressurized using the air compressor assembly. The de-pressurization and pressurization of the air suspension system is initiated using Jaguar approved diagnostic equipment

Brake disc shield.

ach spring and damper assembly i attached to a cast bracket on the lower control arm and to the vehicle body by four studs secured by torque retaining nuts.

Each spring and damper assembly incorporates:

An adaptive dynamics damper, which enables the damping characteristics of the suspension to be adjusted. Refer to: Vehicle Dynamic Suspension (204-05 Vehicle Dynamic Suspension, Description and Operation).   
An air spring, controlled by the air suspension system.

The air springs take the place of conventional coil spring on the rear suspension. n the air spring, a piston compresses the air as the supension moves into bump/jounce, which cushions the movement. A rubber roling sleeve is guided by an outer metal support sleeve and assembled around the damper. The metal suppor sleeve is decoupled from the top mount assembly, which allows greater damper articulation without trapping the air sleeve. This design delivers improved ride characteristics compared to a non-guided air spring, and reduces high frequency generated inputs such as those produced by a coarse road surfáce, for example.

The key sealing points for the air spring are between the:

Piston and damper body.   
Spring unit and 'top moúnt.

The method of achieving a pressure-tight seal between the air spring and the damper means that spring and damper assemblies must be replaced as a complete unit.

The air-tight top mount assembly isolates the damper from the body structure while maintaining pressure within the spring.A pressure retaining valve in the top mount ensures that air cannot be exhausted from the air spring when the pressure is less than 3.0 bar (43.5 fn² This ensures that the roling sleeve does not crease and become damagedThe maximum pressure in the full-bump condition at GVw (gross vehicle weight) is approximately 20 bar (290 Ibf/in²).

The valve block is used by the air suspension module to control the flow of air between the air compressor assembly, the reservoir and the two air springs. The'valve block is installed in the luggage compartment spare wheel well on the ame bracket as the air compressor assembly. Three isolator grommets locate the valve block mounting plate on the bracket.

The valve block incorporates:

Three normally closed solenoid valves, one for each of the rear air springs and one for the reservoir. A pressure sensor to monitor the pressure in the line between the air compressor assembly and the three solenoid valves. The solenoid valvescontrol the ir flow into and out ofthe airsprings and the reseor and are perated by WM signals from :he air suspension module. The air suspension module uses the pressure sensor signal to decide when to pressurize the air springs directly from the air compressor assembly, or from the pressurized air stored in the reservoir.

A series of pipes cary pressurized air betweenthe system components. The irspring pipes are integrated into the electrical haessesheicompressoasseml  ale blck pipe searate from the therpipes hileheale blok t rse pipe is clipped together with the itake/exhaust pipe.A filter, attached to the nderside of the ir compressor assembly, s installed in the intake/exhaust pipe.

### Rear Suspension - Rear Suspension Diagnosis and Testing


The air suspension module uses a combination of infomation from other system modules and data from the suspension height sensors to measure the vehicle and suspension states. Using this ifomation, the irsuspension module applies alorithmt control the rear suspension height required for the current driving conditions.

The air suspension module is installed on the RH side of the luggage compartment, together with the adaptive damping

module, on a bracket attached to the rear quarter panel.

The air suspension module receives the following signals on the high speed CAN bus:

•Vehicle speed - ABS module.   
•Wheel speed sensors - ABSmodule.   
Lateral acceleration - ABS module.   
Steering wheel angle - ABS module.   
Steering wheel anle status - ABS module.   
Engine speed - ECM.   
Gear position target - TCM.   
Vehicle information parameters - CJB.   
CCF (car configuration files) - CJB.   
Power mode (ignition signal) - CJB.

The air suspension module outputs information on the high speed CAN bus for use by other systems as follows:

Fault message - instrument cluster Individual suspension heights - other systems as required.

![](images/_MISSING_8fd81de632e9747e013432d8cf96798c00789c1224ce50c0c0e6a002d9b0814a.jpg)

Four suspension height sensors are used in the air suspension system, two for the front suspension and two for the rear suspension. A front uspension height sensor is attached to each side of the front subframe and connected by a sensor arm and sensor link to the related lower lateral am of the front suspension. A rear suspension height sensor is attached to each side of the rear subframe and connected by a sensor arm and sensor link to the related upper control arm of the rear suspension. On each suspension height sensor,the sensor arm and sensor link convert inear movement of the suspension into rotary movement of the sensor shaft.

ach suspension height sensor contains two independent sensors:

Sensor 1 is used by the air suspension system.   
Sensor 2 is used by the adaptive dynamics system. Refer to: Vehicle Dynamic Suspension (204-05 Vehicle Dynamic Suspension, Description and Operation).

The suspension height sensors measure suspension displacement at each comer of the vehicle and output a coresponding analogue signal to the air suspension module.The data from the sensors is fitered and processed by the air suspension module an used to ensurethat the vehicle remains level and at the corct height at al times by rgulating the supply ofir to each rear air spring unit.

Each suspension height sensor is connected to the air suspension module via three wires, which supply ground, 5 V supply anc signal return.

Each sensing element consists of an array of Halleffect devices araged to measure the direction of the magnetic field of a small magnet attached to the end of the sensor shaft As the sensorhaft rotates, so do the lines of maetic flu from the attached magnet. The signals from each of the Hleffect elements are processed by means of a dedicated integrated ciruit, to generate n output voltage that varies as the sensor shaft is rotated. The sensor has a measurement range of ± 40 round its nominal position and the nominal sensitivity is 57 mv/° of shaft rotation.

For additional information.

The adaptive dynamics system is an electronically controlled suspension system, which continuously adjusts the damping characteristics of the suspension dampers in reaction to the current driving conditions.

The system is controlled by theADM. The ADM receivessignals from three body vertical accelerometers, four suspension height sensors and from other vehicle systems to determine vehicle state, body and wheel motions, and driver inputs. These signals are used by the ADM to continously control the damping characteristics of each damper to the appropriate level, to give the optimum body control and vehicle ride.

The ADM also contains the controller for the electronic differential, where fitted.

The ADM uses a combination of information from other system modules and data from the body vertical accelerometers and suspension height sensors to measure the vehicle and suspension states and driver inputs. Using this information, the AD applies algorithms to control the dampers for the current driving conditions.

The ADM receives the following signals on the high speed CAN bus from the stated system components:

Brake pressure - ABSmodule.   
Brake pressure quality factor - ABS module.   
Car configuration parámeters - CJB. Engine speed - ECM. Enine speed quality factor - ECM. Enine torque flywheel actual - ECM. Enine torque flywheel actual quality factor - ECM. Gear position target - TCM. Lateral acceleration - ABS module. Power mode (ignition signal) - CJB. Power mode quality factor -'CJB. Roll stability control mode - ABS module. Steering wheel angle - ABS module.   
Steering wheel angle speed - ABSmodule.   
Steerin wheel anle status - ABS module.   
Terrain mode requsted - JaguarDrive selector. Torque converter slip - TCM.   
Vehicle information parameters HS - CJB. Vehicle speed - ABS module. Vehicle speed quality factor - ABS module. Front left wheel speed - ABS module. Front left wheel speed quality factor - ABS module. Front right wheel speed'- AB module. Front right wheel speed quality factor - ABS module.   
Rear left wheel speed - ABS module. Rear left wheel speed quality factor - ABS module.   
Rear right wheel speed' - ABmodule.   
Rear riht wheel speed quality factor - ABS module.

he ADM also outputs information on the high speed CAN bus for use by other systems as follows:

Fault message - Instrument cluster.   
Terrain mode change status - JaguarDrive selector.   
Terrain mode - JaguarDrive selector.   
Front left suspension height - other systems as required.   
Front right suspension height - other systems as required.   
Rear left suspension height - other systems as required.   
Rear right suspension height - other systems as required.

The ADM monitors the input signals and operates the damper solenoids. The input signals are used in control functions and a force required for each damper for each function, is calculated. An arbitrator monitors the force requirements from each function' and apportions a force to a damper The force is converted to the appropriate curent and sent to the damper.

The control functions are as follows:

Body Control - Uses body vertical acclerometer and CAN inputs. Calculates road induced body motions 100 times a second and sets each damper to the appropriate level to maintain a flat and level body atitude.Provides improved body control without loss of ride quality.

Roll Rate Control - Uses CAN inputs. Predicts vehicle roll rate due to driver steering inputs 100 times a second and increases damping to reduce roll rate. Provides improved control and driver confidence.   
Pich Rate ControUses  inputs.Predict vehice pith ate due t driverrotteand braking input 00 timesa second and increases damping to reduce pitch rate. Provides improved control and driver confidence.   
Bump Rebound Control - Uses suspension height sensor and CAN inputs. Monitors the position of the wheel 50 times a second and increases the damping rate as the damper approaches'the end of its travel. Provides improved ride quality.   
Wheel Hop Control - Uses suspension height sensor and CAN inputs. Monitors the position of the wheel 500 times a second and detects when the wheel is at its natural frequency and increases the damping. Provides improved ride quality.

Jnder normal rad conditions when the vehicle isstationary with the engine running, the dampers are set to the firm conditior o reduce power consumption.

The adaptive dynamics dampers are monotube, nitrogen gas and oil filld units, which are integrated with a conventional coil spring (front suspension) or an air spring (rear suspension) to form the spring and damper assemblies.The dampers are contiuously variable, which allows the damping force to beelectricl adjusted when the vehicle is being driven.The dampers provide the'optimum'compromise between vehile control and ride comfort.

The dampers have an electrical connector on the end of the piston rod, in the center of the top mount.

In each damper, the damping adjustment i achieved by a solenoid operated variable orifice, which opens up an altemative path for oil w witithe amper When de-eergied the bypass is closedandallthe oil flows throughthe main(frmalve. When energized the solenoid moves an amature and control blade, which work against a spring. The control blade icoporates a orifice which slidesisie  itered housing t open up the ypass asreuired.  compressionoil flws from the lowerportio of the dampertrough hollw pistono asearate soft omfortale theliderhousing and fnd te ppe ti ohe amer her asg themaiiale edtheil tepoie direction.

In the fim setting oil flows through the main (fim) valve only, but when the bypassis opened by any amount the oil flows through both valves in apressure balance. Whenfull eergized the solenoid moves the amature and therefore the sliderto the maximum extension and opens the orifice completely. The damper operates continuously between these two boundary conditions.

The solenoid in each damper is operated by a separate 526 Hz PW (pulse with modulation) signal from the ADM. TheADM continuously varies the current of the PWM signals between a minimum of  A and a maximum of 1. A ie. between the maximum fim setting when de-energized and the maximum soft setting when full energized) to independently increase and decrease the damping of each damper as required.

Four suspension height sensors are used in the adaptive dynamics system, two for the front suspension and two for the rear suspension. A front uspension height sensor is attached to each side of the front subframe and connected by a sensor arm and sensor link to the related lower lateral am of the front suspension. A rear suspension height sensor is attached to each side of the rear subframe and connected by a sensor am and sensor link to the related upper control arm of the rear suspension. On each suspension height sensor, the sensor arm and sensorlink convert linear movement of the suspension intc rotary movement of the sensor shaft.

Each suspension height sensor contains two independent sensors:

Sensor 1 is used by the air suspension system. Refer to: Rear Suspension (204-02 Rear Suspension, Description and Operation).

Sensor 2 is used by the adaptive dynamics system.

The suspension height sensors measure suspension displacement at each comer of the vehicle and output a coresponding analogue signal to the ADM. The alorithms in the ADM calculate the position, velocity and frequency content of the signals and use the results for individual wheel control.

ach suspension height sensor is connected to the ADM via three wires, which supply ground, 5 V supply and signal retum.

Each sensing element consists of an array of Halleffect devices aranged to measure the direction of the magnetic field of small magnet attached to the end of the sensor shaft As the sensorshaft rotates,so do the lines of maetic flu from the attached magnet. The signals from each of the Hleffet elements are processed by means of a dedicatd integrated circuit, to generate an output voltae that varies a the sensor shaft s rotated.The sensor has a measurement range of 40 round its nominal position and the nominal sensitivity is  mv/ of shat rotation.

There is one damper lcated i the alve housing.The damper is used to regulate and dampen the reulated pressure supplied via EPRS. The damper is load dependent through modulation of the damper against retum spring pressure.

The damper comprises a piston, a housing bore and aspring. The piston is subject to the pressure applied by the spring.The bore has a conecting port to the function to which it applies.Fluid pressure applied to the applicable componenti utchao bjcedt the fullarea of the istonwhich moves aginst the ppoig force applied y thesring.he movement of the piston creates an action similar to a shock absorber, momentariy delaying the build up of pressure in the circuit. This results in a more gradual application of clutches improving shift quality.

The valve block spool valves control various functions of the transmission.The spool valves are of conventional design and are operated by fluid pressure.

Each spool valve is locatedit spool bore and held in a default (unpressurized position by a spring.The spool bore hasa number of ports which allow fluid to flow to other valves and clutches to enable transmission operation. Each spool hasa piston which is waisted to allow fluid to be diverted into the applicable ports when the valve is operated.

When fluid pressure moves a spool, one or more ports in the spool bore are covered or uncovered. Fluid is prevented from flowing or i allowed to flow around the applicable waisted area of the spool and into another ncovered port. The fluid is either passed through galleries to actuate another spool, operate a clutch or is returned to the fluid pan.

### Right Hand (RH) steering wheel mounted switch assembly


A LIN (local interconnect network) bus connection from the cockspring to the instrument cluster receives signals from the RH (right-hand) steering mounted switch assembly.

The switch assembly contains a control module. The module outputs a reference voltage to the joy pad in the RH steering wheel switch assembly. The switches in the switch assembly are connected through several resistors in series to a ground point. The control module monitors the resistance in the switch circuit to determine the selected switch function.

When a switch is operated (switch contact momentarily closed), the control module senses the change in resistance and determines the requested function by the measured reistance value. The control module converts this information into aL bus message which passed via the clockspring to the instrument cluster in the LIN bus.

NOTE: The control module in the RH steering wheel switch assembly also passes information from the speed control switches to the speed control module in the same way, but these are not related to instrument cluster operation and control.
