Use extreme care and observe all safety precautions related to the use of refrigerants. Due to refrigerant hazards, always wear safety goggles and non-penetrable gloves when working on or flushing air conditioning (A/C) systems. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury.

When flushing the A/C system, refer to the manufacturers equipment instructions for additional information. Failure to do so may result in system damage or personal injury.

The A/C refrigerant analyzer must be used before the recovery of any vehicle's A/C refrigerant. Failure to do so puts shop bulk refrigérant at 'risk of contamination. If the vehicle A/C refrigerant is contaminated, refer the customer to return to the repair facilitý that performed the last A/C repair. If the customer wishes to pay the additionàl cost, use the A/C recovery equipment that is designated for recovering contaminated A/C refrigeránt. Ail contaminated A/ refrigerant must be disposed of as hazardous waste. For additional information, refer to the manufacturers equipment instructions. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury.

Prior to using the A/C flushing equipment for the first time, follow the operating instructions. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury.

CAUTION: Prior to flushing, remove and discard the desiccant sack. Depending on the equipment used, other A/C components may have to be removed prior to flushing. For additional information, refer to the manufacturers equipment iñstructions before flushing the A/C system.

The heating and ventilation system controls the temperature and flow of air supplied to the passenger compartment. The system is ither a dual zone ór four zone system, depending on vehicle specification.

Operation of the heating and ventilation system is controlled by the ATC module.   
Refer to: Control Components (412-01 Climate Control, Description and Operation).

The system can be operated in automatic or manual mode, with temperature settings selected using the switches on the integrated control panel and, on four zone systems, the rear climate'control panel.

When the engine is running, coolant is constantly circulated through the heater core by the engine coolant pump.

The blower i supplied with power from the blower relay on the R and connected to ground via the blower control module. The blower cotro module reulates the voltae across the blower motorto cotrol blower speed. The voltae set by the blower control module is controlled by a PWM (pulse width modulation) signal from the ATC module. The AT module uses a feedback signal from the blower control module to monitor blower speed.

### Climate Control - Control Components - Component Location Description and Operat


he thermostaticexpansion valve meters the flow of refrigerant into the evaporator, to match the refrigerant flw with the ieat load of the air passing through the evaporator.

The thermostatic expansion valve is a block type valve located behind the heater assembly, and attached to the inlet and outlet ports of the evaporator. The thermostatic expansion valve consists of an aluminum housing containing inet and outlet pasages ball andspring meteing ve stalled nthe inet pasaeand atemperatre sensos instlledn the outet passaeThe temperature sensor consist otemperature sensitive tube cnnected to a diaphram.The bottom end of the temperature sensitive tube acts on the balof the metering valve. Pressure on top of the diaphragm is controlled by the evaporator outlet temperature conducted through the temperature sensitive tube. The bottom of the diaphragm senses evaporator outlet pressure.

![](images/_MISSING_b0603d81be295252a9415b4fe38f34bc8b48a35ac001d58fc39a10040cea9e3d.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_2db7ef8d3956c21cac3e4ad3bc5ad916b56ebb0a4150a50a310e7eef88f17f14.jpg)

Liquid refrigerant flows through the metering valve into the evaporator. The restriction acrossthe metering valve reducesthe pressure and temperature ofthe frigerantThe restriction als changes the liquid stram of refrigerant int a fine spray, to improve the aratio process.Astheefrigerant passes trough the eaporator it absors heat from the airflwing troug the evaporator. The increase in temperature causes the refrigerant to vaporize and increase in pressure.

The temperature and pressure of the refrigerant leaving the aporator act on the daphram and temperature sesitive tube, which regulate the mteing valve penin and so control the vlume of refrigerant flowing trough the orator.The warmer the ir flowing through the evaporator, the more heat avilable to evaporate refrigerant and thus the greater volume of refrigerant allowed through the metering valve.

The heaterelements ony operate when the engine is running. Power for the heaterlements is supplied to the seat heater modules from the heated seat relay in the  which is controlled by a hardwired ignition signal from the .

Seat heating selections made on the TSD and the rear climate control panel are transmitted to the ATC module.   
Refer to: Heating and Ventilation (412-01 Climate Control, Description and Operation).

When the ATC module receives a seat heating request, it sends a LIN bus message to the appropriate seat heater module to energize the heaterelements in the cushion and the squab. The seat heater module relays the temperature signal rom the thermal sensor in the cushion heater element, back to the ATC module. The ATC module uses the temperature signal to regulate the heater elements at the selected heat setting.

Three body vertical accelerometers are used in the adaptive dynamics system:

A front body vertical accelerometer is attached to the body behind the right front whee, on the front sidemember to dash gusset.   
Arear body vertical acclerometer is installed on each side of the luggage compartment, attached to the related rear quarter panel.

he body vertical acclerometers measure acceleration in the vertical plane and output a coresponding analoguesignal to th DM.The alorithms in the ADM calculate the heave, pitch and rol motions of the vehile, which are used by the cotroller t :ontrol road induced body motion.

ach body vertical accelerometer is connected to the ADM via three wires, which supply ground, 5 V supply and signal retum.

The sensing element comprises aingle parall plate capacitor, one plate of which moves relative to the ther dependant on the force acceleration) applied.This causes the capacitance to change as a function of applied acceleration.This capacitance isompared with a fixed reference capacitor in a bridge ciruit and the signal i processed by means of a dedicated integrated iruit erate aoutut oltaetat aries asfucti oappeacclerationheesorututsigal oto approximately 1 ± 0.05 v/g.

The electronic throttle actuator is located on the side of the throttle intake manifold.

The electronic throttle actuator controls the volume of air llwed into the inlet manifolds by means of a DC motor which controls a fla in the body of the throttle. The actuator is contolled by the ECM which operates the actator i response t driver iputs from the AP sensor and other engine related sensors to provide the correct air flow to the intake manifolds.

This procedure is required if: A new ACC radar and, or ACC module are installed. The ACC radar needed to be removed or is misaligned in its position due to another repair operation.

8.

From the diagnostic tool menu, select: Service Alignment Mode. The follow indicator will now be flashing, this indiates that the vehicle is in "service alignment" and now requires driving. The vehicle speed must be above 30 mph (48 kph). Choose a road with plenty of stationary objects, like street lights, road signs, or bariers. Use an inside or óutside lane. Following vehiles too closely will obscure the stationary targets from the radar, a time gap of 2 seconds is recommended.

A straight road will produce a quicker and better result, although the process will stili operate on a curved road. The time that the ACC module takes to align will vary, depending on the route, speed, number of targets, and individuàl module. When the flashing follow indicator light extinguishes, the ACC system is now functional, and a required vehicle speed can now be set by the driver and the ACC system will operate as normal.

### Parking Aid Sensors


The temperature blend doors adjust the proportion of coo ai from the evaporator that passes through the heater core to produce the required output air temperature.

The temperature blend doors for each zone are operated independently to enable individual temperature settings for the different zones. The temperature blend doors are operated by stepper motors, which are controlled by the ATC module usin LIN (local interconnect network) bus messages.

The ATC module calculates the temperature blend stepper motor positions required to achieve the selected temperature and compares it aginst the curent position. If there is any diffrence, the AT module signals the stepper motors to adopt the new position.

Air temperature is controlled automaticall unless maximum heating (H) or maximum cooling (LO) is selected. When maximu heating or cooling is selected, a 'omfort' algorithm in the ATC module adopts an appropriate strategy forair distrbution, blower speed, and air source.

Temperature control in one zone can be compromised by another zone being set to a high level of heating or cooling. True maximum heatig o coing (diplayedasH or L onthe can only e selected for the river's zone. I o s selected for the river's zone, the temperature for the other zone(s is utomaticall set to match the driver's zone.

airconditioningseletedoffin theutomatic mode no coolingof theinlet i wiltake placeThe miimum output air temperature from the system wil be ambient air temperature plus any heat pick up in the air inlet path.

Ifthe Sync climate button on the D is pressed, the ATC module synchronizes the temperature of the other zone(s) with the driver's zone.

Air distribution doors drect the airto the individual vents and registers in the passenger compartment.The doos are operated by stepper motors, which are controlled by the ATC module using LIN bus messages.

When the A/C system is in automatic mode, the ATC module automatically controls air distribution into the passenger compartment in line with its 'comfort' algrithm.Automatic control ioveridden iany of the buttons on the D, or switches on the P or rear climate control panel, are selected. Air distriution remains as selected until one of the AUTO switches is pressed or a different manual selection is made.

Eliminating blind spots is a major element in vehice body design, but because of the structural requirements of B,  and D pillars, blind spots cannot be entirely eliminated.Statistics show that some accidents are directly atributable to drivers moving across ito the path overtaking veiceshat have ot bee seein covential mirs.New miror dsishae improved the situation, however the introduction of a radar-based blind spot monitoring system helps to further reduce the risk.

The blind spot monitoring system comprises:

•LH (left-hand) Blind spot monitoring sensor RH (right-hand) Blind spot monitoring sensor •LH (left-hand) door mirror   
RH (right-hand) door mirror

The system uses two radar modules operating at a frequency of 24 GHz and each combining the radar and electronic module in asingle unit.The modules are located beind the rearumper surface, symmetrically one n each side of the car behind the rear wheels. They areside acing and nlined reawards at an angleof  degrees, which i dictated by theshape at the rear of the vehicle. Each module is calirated to detect a vehice in the drivers blind spot Once a valid target is detected the module illuminates an amber wainglert icon' LE (light emitting diodein the relevant exterior door mior f there i fault r blockaewith the lind spot mitring system an amber waming iicator dot LE light emitingdiode i displayed in the exterior mirr and the message blind spot monitoring not avilable' or 'blind spot sensor blocked' is displayed in the instrument cluster message center.

When the system initiates, it performs a selfcheck, during which the waming icons in the mirors iluminate alteately fora short period of time. Each module does a left/right determination check when the igition is switched on. Each miror has a diferent circuit cofiguration so that the moduls can determine which miror they are connected to f a module detects the wrong mirror it will go into a fault condition.

The blind spot monitoring modules receive vehicle speed on the medium speed CAN (controller area network) and are inactive until the vehicle reaches 16kph (10mph).

Each Blind Spot Monitor module emits a radarfield greater than the blind spot area. The actual blind spot are i calibrated into the module during its manufacture.

CAutioN: The blind spot monitoring system is designed as a driver aid not a safety device. The driver should always exercise due care and attention whilst driving.

Operation of the lamps is performed using overload proof Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistors (MOSFETs). The MoSs ca detect overload ad interuption with the lamps swiched o and short circuit to positive with the lamps switched off.

The MOSFETs are protected against short circuits, removing the requirement for the lamps circuits to be protected by fuses. The s reond to heat erated bincrased curnt fow caused by short circuit.Nomal tis would causethe fus to blow.The oFE react to the heat inrase and cut the supply to theffted circuit. Once the fault has been rectiied or the MOSFET has cooled, the MOSFET will automatically reset and operate the circuit normally.

Ifan overload occurs, the current flow is dependant on the temperature of the related MosFET and can be up to 20 times the rated current of the lamp. The MOSFET heats up and deactiates the load applied to the circuit. When the MOSFET cools the circuit is once again reactivated. This thermal cycling occurs continuously in the event of an overload occuring.

A number of lamps are controlled by relays and these circuits are protected by conventional fuses.

Interior lighting i provided to enable the safe entry and departure from the vehice for the driver and passegers i low ambient light conditions, without any manual switching of the lights.

—NOTE: The term interior lamps also includes the door mirror approach lamps.

The interior lamps are controlled by the  (central junction box) and have 2 modes of operation: manual and automatic. The front interior amps in the front overead console are operated using the JaguarSense'system. The system uses capacitive proximity sensor techology for the switch operation which iintegrl with the veread console. The rearveread console interior lamps have conventional switches.

The interior lighting has 2 modes of operation; automatic and manual.

In automati mode, the courtesy amp functionality is controlled by the  and reacts to the vehicle being locked or unlocke and opening the vehicle doors.

n the manual mode the interior lamps can be switched on and off with the JaguarSense system and will not iluminate automatically when the vehicle is unlocked or a door is opened.

The driver's and passenger door approach lamps are controlled by the driver's door module and the passenger door module respectively and 'operate with the automatic mode.

The interior ilumination also includes'ambience'lighting. When the side or headlamps are switched on, phosphor blue LED (ight emitting diode'siluminate the instrument panel center switch surround, the JaguarDrive rtay control and also illuminate the door handles and door pockets. On high specification vehicles the instrument panel air vents are also iieo'achohentanddc proiteiigmitehee the vehicle.

The CJB receives the following inputs which affect the operation of the interior lamps:

Ignition status   
•Door latch switches   
Luggage compartment lid latch switch   
Glovebox lamp switch   
Unlock signal   
Front roof console interior lamp - 'JaguarSense'   
Front roof console map reading lamps - 'JaguarSense' Rear roof console map reading lamps   
Delayed power off relay   
Vanity mirror lamp switches   
Side and headlamp status (ambience lighting only).

The interior lamps fade on when any door is opened and fade off slowly after 20 seconds after the last door is closed.

In this case the interior amps cannot be witched offusing the interior lamps witches or JaguarSense eature and require diagnostics to reset the lamp functionality.

### Front End Body Panels -


The intrusion detection module electrical connections, particularly those to the sensors mounted in the roof console, are very delicate and must be handled with care.

The intrusion detection module is an electro-statically sensitive part and should only be handled in an electro-statically ontrolled environment.

When armed, the active anti-theft system can be triggered in one of the following ways:

A door ajar switch indicates a door has been opened. The engine compartment lid or luggage compartment lid ajar switches indicate that either has been opened Either front door latch mechanism indicates a door has been unlocked. The emergency key blade is used to open the L front door. The CJB or RJB are disconnected (this may result in only a partial trigger). An attempt is made to start the engine without a valid 'signal from the Smart Key. The battery backed sounder is disconnected (partial trigger only). The vehicle battery is disconnected on a vehice fitted with a battery backed sounder (partial trigger only. The inclination sensor detects a change in vehicle attitude. The intrusion detection module detects movement within the cabin. Panic alarm from the Smart Key.

The door modules provide the interface between the door latchmotors, the door latchswitches and the The doo modules provide door switch status ifomation and enable the door latch-motors on request from the C or the keyless vehice module.

The keyless veicemodule iterfaes with the entral locking, Radi Frequency (RF) reiverand collectsF sial ifomatior which is transmitted from the Smart Key.This infomation is translated into commands which are passed on the medium speed CAN bus to the:

CJB,   
RJB   
door modules, and instrument clúster.

The keyless vehicle module also monitors:

•4 interior antennae,   
1 luggage compartment antenna,   
a rear bumper antenna, and   
4 door handle antennae if the passive entry system is fitted.

On vehicles with passie entry, the aitional fast latch motors are controlled via the keylessvehicle module and the locking status is passed to the CJB on the medium speed CAN bus.

The rear view miors comprise an interio mir mounted to the windhield, and anexterio mimor mounted on each front door cheater.The types of mirors and associated operating functions installed depend on the specification and trim level of the vehicle.

The interior rear view mirror is provided as a electrically operated automatic dimming type.

The automatic dimming mirror comprises an electro-chromatic glass housed within a surounding case that is atached with a bal joint conectoto the mirr stem. Themiror stem inorporates an8pinelectrical coect that  coected to the oof panél wiring harness.

Light sensors are mounted on the front and rear of the mirr surround case. The sensors control the automatic dimming feature to reduce glare from the headlights of following vehicles.

The automatic dimming function is permanently active when the ignition is in power mode 4 (Acessory) and power mode 6 (ition).The fwardaigight eso moitors the ambint iht evel at thefront of the eide; theeward faing light sensor monitors the light level coming from the rear of the vehicle. When light from the rear of the vehicle exceeds the ambient light level from the front of the vehicle, the automatic dimming circuit darkens the interior miror surface.

Automatic dimming is inhibited when reverse gear is selected to provide the driver with maximum vision. On vehicles with automati trasmision, the reverse gearsli provided by te  (trnsmission control modulevia the high speed N bus to the CJB. The CJB then provides a power feed to the mirror.

lectricall operated and heated exterior mirrors are installed asstandard.Depending on the specication and trim level ofthe ehicle, the following options are available:

Power fold (switch pack operated feature) and auto fold (remote handset operated feature)   
Memory recall   
Reverse gear mirror dip

-he power fold/auto fold feature is available only when power fold mirrors are installed to the vehicle.

The auto fold and reverse gear mirro dip functions are not customer configurable, but may be enabled or disabled by the dealer using the Jaguar approved diagnostic system.

The LH door miror incorporates an ambient air temperature sensor that is hardwired to the EM (engine control module. The ECM is conected to the and ther control modules via the high speed CN bus.The sensor provides ifoation to the Etats ten tasmiteon teedim seed anbus fosey oer conro odules.

The exterior mirror lamps are controlled by the interior lighting function

The door mirrors are controlled using aswitch pack locatedon the driver's door The witch pack contains  non-latching miror select sitches labeled and ' and a 4-way directinal joystick. The witch pack is connected to the driver door control module vi the LiN bus.The driver and front passenger door control modules ar conected vi the medium speed CAN bus.A hardwired connection between each door control module and the corresponding door mirror provides the supply and ground paths for the mirror motors.

:ach exterior door miror incorporates 2 motors to control horizontal (left/right) and vertical (up/down) adjustments.

On vehicles installed with a drivers power operated memory seat and memory exterior mirors, a potentiometer is incorporated within each mirror motor and is used to provide infomation regarding the actual motor positions. The current position and memory positions of each door mirror motor are maintained and storéd within the coresponding door control module.

The memory exterior mimor positions are also monitored and stored within door control module memory when the reverse gear nirror dip fúnction is used.

When reverse gear isselected, the door control module stores the current mirror position and wil then dip passenger mirror glassto a default dip position. While reverse gear is selected it is possible to store a prefered dipped mimor position by adjusting the passenger mirro glass to the desired position via the miro switch pack. When the desired position i achieved using the switch, the new dip position willbe automatically stored by the door control module when reverse gear is de-selected.Therefoe wheneverse gear is re-selected, the dip position realled by the door control module will be the ew reverse gear mirror dip stored position. When reverse gear is deselected the mirror glass will utomatically move to the previous stored position prior to reverse gear selection.

Reverse gearmirror dip is only available when memory mirros are installed, and reverse gear mirro dp is enabled within the instrument cluster.

f the driver selects a memory recallfunction using the memory seat switch pack, the driver's memory seat and exterior nemory mirrors are moved to a stored memory position.

Exterior mirrors with the power fold/uto fold feature icoporate a motor located in the hinge of each exterior mirror arm. Operation of the power fold feature isachieved using the exterior miror switch pack. peration of the auto fold feature is achieved using the remote handset.

The power fold function is active when the ignition is in power mode 6 (Ignition).

Both exterior mirrors wil power fold when the mirror switch pack'' and 'R'switches are pressed together. Pressing the switches again will unfold the mirrors.

When the instrument cluster is cofigured for the auto fold feature, the mirrors wil fold in when the remote handset lock button is pressed.The mirrors willunfold when the vehicle is unlocked using the remote handset unlock button.

NOTE: If the mirors are folded in using the miror switch pack (power fold and the vehicle is then locked, subsequent unlocking of the vehicle will not unfold the mirrors.

When the remote handset unlock button is operated, the C recognizes the remote handset for that vehicle and acknowled :he request.

When the vehicle is locked the door control modules reverse the polarity of the mirror fold motor, power and ground connections to operate the mirrors in the opposite direction.

Exterior mirror heating is provided with heater elements bonded to the back of the mirro glass. Power supply for the miror heating elements is provided by the corresponding driver or passenger door control modul.

Operation of the exterio mirror heaters is full automatic and not controllable by the driver Exteri miror heater peration is determined by ambient air temperature and windshield wiper status.

Make sure that the vehicle battery is fully charged before carying out this procedure.

After the battery has been disconnected or a new window regulator and motor or door module has been instaled, it is necessary to initialize each door window motor separately to operate the one-touch and anti-trap function.

DIn addition to this manual procedure, the approved diagnostic tool can also be used to initialize the door window motor.

Start the engine.

Operate the window control switch until the door window glass is in the fully closed position, continue to operate the window control switch for a further two seconds.

3.Release the window control switch.

4Operate the window control switch in the closed position and continue to operate the window control switch for a further two seconds.

5Operate the window control switch until the door window glass is in the fully open position (one-touch down).

If the door window motor initialization has been completed correctly, when the window control switch is operated, the door window glass should move to the fully closed position (one-touch up) automatically.

If the door window glass does not fully close automatically (one-touch up), repeat the complete proceure.

Operate the window control switch once to the close position.

If multiple attempts have failed to initialize the door windo motor, refer the diagnosis and testing procedure. For additional information, refer to: láss, Frames and Mechanisms (501-11, Diagnosis and Testing).

7.Repeat the door window motor initialization for each door window motor.

The closing mechanism of the doors is by an electronic latch with the adition of a soft-closing motor.The closing motor pull :he latch closed for the last 6 mm of travel.

3oth the sliding glass panel and front blind motors have a thermal protection device built into the control module software t orotect them from overheating. The operating parameters are as follows:

If the motor temperature is between 60 and 77 degrees  the roof operation is restricted to a close only function.   
Ifthe motor temperature exceeds77 degrees during the closing function the movement will not be interupted.   
If the motor temperature exceeds 77 degrees C when the roof is closed movement will be inhibited.   
If the anti-trap function is operational when closing, the reverse movement of the motor willcomplete its movement regardless of motor temperature.

Thermal protection for the sliding glass panel motor and front blind motor are functioned in unison, therefore if one motor exceeds 0 or 77 degrees  the same restrictions, as defined above, wil apply to both motors. For example if the front blin cannot be opened due to thermal protection the sliding glass panel will also ignore the opening command.

In service, if any fault is detected, the message center displays the warning Check Pedestrian System.

The hood deplyment actuators are non-serviceable components. If they are replaced their bar code labels must be read anc recorded in the service database against the VIN (vehicle identification number) for security purposes.

After deployment of the pedestrian protection system, the vehicle must be stopped as soon as it is sae to do so. The hazard ing amps willbe activated and can only bewitched offby pressing the gine START/SOP button to tum the ngine off and onagain. A waming message Check Pedestrian System wil appear in the message center and the vehicle should be transported to the nearest dealer/authorised repairer. The vehicle must not be driven when the hood has been deployed.

![](images/_MISSING_b8fef463afda382cf26e50651ee4c19d3e27e32537eb4bcb3260d3fb0a6abf03.jpg)

The hood actuators are pyrotechnic air bags installed on mounting brackets next to the hood hinges. When the hood actuators are deployed, interface plates on the actuators contact reinforced areas on the hood, and raise the rear of the hood.

![](images/_MISSING_7feb95ffea237b12f04eb232796175e0f296035961693b35f7b80879b6c0f683.jpg)

E128693

The pedestrian impact sensors are acclerometers mounted on the rear ofthe front bumper. The RCM uses the sensor inputs to monitor for low level impacts typical of pedestrian accidents.

The two-piece hood i faricated from aluminum.The inner panel has a hexagonal structure, which allows the energy from an ipact t be asoedeffetively across the fullarea of thehood.The hoodals hasufint strength inthe ear coss-bean to accept the forces from the actuators and maintain a stable condition.

When deployed, the front hood latches act as the pivot points and the rear hinges allow a controlled degree of upward movement before retaining the hood at the end of its deployment, thus limitin its total upward travel and stabilizing its position.

Hood Hinges

![](images/_MISSING_cd4b1c2fd5f5f8895c2562ef44f6266ba22ea068052a462afa1cecb3ffc148d5.jpg)

E95115   
![](images/_MISSING_d121639b488847647e56b057fe5128ad0d028cc59af6954eaad2d63cfb21d257.jpg)

The hood hingesincorporate anumber of leaves.Thisincludes a leafattached to the body, an intermediate leaf and a lea attached to the hood.During nomal peration the hinge opens and closes using the hood and inteediate leaves. These are attached together by a firin pin. When the actators are fired the firing pins fail This allows the hood and intermediate leaves to separate and deploy the hood upwards.

The hinges deform during the deployment process and will need to be replaced.

The body plays asigificant role in the ncreasing trend of evermore rapidy changing model variants.The diffent customer groups arestrngined by the desig andshape of the body. At the same time the stabilit of the body plays the most important part in ensuring passenger and driver safety.Lightweight construction, altemative materials, composite materials, plastics and appropriate joining processes are all design features that characterise modem Jaguar vehicle bodies.

In terms of manufacturing technology, modern safety cell bodies can be produced almost without any problems. Jaguar guarantee high quality standards by ensuring that mechanical strength properties are tried and tested in numerous computer simulations, crash tests, by testing materials and by employing sophisticated manufacturing technologies. In the event of repairs it is vital that the production quality standards are upheld.This requires a well-equipped workshop, and places particular emphasis on the qualifications of the workshop technicians. Up-to-date knowledge of curent manufacturing tchlesand cotiustring o eepa metodand thisare ital oig-qality ody reairhe moe specific repair manuals and the genral repair techniques provide valuable support when undertaking body repairs.

### Identifying the correct Jaguar Approved Body Repair Facilities


General notes:

Exact diagnosis of the extent of the damage enables proper repair planning   
All body repairs must be carried out in accordance with the guidelines in this Body Repair Manual   
The stability and strength properties of the body must be taken into account during body repairs.The body has exact defined deformation patterns that must not be affected by any repair work   
For instance, the crumple zones absor the bulk of the impact energy. I any unprofessional repair techniques or methods are used in these areas then this can pose a fundamental threat to vehicle safety

Hidden damage:

Aswellas looking at extemal indicators like flaked off paint, it is vital to check for hidden body damage or deformatior that is not visible from the outside. Large attached parts like bumpers and inner fenders often need to be removed to allow accurate assessment of damage to underlying body parts Gap dimensions offer another altemative for diagnosis by visual inspection. If water leaks occur after bodywork repairs, the cause can be established using the checks described below. A systemati and logical procedure is required to locate water leaks. Before beginning extensive checks, a thorough visual inspection must be carried out.

Visual Inspection

- The following characteristics may indicate existing leaks:   
Check the clearance and accurate fit of ancilary components such as the hood, taigate,iftgate, doors, and so on.   
Check for correct fit and possible damage to sealing elements such as blanking plugs, rubber door weather strips, and so on.   
- Check water drain holes for unhindered flow.

Various tests can be used to provide further information on possible leaks:

- Water test   
-Washer test   
- Road test   
- Chalk (powder) test

Water test

OTE: Never aim a jet of water directly at a door weather strip or rubber seals.

Carry out the water test with a second person present (in the passenger compartment).   
Use variable washer nozzles (concentrated water jet to fine spray mist).   
Start in the lower section and spray the whole area, working upwards in stages.

### Roof opening panel - front and rear fixed glass panels


In this test, the clamping load and the bearing surface of the seal are checked. Performing the test:

- Dust the door seal with powder or coat with chalk.   
-Coat the bearing surface of the seal with a thin film of petroleum jelly.   
-Slowly close the door and open it again.   
- Check the width and continuity of the imprint on the door seal.

If a vehicle develops a leak after body repairs, the following points must be taken into consideration in particular:

The correct seating of ancillary components and their seals must be checked.   
The correct alignment of doors/tailgate and liftgate must be checked. The associated seals must not be damaged and must be installed correctly.   
Check that panel seams are correctly sealed.   
The correct seating of rubber grommets must be checked.   
Directly-glazed windows must have correct and complete bonding.

Diagnosis: - Water ingress in the lower part of the interior door trim or in the rocker panel area.

- The water shield fitted behind the interior door trim exists to drain off water that has entered the door via the   
drainage holes,either downwards or outwards. If the water shield seal is damaged or has been fitted incorecty,   
then water can get into the passenger compartment.   
In addition to this, the drainage holes can become clogged with leaves, dirt or excess cavity protection agents. Water gathers in the door and ingresses into the passenger compartment. Check water shield for damage or correct fitting.   
- If the water shield needs to be re-bonded, then approved seam sealer should be used.   
- Before the water shield is installed, the drainage holes must be checked for unhindered flow.

Diagnosis:

- Ingress of water into the rocker panel area Cause: - Insufficient clamping load between seal and door. Corrective action:

DNOTE: When adjusting the clamping load, the profile alignment of the relevant components must always be taken into consideration.

NOTE: Do not realign the flange too far in the direction of the door as this can reduce the bearing surface of the seal to the door.

- Check clamping load:   
The easiest way to check the clamping load of a seal to the respective bearing surface is by means of a paper strip test. This consists of trapping strips of paper at various points between the door and the seal, and fully closing the door If it is possible to pul out the paper with no great resistance, then the clamping load is too low.   
- Adjust the clamping load:   
- The clamping load is normally adjusted using the striker. When doing so, the edge alignment from the door to the side panel, or from the front door to the rear door must be taken into account.   
- Another setting method is to realign the panel flange for the seal mounting. The clamping load is increased by moving the flange towards the door.   
Check the bearing surface:   
Apply chalk evenly to the surface of the seal. Evenly coat the bearing surface of the door with petroleum jelly. ose the doo fuly, the lock mustengaepenthe doorThe imprint of the chalk earing urface cane identified in the film of petroleum jelly.   
- The bearing surface should be at least 5mm across at all points.

Other causes:

- The door seal must completely seal the door where it meets the bodywork. Water can ingress direct o ndirec into the interiorof the vehice if the seal is damaged at any point. rective action: - A damaged or worn door seal must always be installed in full. -When installing the seal, the following must be taken into account: -Always fit the seal first in the area of the narrow radii (corner points). Next, secure the seal to the flange evenly by tapping lightly with a rubber hammer The installed seal must not be kinked at any point.

VOTE: The prescribed length of a seal must not be shortened.

Other cause:

The door seal is attached to the welded flange all the way round. If this welded flange is uneven or damaged at any point (usually in areas with small radii) then this point could be subject to leaks. - A stretched seal carrier can also cause a leak. - In both cases, water gets into the vehicle interior under the seal carrier. Corrective action: - Align the deformed welded flange using a hammer and anvil block, prevent and, if necessary, repair any paint damage.

n the case of the roof opening panel - front and rar fixed glass panels, the same problems can arise as for a windscreen.The ame corrective actions must therefore be used.

NOTE: I the case of the sliding central glass panel, the rubber seals and the lock actuator or latch mechanism must be :hecked first of all.

Diagnosis: - Ingress of water at the roof opening panel.   
Cause: - The roof opening panel frame incorporates drain holes in each front corner allowing water to drain via the A-pillars and each rear comner allowing water to drain via the roof panel channels.   
- Damaged, worn, or incorrectly fitted seals on the sliding central glass panel.   
- Incorrect alignment of the sliding central glass panel.   
- Damaged, worn, or incorrectly fitted seals on the roof opening panel frame.   
- Water drain channels or water drain holes blocked.

Corrective action:

- Check the seals on the sliding central glass panel, install as necessary.   
Check the corect adjustment of the sliding central glass panel, adjust as necessary, replace any worn or damaged components as necessary.   
- Check the internal seal of the roof opening panel frame, realign or install as necessary.   
- Check the water drain channels and holes for blockages, clear blockages as necessary.   
- Check the drainage system for unhindered flow.

Diagnosis: - Ingress of water into the luggage area.

Cause:

- The leak problems of the luggage compartment lid correspond to those of the doors.   
- In addition to this, the area to be sealed is much bigger. The routing holes for cables and hoses must also be sealed.   
- The rubber grommets for the routing holes must be checked for damage and correct seating (fully unhooked).   
- The grommets around the luggage compartment lid hinges may leak.

- Check the rubber grommets and re-position, reseal or install new, if necessary.

Belt squeal is a high frequency air-bome noise generated by slippage of the ribbed Veebelt on the power steering pump pulley.'Squeal increases with system loading and at full lock

Clonk is a structure-bome noise heard as a loose-sounding ratle or vibration coming from the steering column. Clonk can be i rivig ai ecbleesoug rooi  mpcha maasr. Clonk requires a tie-rod load impact

Column knock is a loose-sounding ratte or vibration generated by the steering column shaft contacting other portions of th column assembly. The noise i both audible and tactieColumn knock is enerated by driving over coblestones or rough pavement. It is not necessary to turn the steering wheel to create this noise

Column rattl isa metalic sounding noise created when appying ahighly impulsive force to the steering wheel Column rattle is often used to comine the more general group of colum nises incuding clonk and column knock. Column ratte noises can be caused by clonk, knock, loose column components, bonus parts etc. A series o parked, straight-line driving, and coering tests should be carried out to isolate the source/sources

Grinding ia low freuency noise in the column when the steering wheel is tumed. is generally caused by inteference between moving components such as the steering wheel to steering column shroud

Grunt is a honking' sound eliited when coming off one of the steering stops. Grunt is generally excited during parking manoeuvres with á low to medium speed steering input

Hiss or Valve Hiss is a highfrequency sound coming from the steering gear when the system i loaded. It i a rushing or 'swish noisethat desn't change freuncy ith .Hissthe neral noise geerated by the flow of hyuli fuid trough restrictions in the steering system. Restrictions include the rotary teering valve, power string tubes, conectors, tuning

orifices, etc. Hiss can be air-bome and structure-bome, but the structure-bome path through the steering intermediate shaft is usually'dominant

Moan is the general structure-bomne noise of the steering system. Moan is primarily transmitted to the driver via the body structure through the pump mount, engine mounts, power steering lines and power steering brackets. On some veices, moan ia loud humming noise,often present when the wheel is turedand the system is laded. It may change frequncy with engine RPM and if the system is loaded or unloaded

CAuTIoN: Do NoT attempt to adjust the steering gear yoke. Failure to follow this instruction will invalidate the steering gear warranty.

Steering gear knock is a ratle sound and steering wheel vibrtion caused by separation of the steeing gear and pinion while drving over bumps. It is astructure-bome noise transmitted through the intemediate shaft and column. Steering gear knock can also be heard as a thump' or impact noise that occurs with the vehiclestationary when the steering whee is released from a loaded position and allowed to retum to rest. Noise occurs with the engine on or off

Weep is an air-bome noise, occasional generated when turing the steering across lock at a constant rate. When present on a vehicle the noise, once initiated can often be maintained acrossa large proportion of the available steering movement

Whistle is similar to hiss but is louder and of a higher frequency.tis also more of a pure tone noise than hiss. Whistle is air-borne and is generated by a high flow rate of hydraulic fluid through a smal restriction

The steering column comprises the upper column assembly, the intermediate shaft assembly and the steering whee. The 3 component are positively connected together to pass driver rotary input from the steering wheel to a linear output of the steering rack.

The electric steering column is a standard fitment on all models.The upper column assembly contains electrical adjustment for stering wheel reachand ake the lectic colm lck mechaism and the serng angeensoreeingadjustment memoy positions are stored in the driver's seat module. The column also features a tilt away' function which moves the steering column away from the driver allowing easier exit and entry to the vehicle.

Column adjustment is provided by a single motor for both reach and rake adjustment. Operation of the column adjustment is controlled by a four way joystick type switch located in the column lower shroud.Colum adjustment is an integral part of th driver position memory'system.

Power for the steering column operation is supplied via a megafuse in the  (battery junction box) to the C (entral junction box).The C in tum supplies power to the column djustment motor, the reach and rake solenoids and also the adjustment potentiometers in response to driver requests made with the column adjust switch.

The column adjust switch is a joystick type, 2-axis switch with positions for reach and rake adjustment.The switch can also b rotated to change the mode selection from auto to manual The switch is hardwired to the  with  wires. The  wires provide a power supply to the switch and the mode select switch, the third connection is a ground provided by the CB. Up/down (rake) and in/out (reach) selections on the switch are each passed through a resistor of ifering values to the B. he monitos te utut val from theitch and peratesthe clum adjustent moto inthe equired directiad simultaneously energizes the required solenoid for rake o reach adjustment. When the applicable solenoid is energized, a clutch is engaged and locates on a lead screw. The motor rotates the lead screw and the rotational drive of the screw is transferred into linear movement of the applicale clutch to move ither the rake or reach adjustment. For reach adjustment, the lead screw drives the outer housing in or out as reqired. For rake adjustment the lead screw drives a rake lever which moves the column up or down as required.

he position of the column is moitored by potentiometers which are connected to the .The  monitors the output signal rom' the potentiometers to precisely controi the positioning of the column in each plane.

The C controls the memory postioning of the column via a medium speed CAN (ontrolle area network bus connection to the driver's seat module.The  reives ioation ardng the particular remote handset used to enter the veiceand outputs positional information relative to that stored for the handset This ifomation is used by the  to move the column to the memorized position relating to the remote handset used.

Theumidity and temperature sensor is behind a gril i the instrument panel, on the nboard side of the steering column. The sensor incorporates:

• ANTCthermistor to measure temperature.   
Acapacitive sensor element to measure humidity.   
A motor driven fan to draw air through the sensor and over the sensing elements.

Humidity within the passenger compartment is controlled by raising and lowering the evaporator temperature. An increase in evaporator temperature increases the moisture content of the air entering the passenger compartment. Lowering the evaporator temperature reduces the moisture content of the air entering the passenger compartment.

The driver can use the joy pad' on the RH steering wheel switch assembly to navigate through a series of menu-driven features. The menu's are displayed in the RH side of the instrument cluster and override the tachometer display. I another function of higher priority is required to be displayed, then the menu display willalso be overidden. The menu will be displayed until the driver closes the menu display.

When the driver uses the joy pad on the RH steering wheel switch assembly the menu appears as vertical stack of 6 rows o nenu selections as follows:

Main Menu Show Warnings (OK) Vehicle Set-up Trip Computer Display Settings Service Menu.

Most menu levels are contained on one page, however forlists with more than 6 subitems aditional up/down arrows are positioned adjacent to the menu to signify there are addtional menu tems to display. The menu items and sun-menu items will not obscure any active warnings in thé instrument cluster.

ependent on vehicle specification, if a feature is not present on the vehicle, it will not be shown in any of the menus.

The AHB sensitivity is only available for NAS markets as a test option.

he instrument cluster menus are navigated and items selected using the joypad control.The joy pad control ia 2-axis switch vith a central button (OK).

To exit the menu's, select the top menu 'Main Menu' and press OK to close the menu display.

The AHB operates as part of the automatic headlight system. When driving at night with the lighting control switch in the automatic position and the LH steering column multifunction switch in the central position, with sufficient darkness (approximately 1 lux or less) and a suitable road speed, the AHB will automatically operate the high beam lighting when neessary. The driver can manually override the AHB system at any time. When the AHB system is activated, pulling the LHsteering column multifunctio switch to the high beamflash positio or pushing it foward to the high beam position will dectivate the system and the AHB warning indicator in the instrument cluster will extinguish.

When the multifunction switch is returned to the central position, from a forward high beam position, the system is re-activated and the AHB warning indicator will illuminate again.

Clicking, popping or grinding noises may be caused by the following:

Cut or damaged CV joint boots resulting in inadequate or contaminated lubricant in the outboard or inboard CV joint bearing housings   
Loose CV joint boot clamps   
Another component contacting the rear drive half shaft   
Worn, damaged or incorrectly installed wheel bearing, suspension or brake component

Vibration at highway speeds may be caused by the following:

Out-of-balance front or rear wheels   
Out-of-round tires   
Driveline imbalance   
Driveline run-out (alignment)

The air compressor assembly incorporates:

A two stage compressor driven by an electric motor.   
An air drier.   
A main exhaust valve.   
• A pilot exhaust valve.   
An air intake / exhaust port.   
A HP outlet port.

The compressor motor is operated by power from the air suspension relay in the R, which is controlld by the air suspension module.To prevent damage caused by overeating, the temperature of the compressor and motor i calculated by a software model i the i suspension module.The alculated temperature i based on compressoperating pressure, olte, me d ambient air temperature. The air suspension module discontinues compressor operation if the calulated temperature increases to 00 (1.Compressor operation resumes when the ir suspension module calculates the temperature has decreased to 80  (176 F).

The air drierremoves moisture from the air delivered by the compressor to the HP outlet port, and consists of a chamber that contains water absoring desiccant beads. When the air suspension system is depressurized, air is vented back through the air compressor assembly, t initite air drier reeneration. The lean dry ir vented from the system re-activates the desiccant beads.

The main exhaust alve controls the release ofir from the irsupension system trugh the irintake/exhaust port. t also acts as a PRV (pressure relief valve) and minimum pressure retention valve. The PRV function limits the maximum pressure from the compressor to 17.5 bar (254 f/in². The minimum pressure retention function limits the minimum pressure in the system to between 0.25 and 1.00 bar (3.75 and 14.5 Ibf/in2).

The pilot exhaust valve is a solenoid operated valve that controls the operation of the main exhaust valve. A pwM (pulse width modulation) signal from the ir suspension module controls the pilot exhaust valve to apply system pressure to thepilot chamber of the main exhaust valve.

The system is controlled by buttons adjacent to the JaguarDrive selector on the floo console. The buttons allow the selection of oné of the following thrée modes:

Special modes off Winter mode Dynamic mode.

The instrument cluster will display the selected JaguarDrive control mode in the message center.   
Refer to: Instrument Cluster (413-01 Instrument Cluster, Description and Operation).

The JaguarDrive control system uses a combination of a number of vehicle sub-systems to achieve the required vehicle characteristics for the mode selected. The following sub-systems make up the JaguarDrive control system:

EMS (engine management system). For additional information, refer to:

Electronic Engine Controls (303-14B Electronic Engine Controls - V8 S/C 5.0L Petrol, Description and Operation), Electronc Engine Controls(03-14Electronic Engine Controls -  5. Petrol, Description and Operation). Automatic transmission. Refer to: Transmission Description (307-01 Automatic Transmission/Transaxle, Description and Operation). Brake system. Refer to: Anti-Lock Control - Stability Asst (206-09 Anti-Lock Control - Stability Assist, Description and Operation). Adaptive dynamics. Refer to: Vehicle Dynamic Suspension (204-05 Vehicle Dynamic Suspension, Description and Operation). Electronic differential control (where fitted).

he JaguarDrive control software is stored in the JaguarDrive selector module located below the JaguarDrive selector. The nodule detects the selection made using the buttons and transmits a signal on the high speed CAN bus, which is recived ach of the sub-system control modules.

ach of the affected sub-system control modules contain software, which appies the correct operating parameters to their :ontrolled system for the JaguarDrive control mode selection made.

Each sub-system control module also provides feedback for the selected mode so that the JaguarDrive control software can check that all systems have changed to the correct operating parameters.

NOTE: The JaguarDrive control system is a co-ordinating system only. It CANNOT generate a fault in one of the articipating sub-systems. All participating ub-systems should be FULLy diagnosed before assuming a fault with JaguarDri control. The JaguarDrive selector module should not be replaced until allother options have been exhausted.

The ZF HP28 transmission is an electronically controlled, hydraulically operated, six speed automatic unit. The hydraulic anc electronic control elements of the transmissin, including the M (transmissioncontrol module), are incorporated in a sing unit located inside the transmission and is known as 'Mechatronic'.

5.OL SC (supercharger) and 3.0L diesel models use an uprated derivative of the ZF 6HP28 transmission used in the 5.0L naturally aspirated módels.

The ZF 6HP28 transmission has the following features:

Designed to be maintenance free   
Transmission fluid is 'fill for life'   
The torque covertefeatures a cotrolled slip feature with electronically regulated control of lock-up, creating a smooth transition to the fully locked condition   
Shift programs controlled by the TCM Electroni park lock, controlled by the TCm, with a mechanical emergency release   
ASIS (adaptive shift strategy), t provide continuous adaptation of shift changes to suit the driving style of the driver, which'can'vary from sporting to economical. Connected to the ECM (engine control module) via the high speed CAN (controlle area network) bus for communications Default mode if major faults occur   
Diagnostics available from the TCM via the high speed CAN bus.

The transmission selections are made using the rotay JaguarDrive selector in thefloor console and two padde switches on the seering wheel. Refer to: Exteral Controls (307-05, Description and Operation).

Operation of the transmission is controlled by the TM (transmission control module), which electrically activates various solenoids to control the transmission gear selection. The sequence of solenoid activation is based on programmed information in the TCM memory and physical transmission operating conditions such as vehicle speed, throttle position, engine load and JaguarDrive selector position.

The shift elements, clutches and brakes are actuated hydraulically Fluid pressure is applied to the required clutch and/or brake, pressing the plates together and allwing drive to be tranmitted trough the plates.The purpose of the shift lements is to perform power-on shifts with no interuption to traction and smooth transition between gear ratios.

The transmission comprises the main casing which houses allof the transmission components. The main casing also incorporates an integral bel housing.

A fluid pan is attached to the lower face of the main casing and is secured with bolts. The fluid pan is sealed to the main casing with a gasket. Removal of the fluid pan allows access to the Mechatronic valve block. The fluid pan has a magnet located around the drain plug which collects any metallic particles present in the transmission fluid.

Afluid fitrlocated inside thefluid pan. f the transmission fluid becomescontaminated or afterany sevice work, the fluid pan with integral filter must be replaced.

The integral bl housing provides protection for the torque converter assembly and also provides the attachment for the earbox to the engine clinderblock.The torque converteris a non-seiceable assembly which also contains the lock-up clutch mechanism The toue coverterdrives a cscent type pump vi drivetangThe fuid pump ilcatedin the main caig, behind the torque converter.

The main casing contains the following major components:

Input shaft   
Output shaft   
Mechatronic valve block which contains the solenoids, speed sensors and the TCM Three rotating multiplate drive clutches   
Two fixed multiplate brake clutches   
A single planetary gear train and a double planetary gear train.

The TC (torque converter clutch is hydraulicall controlled by an EPRS, which is controlled by the M. This allows the torqu converter to have three states of operation as fóllows:

Fully engaged   
Controlled slip variable engagement Fully disengaged.

The TCC is controlled by two hydraulic spool valves located in the valve block. These valves are actuated by pilot pressure supplied via a solenoid valve which is also located in the valve block. The solenoid valve is operated by PWM (pulse width modulation) signals from the TCM to give full, partial or no lock-up of the torque converter.

Active regeneration start when the particulate loading of the DPF reaches a threshold as monitored or determined by the DP ontrol software.he threshold calulation  based on riving stle, distance travelled and back pressure signals from the differential pressure sensor.

Active regeneration generaly occus every 250 miles (400 km) although this is dependant on how the vehicle is driven. For exampletheeirivenat low lad i urantrafirulal activeatinilcurmoreoftenThis duto the ai bildp of pariulates te F h i te iceriveat igh sees when passe rti wil he occurred.

The DPF softwar incooratesa milege trigger which i usedas back-up foractive rgration. Iactivergenration has not been initiated by a back pressure signal from the diffential pressure sensor, regeration iequested based on distance travelled.

Active regeneration of the DPFi commenced when the temperature of the DPF is increased to the combustion temperature of the partices. The DF temperature is raised by inreasing the exhaust gas temperature This is achieved by introducing post-injection of fuel after the pilot and main fuel injections have occurred.

.t is determined by the DPF software monitoring the signals from the two DPF temperature sensors to establish the emperature of thé DPF.Depending on the DPF temperature, the DPF software requests the ECM (engine control module t erform either one or two post-injections of fuel:

The first post-injection of fuel retards combustion inside the cylinder which increases the temperature of the exhaust gas.   
The second postijection of fuel  ijectedate n the powerstroke cycle.The fuel partly comust in the clinder, bu some unbumt fuel also passes into the exhaust where it creates an exothermic event within the catalytic converter further increasing the temperature of the DPF.

The active regeneration processtakes up to 20 minutes to complete.The first phase increases the DPF temperature to 500 (92.The second phase further increases the DPF temperature to 600C (112F) which is the optimum temperature for article combustion. This temperature is then maintained for 15-20 minutes to ensure complete oxidation of the particles within the DPF. The oxidation process converts the carbon particles to carbon dioxide.

The active regeneration temperature of the DPF i closely monitored by the DPF software to maintain a target temperature of 600(11t theFiThe emperature cotro sures tat the tmperatures  not exceed the peratial mits ofte turcharnd the atalytic certerThe trhrnet mperature must ot exce 830526and the catalytic converter brick temperature must not exceed 800°c (1472°F) and the exit temperature must remain below 875° (1382°F).

During the active regeneration process the following ECM controlled events occur:

The turbocharger is maintained in the ful open position. This minimizes heat transmission from the exhaust gas to the turbocharer and reduces the rate of éxhaust gas flow llwing optimum heating of the DP. f the driver demands an increase in engine torque, the turbocharger will respond by closing the vanes as necessary. The throttle is closed as this assists in increasing the exhaust gas tmperature and reduces the rate of exhaust gas flow which has the effect of reducing the time for the DpF to reach the optimum temperature. The EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) valve is closed. The use of EGR decreases the exhaust gas temperature and therefore prevents the optimum DpF temperature being achieved.

f due to vehice usage and/or driving style, the active reeeration process canot take place ori unable to rgenerate th D the daler ca force rerate the Thi is achived by ither drivig the vie ntil the egine iat t norma operating temperature and then driving for a further 20 minutes at speeds of not less than 30 mph (48 km/h).

The climate control system is controlled by the ATC (automatic temperature control module. It controls the heating and entilation sstem and teaicoigsystem t reuate the temperature lume and dtriuti ointthe passenger compartment. The system is eithera dual zone or four zone system, depending on vehicle speification, which is fully automati and capable of supplying individual temperature levelto each zone of the passenger compartment, up to a maximum diffentia oapproximatel.Manual verridesforthe ystm icude ietisoure, blowerspeed and air distribution.These selections can be made on the TSD (touch screen display), the P (integrated control panel and, on four zone systems, the rear climate control panel.

The two and four zone climate control systems contain the same hardware. Diferent software in their respective ATC modules produces the different functionality required by the two systems.

The source of inet air is automatially controlled by theAT module, unlessverridenby pressing the air eirulation switch on the P integrated control panel to givetimedor atched recirulation. Abrief press ofthe witch illminates the switch indicator and activates timed recirculation. Pressing and holding the switch causes the switch indicator to flash and then illuminate constantly, indictig that the iinet  atched reiulatin and theitch can be leased.A second press o the switch cancels rirculation and the ATC module retums the rcirculation door to the fresh air position. Timed reirculation is automatically cancelled after a set time, which varies with ambient air temperature.

During automatic control, the ATC module determines the required position of the reciulation doo from its 'comfort' algorithm aiie soee oieoeteiuifoies thet fresh ir for  seond reethe ii the eiceThe  modue reeatthisyleni the oltio longer present.

The sensitivity of the pllution sensor can be adjusted on the TSD (touch screen display) using the Setings button on the t aehe lg unieoffugieiimeti. If tere ia fault with the polutio sensor the A module disables automati operation of the reirculation door.

When A is selected the ATC module maintains the evaporator at an operating temperature that varies with the passenger compartment coling requirments. If the requirement for cooled air decreases, the ATC module raises the evaporator operating temperature by reducing the flow of refrigerant provided by the A compressor The AT module closely controls the rate of temperature increase to avoid introducing moisture into the passenger compartment.

fhe rquirement for cooledair increases, the A module lowers the eaporator perating temperature by increasing the flow f refrigerant provided by the A/Ccompressor.

When A/C is off, the compressor current signal supplied by the ATC module holds the A/C compressor solenoid valve in the minimum flow position, effectively switching off the A/C function.

The AT module incorporates limit for the operating pressure of the refrigerant system. If the system approaches the high pressure limit, the compressor current signal is progressively reduced until the system pressure decreases.f the system falls below the low pressure limit, the compressor current signal is held at its lowest setting so that the A/C compressor is maintained at its minimum stroke. This avoids depletion of the lubricant from the A/ compressor.

All vehiceshave auoad sesoristalled in the center of the defrost grillof the instrument panel. ehices with a four zne systems have a second, identical, sunload sensor installed in the center of the parcel shelf.

The sunload sensor consists of two photoelectric cell that provide the ATC module with inputs of light intensity; one as sensed coming from the left of the vehicle and one as sensed coming from the right. The iputs are a measure of the solar heating effect o the veice and are used by the A module t adjust blower spee, temperature and ditiutint mproe comfort in the individual zones.

WARNINGS:

BEFORE CHECKING AND TOPPING-UP THE BATTERY ELECTROLYTE, REFER TO THE HEALTH AND SAFETY PRECAUTIONS SECTION.

AGM TECHNOLOGY BATTERIES ARE FULLY SEALED FOR LIFE AND NO ATTEMPT SHOULD BE MADE TO CHECK OR TOP UP "HE ELECTROLYTE LEVEL.

On certain types of battery the electrolyte level may need to be checked.

Make sure the battery is of a type suitable for topping up. These types of batteries willhave cell plugs visible on the top face of the battery or a removable access panel to allow access to the cells. On batteries with a clear or opaque case and level marks, check the electrolyte level by visual inspection of the maximum level indicator mark on the battery casing indicating adequate level above the battery separators. On batteries with black cases, remove the cell plugs or access panel and ensure the electrolyte level is level with the indicator in the cell hole. A flashlight may be required to see the electrolyte level on this type of battery.   
If the electrolyte level is low, top-up using distilled water.

INOTE: Maintenance free and Valve Regulated (AGM) batteries are sealed and therefore cannot be topped up.

The battery is located under the floor in the RH (right-hand) side of the luggage compartment.

The AFS is controlled by an AF control module which is located on the instrument panel frame, behind the glove compartment. The AFS actuators are bi-polar (2 phase) dc stepper motors which are driven by a power output from the AFS power module. The AFS control module receives front and rear suspension height data and vehicle speed signals from the ABS module to adjust the projector module vertically to increase the beam range as the vehicle speed increases.

When the AF control module receives an ignition on signal, the control module perfoms the iitialization procedure which ensures that the headlamps are correctly aligned on both their vertical and horizontal axes.

Vhen activated, AHB will switch the headlamps to high beam when all the following conditions occur:

No relevant oncoming traffic   
No relevant preceding traffic   
In non-urban environment, i.e. with no street lighting   
Ambient light level is below 1 lux – refer to 'Light Levels' section that follows Road speed is suitable - refer to 'Road Speed' section that follows.

When activated, AHB will switch the headlamps to low beam when any of the following conditions occur:

Relevant Oncoming traffic is present   
Relevant Preceding traffic is present   
In urban environment, i.e. with street lighting   
Ambient light level is above 1 lux - refer to 'Light Levels' section that follows   
•Road speed is not suitable – refer to 'Road Speed' section that follows   
Unrecognisable reflective inputs from road signs or markings - refer to 'System Limitations' section that follows.

High beam is generally not required with light levels 'above 1 lux.

Dips, hollows or crests in the road Highly reflective static Road signs

Tight bends   
Poorly illuminated vehicles e.g. cyclists or small mopeds   
Motorway central barriers   
Extreme weather conditions e.g. Fog, heavy snow   
Exterior domestic or industrial lighting

### CAN Harness Architecture


RL (daytime running lamps use the ful intensity low beam headamps which are permanently iluminated when the vehicle i jeing driven. Two DRL systems are available depending on market requirements.

The  (entral junction box) controls the operation of the DRL The DRL are activated once the B detects an ignition on ower mode 6 sinal.

The CB also monitors the lighting control switch and the auto lamps feature and overides the DRL if required.

The DRL for this market use fullintensity low beam headamps. The side markeramps, tail amps and license plate amps will be on, but instrument cluster illumination will be off. DRL are active when the following parameters are met:

PARK is not selected on the electronic transmission selector EPB (electronic parking brake)is off Power mode 6 (ignition on) detected by the CIB The CiB receives an engine running signal The lighting control switch is in the off or side lamps position.

On vehicles fitted with the automatic headamps feature, DRL are verriden if the lighting control switch i in the 'Auto' position and the CJB receives a signal from the rain/light sensor to activate the exterior lihts.

When the  recives a signal to de-activate the automatic headamps feature the DRL function i restored providing the parameters for DRL activation are met.

Ifa module logs a Bus Off DC, it means that the module has detected CAN transmission erors and has disabled it's own CNtransmissions and discoecteditself rom the etwork in an attempt to allow the rest of the etwork to function. At this point the Bus Off DTC s set. A common cause of Bus Off DTs can be a short circuit in the CAN network.

The active antitheft system is availale with three different levels of vehicle protection depending on market speification:

Hinged panel sensing Hinged panel and intrusion sensing Hinged panel, intrusion and inclination sensing.

'he system is controlled by software in the CB and RJB (rear junction box) and indicates a trigger condition:

Visually, using the direction indicators, Audibly, using the vehicle horn and either a passive or active sounder to indicate a trigger condition.

The passive sounder takes the form of an antitheft disc hom located at the rear of the engine compartment on the LH side.   
The active sounder takes the form of a battery backed sounder located in the same position.

The battery backed sounder is fitted with an inclination sensor. The battery backed sounder is a intelligent unit, and communicate to the CiB over a LiN (local interconnect network) bus connection.

Monitoring of the hinged panel is carred out using switches located in each doorlatch assembly, the engine-compartment-li atch assembly, and the luggage-compartment-lid atch assembly. The condition of the switches is monitored by the CB.

Monitoring of front door lock status is caried out using switches located in the doo latch mechanisms. The condition of the switches is monitored by the front door modules and transmitted to the CB over the medium speed CAN (controller area network bus.

Monitoring of the cain interior is caried out using an intrusion detection module mounted behind the roof console.The intrusion detection module comprises an ultrasonic sound wave sensor to determine if there is movement within the cabin.

Information from the intrusion detection module is communicated to the CJB over a LIN bus connection.

he larm inicator is LEDight emitting diodelocated n the instrument cluster When the igition i offthe iicator gives visual indication of the active anti-theft system to show if the alarm system is active or not active.

Dperation of the battery backed sounder is controlled by the C on the LIN bus. The sounder is also connected with a rmanent battey supply via the .An integral, rechrgeable battery powers the sounder if the battery power supply fror :he CJB is interrupted.

An inclination sensor is incorporated into the battery backed sounder, to monitor vehicle altitude, see Inclination Sensor.

The opening and closing functions are controlled by the luggage compartment lid module. The module receives a permanent battery power supply from the RB. To initiate the luggage compartment lid opening sequence a luggage compartment lid release-request is recived by the i from one of the following:

KVM (keyless vehicle module) - signal originates from the Jaguar Smart Key Auxiliary lighting panel - interior luggage compartment lid button Rear bumper mounted - exterior luggage compartment lid button

The CJB responds with the following simultaneous actions:

A hardwire power release to the latch actuator mechanism An opening signal transmited to the power luggage compartment lid module via the medium speed CAN bus.

he processing of the opening signal by the CJB is influenced by a number of factors:

Source of 'opening signal' Vehicle status: locked or unlocked Vehicle equipped with or without passive entry.

Once the atch is released the uggage compartment lid module actuates the motor located in the powered strut to raise the ugcomparmnt itfuleno pres positnWhenthe uggompartmnt iiiening cyclehe autmatisoppoif the liuiedy alssoloateithe oto healsensosial tanmiethe luggage compartment lid module is synchronized with the pre-set memory indicating the stop position of the luggage compartment lid.

To close the luggage compartment lid a hardwired signal is transmitted directly to the luggage compartment lid module when the button, locate on lid's cosing edge is pressed.The moduleperates the pindlemotor in the pposite irection to close the luggage compartment lid to the latch position.

When the latch engages with the striker plate a signal transmitted from the latch actuator mechanism to the luggage compartment lid module cofirms the latch is engaged.The module de-activates the spinde drive and activates the power cinch motor to pull the latch closed through the ast 6 mm of travel. A mechanical cable conection between the motor and latch assembly is used to complete the closing process.

If the battery is disconnected when the luggage compartment lid is closed, the stored and calibratedd opening heights will remain stored when the battery is reconnected. However if power supply to the luggage compartment lid module is disconnected when the luggage compartment lid i open the system wil not ecognize the lid's position and ubseuently wil not function to any switch commands when power is reinstated.To re-calibrate the system, the luggage compartment lid must be moved manuallyto the closed position where it willperfom a soft close and reset the hall sensor counters to zero.

NOTE: If required the luggage compartment lid can be opened and closed manually.

CAUTION: DO NOT CLOSE THE LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LID IF THE VEHICLE BATTERY IS DISCONNECTED. It iS AVISabe to close the latch claw when working on a vehicle with the battery disconnected to prevent accidental closure.

The powered strut operates the swan-neck hinge on the right-hand side of the vehicle.Balljoints positioned at each end of the strut allow it to articulate between fixed mount on the vehie and the moveable hinge. The powered strut opens and closes the luggage compartment lid using anelectricall driven spindle located in the struts intemal electric motor; the lid opening operation is also aided by spring assistance.

he spindle drive comprises an inner and outer tube where the motor and gears in the inner tube drive a threaded spindle vhich' runs on a threaded nut fixed to the inside of the outer tube.

The spinde drive incorporates anoject detection function controlled by the luggagecompartment id module. The function is similrto the antitrap function of acoinglecti window but peratesi both irections. f the ject detection feature activated while the luggage compartment d is either opening or closing, the spindle motor i reversed for a preset period.

A halsensor, located in the spindle motor, monitors the speed of the motor If the speed decreases below a set threshold, indicatig anostctin and asing the mot current drw the powerfeed t the motversed causing he lug compartment lid to move in the opposite direction of travel.

The amount of travel in the opposite direction, before stopping, is determined by the hallsensor count. An exception to the object detection reverse travel functionoccurs when the luggage compartment li i opening through its first few degrees of travel from the tched poition. In these ciumsances i anostace is detected the luggaeompartment idstop inthe position of the obstruction and no travel in the opposite direction occurs.

The exterior mirrors incorporate the following:

Blind spot monitoring indicator •Auto dimming function Turn signal indicators Approach lamps Exterior temperature sensor Heated mirror function Reverse dipping function

Movement of the door mirrors is controlled from a switch pack located on the drivers door. The switch pack contains 2 non-latching mirror select buttons labeled'L' and'R' and a 4-way mirror movement switch. Door miror movement commands are transmitted to the driver's door module over the LiN (local interconnect network) bus. The drivers door module transmits any mimor movement commands to the passenger door module over the medium speed CAN (controller area network) bus.

Movement of the door mirors is caried out by the respective door module. The door modules provide suppy and ground path o the mirror motors and monitor mirror position via potentiometers located in the mirror housings.

3oth exterior door mirrors and the interi mirrorfeature an auto dmming function. The iteriorrear view mirro contains one oward and one reward facing light sensor.The light sensors control the uto dimming feature of the interior mirr to reduc glare from the headlights of following vehicles.

When auto-dimming of the interior mirror is required, a supply is provided by the interior mirro to both door miros t initiat he door mirror auto-dimming sequence.

Blind spot monitoring function alerts the driver to a vehicle located in the vehicle blind spot. A waming indicator is located in each exterior mirror towards the outer edge.
