The RCM i installed on the top of the transmission tunnel i line with the / pillars, and controls peration of the SR (supplemental restraint system). The main functions of theRCM include:

Crash detection and recording.   
Air bag and pretensioner firing.   
• Self test and system monitoring, with status indication via the air bag waming indicator and non volatile storage of fault information.

The RCM determines which elements of the SRS are to be deployed by using two internal areas:

Crash severity evaluation.   
Deployment handler.

Crash severity evaluation uses data from the RCM intemal accelerometer, the front crash sensor and the safety belt buckle itch. Basedon this data the RM deides which level of ir bag module deploment i required and forwards the iformato :o the second area, the deployment handler.

The deployment handler evaluates the status of the seat track position sensor and safety belt buckle sensors before a decisio s made about which restraints should finally be deployed.

Data from the side crash sensors is used by the RCM in conjunction with acleration data from the RCM intemal acceleromete to make a deployment decision. The RM processes the aceleration data and, subject to an impact being of high enough severity, decides whether the side air bag module and air curtain should be deployed.

nboard testing of the ir bag modules, front safety belt pretensioner iing circuits, waming indicator circuits and module tatus is performed by the RCM together with the storing of fault codes. The impact and pressure sensors perform basic

self-tests.

The RCM drives the air bag waming indicator via a high speed CAN signal. If the waming indicator fails, a fault code is recordedand a waming tne sunded placeohe dicato further aut ccurs.The  alo provides atempory back-up power supply to operate the air ba modules i the event that in crash coditions, the battery suppy is lost.n the event of a crash, it records certain data which can be accessed via the diagnostic connector.

A safing sensor in the RCM provides confimation of an impact to verify if air bag and pretensioner activation is necessary.A roll-over sensormonitors the lateral attude ofthe vehice.arious firing strateies are employed by the RM t esure that during an accident only the appropriate ir bags and pretensioners are fired. The firing strategy used also depends on the inputs from the safety belt buckle switches and the occupant monitoring system.

An energy resere i the RCM ensures there is always a minimum of150 mileconds of storedenergy vilable if the power suply from theiitionwitch i disupted during a crash. The stored energ iufiient to producefiing ignals forthe driver air bag, the passenger air bag and the safety belt pretensioners.

Whenthe ition iswitched ontheM perfos a selfest and then perfoms cylical moitoring of the system. f fault detected the RCM stores a related fault code and illuminates the ir bag waming idicator The faults can beretrieved by Jaguar approved diagnostic equipment over the CAN bus. If a fault that could cause a false fire signal is detected, the RCM disables the respective firing circuit, and keeps it disabled during a crash event.

The driver air bag is controlled by the RCM, which chooses between single or dual stage deployment, depending on the ccupant positio and the crash everity.To reduce the risk of an air ba inducednjury to driver who i positioned closet :he teering wheel, the 690 mm diameter air bag deploys radially. The volume of the driver air bag is 57 liters.

The driverirbaghas a non-zide propelant that reduces particulatesand effuents. It consists of atwo stageiflator with separate chambers for the two inflation stages, each being independently activated by the RCM. It has two electrical connectors that are color coded and mechanically keyed to the respective connector on the inflator.

The passenger air bag is controlled by the RCM, which chooses between single or dual stage deployment, depending on the occupant status and the crash severity. It consists of a two stage inflator with two air bag electrical connectors to accommodate the two stage inflation. The volume of the passenger air bag is 110 - 120 liters.

The heated gas iflator consists of a high-pressure mix of clean air and hydrogen gas, triggered by two separate ignition squibs. It produces a cotrolled geration of clean gas to apidly fil the i bag t i clasied as a stored fammable as (not as an explosive) and assuch, has less restrictivestorage and transportation requirements.t produces a very clean bum and almost no particulates and is almost free of any toxins, making disposal or recycling much easier.

The side air curtains have a capacity of approximately 2liters and arefited along both sides of the car They deploy from behind the headinerabove the doors, and are anchored at their front and rear extremities to maintain tension across the lower edge of the curtin. Their deployment area extend between the and pilltrims passing over the upper pillar trihe iflated portion ofthe urtin provieshead protection foutercupant i both the frot nd raro the ar nd a significant level of protection against objects such as poles and trees.

Theside ir curtains have a rapid fil time of lessthan25 ms and when fullyiflated, are pproximately 150mm thick.The curtains are itemall divided into separate chambers and, when an area of the inflated air bag i impated, gases transfer through internal vents to chambers further away from the impact, absorbing energy.

The side air curtains use standard hybrid inflators, which inflate the curtains with gas produced from a combination of pyrotechnic charge and compressed gas.

A pretensioner is incorporated into each of the safety belt retractors.They are pyrotechnic devices that are controlled by the RM (restraints control module) in the SRS (supplement restraint system). When deployed both the safety belt retractor pretensioner and safety belt buckle pretensioner fire i cojunctio with each other and tighten the seatbelt during a collision to ensure the occupant's are securelý held in their seats.

NOTE: Prior MY1 NAS vehicles only, you wil find a pretensioner on the safety belt buckle and safety belt retractor on the driver's side only and a pretensioner on the safety buckle on passenger side.

Step 1:

Visual inspection, assess overall vehicle condition. Has damage travelled, distorting internal structural panels?

This is a visual check of the complete vehicle.

Possible indicators:

Panel misalignment   
Panel gaps no longer uniform   
Hinged panels catch on locks   
Exterior cosmetic panels show signs of stress distortion   
Customer describes unusual driving characteristics post incident

Ifstructural distortion is visible, vehice body aligment should be checked/orrected on a body repair jg, refer to category facility.

If no visual indications of damage transfer, go to Step 2.

Step 2:

If no visual signs indicate distortion to intemnal structural panels, but the customer is concered with unusual driving characteristics post incident, and there i no damage to the suspension.Vehicle body aligment should be checked using four-wheel alignment geometry equipment.

If structural distortion is identified refer to category A facility.

Step 3:

If there is no sign or concerm regarding vehicle body alignment, focus on the local area of damage.

Do any of the panels require replacement?

If no, go to Step 4.

If yes, are any of the panels secured with:

Bonding adhesive?   
Fixings?   
Weld?

If yes, refer to category A facility.

Step 4

Do any of the panels require welding i.e. ripped or torn aluminium panel?

If no, go to Step 5.

If yes, refer to category A facility.

Step 5

Can the damage be repaired by hand using serrated spoon, dolly, file and/or hot air?

If no, refer to category A facility.

The Fronius 2700 Alu Edition G Welder utilies a 100%digitally controlled power source, this producesfinal weld attributes of:

Smoothness Refinement Consistency Repeatability

The accuracy of the approved equipment enables the delivery of one droplet of wire per pulse. This enables welding of ncredibly thin parent material, i.e 0.6mm sheet can be welded using a 1.2mm filler wire.

The approved MIG welder uses Direct Current, (DC) and does not produce High Frequency, (HF), at start up, (initial arc)

The SRS contains components which are potentially hazardous to service personnel if not handled corectly. The following uidelines and precautions are intended to alert personnel to potential sources of danger and emphasise the importanceof ensuring the integrity of the SRS components installed to the vehicle.

Following seat belt pre-tensioner deployment, the seat belts can still be used as conventional seat belts but will need to

be replaced as soon as possible to make sure full SRS protection.

f the SRS components are to be replaced, the part number/bar code of the new unit must be recorded.

Never drop an SRS component. The airbag diagnostic control unit is a particularly shock sensitive device and must be handed with extreme care. Airag modules and seat belt pre-tensioners could deploy i subjected to a strong shock. Never wap your ams around an aiag module. f a module hasto be caried, hold it by the cover with the cover uppermost ánd the base away from your body.   
Never transport airbag modules or seat belt pre-tensioners in the passenger compartment of a vehicle. Always use the luggage compartment of the vehicle for carrying airbag modules and seat belt pre-tensioner units.   
Neverattach anything to an airag cover or any trim component covering an airbag module. Do not allow anything to rest on top of an airbag module.   
Always keep components cool, dry and free from contamination.   
Never apply grease or cleaning solvents to seat belt pre-tensioner units, component failure could result.   
Always store an airbag module with the deployment side uppermost. If it is stored deployment side down, accidental deployment will propel the airbag module with sufficient force to cause serious injury.

Only use deployment equipment approved for the intended purpose. Deployment of airbag / pre-tensioner modules must be performed in a welventilated area which has been designated for the purpose. Make sure airbag / pre-tensioner modules are not damaged or ruptured before attempting to deploy. Where local legisation exists, notify the relevant authorities of intention to deploy irbag and pretensioner units. When deploying airbag pre-tensioner units, make sure that al personnel are at least 15 metres (45 feet) away from the deployment zone. Make sure deployment tool is connected correctly, in compliance with the instructions detailed in the SRS section of this manual In paricular make sure deloyment tool is Not connected to battery supply before connecting to irag module connector. When deploying seat belt pre-tensioners, make sure pre-tensioner unit is secured correctly to the seat. When removing deployed airbag modules and pre-tensioner units, wear protective clothing. Use gloves and seal deployed units in a plastic bag. Folwing deployment of any component of the SRS system within the veicle, allS components must be replaced. o not reuse  aaeany ar o the sem.   
Do not lean over an airbag module when connecting deployment equipment.

### Additionally, the following items must be inspected for damage and replaced as n


The replacement and inspection policy is dependent on the type and severity of the crash condition. The following guideline are the minimum that should be exercised as a result of the deployment of specific SRS components.

Check for structural damage in the area of impact paying particular attention to bumper armatures, longitudinals anc bracery.

CAuTION: If the front airbags are deployed, the following components must be replaced:

Driver airbag module   
Passenger airbag module Fly leads (where applicable) connecting front airbag modules to SRS harness Front seat belt buckle pre-tensioner Rear seat belt pre-tensioners - if installed Driver's seat belt retractor - if installed   
Rotary coupler   
Any front impact sensors that have been physically damaged or if a fault is being registered   
Restraints control module (RCM) if the three crashes/impacts have been stored

Front passenger's seat belt retractor and webbing, tongue latching function, 'D' loop and body anchorage point   
Rear seat belt buckles, webbing, buckle covers, body anchorage points and tongue latching function   
Fascia moulding adjacent to passenger airbag module   
Steering wheel   
Front seat frames and head restraints   
Steering column - if adjustment is lost or if there are signs of collapse   
Seat beit height adjusters

Rear seat belts

CAUTIoN: If the side (thorax) air bags are deployed, the following components must be replaced on the side of the ehicle on which the deployment occurred:

Side (thorax) airbag Any side impact sensors that have been physically damaged or if a fault is being registered Restraints Control Module (RCM) if the three crashes/impacts have been stored

cAutioN: If the head airbag modules are deployed, the following components must be replaced on the side of the vehicle on which the deployment occurred:

Head airbag modules   
Link lead between airbag gas generator and restraints control module (RCM) harness   
Airbag retaining clips   
Internal trim finisher   
Front seat belt buckle pre-tensioners   
Any side impact sensors that have been physically damaged or if a fault is being registered   
Restraints Control Module (RCM) if the three crashes/impacts have been stored

dditionally, the following items must be inspected for damage and replaced as necessary:

Headlining   
Component mounting brackets   
Front seat belts, retractors and webbing, tongue latching function, 'D' loop and body anchorage points   
Rear seat belt buckles, webbing, buckle covers, tongue latching function, and body anchorage points   
•Adjacent trim components   
Seat belt height adjusters

CAUTIoN: If the seat belt pre-tensioners are deployed during a rea impact, the following components must be replaced

Seat belt pre-tensioners Front and rear seat belt retractors used during the impact Restraints Control Module (RCM) if the three crashes/impacts have been stored

Various options are available for the front seats with regard to temperature control and electrical adjustment. Seats are non-heated, heated or heated and cooled (climate), with the following adjustment options:

10-way adjustment on the driver seat and 8-way adjustment on the passenger seat.   
16-way adjustment on the driver seat and 12-way adjustment on the passenger seat.   
18-way adjustment on the driver and passenger seats.

8-way adjustments consist of seat lide, seat height, squab recline and 2-way lumbar adjustment. 10-way adjustment adds cushiontilt.12-way adjustment adds head restraint.16-way adjustment add cushion extension and replaces 2-way lumr adjustment with 4-way. 18-way adjustment adds squab bolster adjustment. The controls for seat adjustment are installed in the outboard side shield of the related seat cushion.

The driver seat on all options has a -channel memory for easy recallof stored position settigs for the seat, steering column an doo mirors.Passengr seat ith 1-way ustment al have channel memory. The controfor memory peratin are in the related front door casing. Lumbar and squab bolster setings are not included in the memory function.

Some climate seats with 18-way adjustment also incorporat a massage function. The massage function is produced using itia umarcls.peratin othe massaefunctin s controllefome Climate/ Front ClimateFrot Seat men the TSD (touch screen display).

Operation of the temperature settings for heated and climate seats is controlle from the Climate / Front Climate / Front Seat menu of the TSD.

Both front seats incorporate an AWs (anti-whiplash system) consisting of active, energy absorbent backrest mechanisms. Together with corectly positioned headests, the Aw helps reduce the liliood of neck and spinal injury in the event of rer impact. In a low speed rear impact, Aw automatical moves and reclines the backrest by a smallamount, to change the posture of the seat occupant and reduce the relative front to rear motion between body and head.

A map pocket i installed on the rear of each front seat squa.Depending on trim level, some vehices also have a folding tr attached to the rear of the squabs.

The following options are available for the two outer rear seats with regard to temperature control:

Non-heated seats.   
Heated seats.   
Climate seats.

peration of the temperature settings for heated and climate seats is controlled from the rear climate control panel and th Climate / Rear Climate / Rear Seats menu of the TSD.

Stall Detection

A seat adjustment motor is deemed to have stalled if there i no change i the input from the feedback sensorof the moto for 200 ms. f a stallcondition is detected then the drive to that motor is cancelld for the remainder of the memory recall operation or until the witch is re-selected (manual movement).The motor may be activated again, to move past the stall position, by pressing the appropriate switch for more than  seonds. If sensor eack is detected, then the motor will continue t be driven until the witch is relased. If sensor feack is not detected, then the moto i only driven for 0.5 second and then stops until the witch is released and pressed again, when a further .5 second of activation is permitted. This is known as inch mode, which allows seat adjustment to be maintained if sensor feedback is lost.

When a replacement seat module i fitted it should be calibrated using Jaguar approved diagnostic equipment so that the module can learn the positions of the adjustment motors.

Battery Monitor

If the battery voltage drops below 10.5, then the driver seat module ignores all requests for a memory recall until the battery voltage has reached 11. . This willconserve as much power in the vehicle battery as possible to enable engine cranninng.

Seat massage requests from the START / STOP buttons on the TSD are sent via the medium speed CAN bus to the appropriat seat module. The seat module processes the requests and transmits them to the master massage solenoid on the LiN bus

connection.

When a START button is pressed, the master massage solenoid operates the relevant master and slave solenoid valves and activates the pump. The massage function operates in 10 minute cycles. After a 10 minute cycle i complete the user must re-select the function if a further 10 minute cycle is required.

When a STOP button is pressed, the 10 minute cycle is completed, or the ignition is switched off the solenoid valves are opened to deflate the massage 'cells and the air pump turned off.

During operation the bottom cell pairinflate and then deflate.As the first cellpair are deflating the second cell pairstart t inflat. Thissequence is rpeated for allive cell pairs, from cell pair one at the bttom to cell pairfive at the top. ell inflation time, which varies between cell pairs, is as follows:

Cell pair one - 3 seconds.   
Cell pair two - 2.6 seconds.   
Cell pair three - 2.8 seconds.   
Cell pair four - 2.2 seconds.   
Cell pair five - 1.6 seconds.

Electric motors are used to provide adjustment of seat slide, seat height,squab recline and, where fitted, cushion tilt, head restraint and cushion extension. Anair pump and flatale cushions are used to provide ajustment of the lumbarsupport nd the squab bolster supports (where fitted).

Allf the seat adjustments are controlled from the seat witch pack on the outside of the seat cushion. On non memory seats, the control switches are connected directly to the adjustment motors. On memory seats, the switches are connected to the adjustment motors via a seat control module. Memory seats also have a memory switch pack in the related door panel.

ach adjustment motor contains a Hall position sensor.The sensors provide position feedback signals which, on seats with a nemory function, are used for memory store and recall operation.

he seat slide motor is an integral component of the cushion frame. The motor drives a gear on a wom drive lead screw, whi s integral with the floor rail. The lead screw has a stop at each end to limit the fore and aft seat movement.

The seat height motor is located below the seat. The motor drives a gear on a lead screw. The lead screw moves a lever mechanism, which raises or lowers the seat cushion.

The squab recline motor is located in the squab frame.The recline motor rotates a shaft connected to the squab frame, whic changes the angle of the squab.

The tilt motor is loated below the seat. The tilt motor drives a gear on a lead screw to raise the front of the seat cushion.

he head restraint motor is located in the upper section of the squab frame and is accessible by removal of the seat back. notor moves a cradle by a rack and pinion arrangement. The crade has two head restraint stems, which raise and lower the iead restraint as the motor moves the cradle.

he cushion extend motor is located below the seat. The motor drives a gear on a lead screw, which extends or retracts th iront of the seat cushion.

Lumbar adjustment is provided by a lumbarsupport and air pump installed i the squab.The lumbar support consists of n le shi ih ithei-marppordcel-mpor) endg vehicle specification. On vehicles with massage seats, the dual cellumbar support is operated by the ir pump of the massage system.

Squab bolster adjustment is provided by inflatable cushions on the inside faces of the squab bolsters. The iflatable cushions are operatedsimultaeously by a solenoid valve block and the ir pump of the lumbar support or the massae seat system.On vehicles with massage seats, the squab bolster solenoid valves are incorporated into the valve block containing the slave massage solenoid valves.

Squab and Lumbar Support

![](images/_MISSING_5af1c0d5afd27205faecc37a64a7fa02c97b425cad24972958830946cfe7e945.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_80e8f8c619af00f01def2561f763d0fc334ac49881ce3a2deb9072b0ed7515d5.jpg)

Where fitted, the massage ystem in eac seat consistsof an air pump, air cel pads masterand slave solenoid alve blocks. The air pump i also used for adjustment of the lumbar and squab bolster supports.The slave solenoid block also incorporates the solenoid valves used to control the squab bolster supports.

Operation of the massage system is controlled with START and STOP buttons on the climate menu of the TSD and is independent of the lumbar ánd squab bolster adjustments.

### Principles of Operation


![](images/_MISSING_2a7eaff70cdff8370fb5b30562d1f5b8fb1a086ebe9dde6c1c7d99f3ff912aec.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_61b84e9cf0f70bb62f1cbc8008c7e8dce6d1f3cc05d01ab30b42ce4d5987109d.jpg)

The ir pump is located undemeath the seat at the rear of the squab. The pump is housed inside a NH (noise, vibration and harshness) casing to cut down the pump operation sound level. Operation of the air pump is controlled by the master soleno valve block.

The maximum pump pressure is controlled by a pressure relief valve in the lumbar solenoid valve block.The maximum pressur range is 310.5 to 379.5 mbar (4.5 to 5.5 Ibf/in2.).

A thermal protection device in the air pump stops pump operation if the temperature increases to 72±4 (1627 .The pump will not re-start until 10 minutes after the temperature decreases below the cut-off temperature.

Heated seat incorporate heaterelements in the cushion and the squab of the seat. Power to the heaterelements of the front seats i cotrolled by two seat heatermodules attached to a bracket on the cabin floor, under the carpet at the front left corner of the LH front seat. Power to the heater elements of the two outside rear seats is controlled by two seat heater modules attached to a bracket on the back of the rear seat squab.

Each cushion heater element has a thermal sensor, which suppies a fedback temperature signal to the related seat heater module. The squa heaterelements do not have a thermal sensor, and are regulated at the same temperature as the cushion heater elements.

The bloweris also controlled by the climateseat control module.

jeat heating and coling for the front and rear seats can be selected on the climate menu of the TSD. Seat heating and cooling for the rearseats ca also be sleted on the rearcimate contol panel. In the event of suspected climate seat faults use the pinpoint tests detailed below

First, check the integrity of the three seat climate control module harness connectors:

Disconnect each connector   
Inspect each connector for cracks and breaks, replace as required   
Check the integrity of connector terminals for bent terminals, backed-out or badly crimped wires. Rectify as required   
Reconnect all connectors and retest. If seat climate functions are still faulty, note any DTCs that have been logged by the seat climate control module(s) and refer to the table and pinpoint tests below:

Red - safety belt status changed from fastened to unfastened.

Diagnosis:

Ingress of water into side luggage compartment area Cause: - The forced air extraction for the vehicle interior is located in the quarter panel lower extension. - The rubber flap of the forced air extraction must be able to move freely.

- Remove the forced air extraction.   
- Check the seal area between the bodywork and housing, as well as the rubber flap.   
- Install a new seal if necessary.


### Connecting a Slave Battery Using Jump Leads


For electrical systems, pinpoint test steps are used to identify the source of a concem in a logical, step-by-step manner.   
Pinpoint tests have two columns: CONDITIONS and DETAILS/RESULTS/ACTIONS.

The CONDITIONS column is used exclusively for graphics and icons (with or without captions) and the DETAILS/RESULT /ACTIoNs column provides direction to another test step or specific corrective actions.

The boxed numbers indicate the order in which the described action is to be carried out.

WARNINGS:

TO AVOID ACCIDENTAL DEPLOYMENT AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY, THE BACKUP POWER SUPPLY MUST BE DEPLETED BEFORE REPAIRING OR REPLACING ANY AIR BAG SUPPLEMENTAL RESTRAINT SYSTEM (SRS) COMPONENTS. TO DEPLETE THE BACKUP POWER SUPPLY ENERGY, DISCONNECT THE BATTERY GROUND CABLE AND WAIT ONE MINUTE. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THIS INSTRUCTION MAY RESULT IN PERSONAL INJURY.

Do not use a multimeter to probe the restraints control module. It is possible for the power from the meter battery to trigger the activation of the airbags. Failure to follow this instruction may result in personal injury.

CAUTION; Diagnosis by substitution from a donor vehicle is NoT acceptable. Substitution of control modules does not guaranteeconimation of a fault, and may also cause additional faults i the vehicle being tested and/or the donor vehicle.

Ensure that electrical equipment is maintained in good condition and frequently tested. Faulty equipment should be labelle and preferably removed from the work station.

In cases of electrocution:

Switch off the power supply before approaching the victim

The ceramic sheathed element glow plugs are made froma heat-resistant, electrically conductive ceramic material. The ceramic sheathed-element glow plugs outer laer is heated directly and iself reulating.The selfregulation allows the resistance of the sheathed element to automaticall increase as the heat inreases preventing the glow plug from overeating. In addition, during the heating process and under the control of the glow plug relay, the gow plug can be operated above their nominal voltages.This permits heat-up speeds of 100C per second.The sheathed-element glow plugs reach a maximum glow eatre00domte10oa ietheists w times.

The glow plug is a tubular heating element that protrudesinto the combustion chamber of the engine.The heating element contains aspiral filment encased i magesium oxide powder. At the tip ofthe tubular heating element is the heater coil. Behind the heatercoil s a control coil The control coil  coected i series and reulatesthe heater coil to ensure that t does not overheat.

Each cylinder bank has a separate hamess connecting the three glow plugs. The hamess connects into the engine wiring haress and each harness has a connector block which attaches to each of the glow plugs for that bank.

The glow plg module recives a battery oltae feedvi a25A muse the  nda 100 midifusein the  engine junction box.Operatin of the gw plug modue is controlled by the , which also controls the illminatin of the glow plug indicator in'the instrument cluster.

The system has been designed as a lowvoltage glow system. At 7 volts, the nominal voltage of the sheathed-element glow i eratheoltte aleiaiheiwatehee to the sheated-lement gw plugand contro ther gw temperature preiselo the speiiequiement othe engie. This produces the optimum gow temperature even when the main circuit voltageis interupted during engine starting.The lower power cosmption of the cerami gw plug and theirtimestaggered activatio reduce t a miimum the peak load on the main circuit during the cold start and immediate post-start periods.

n the event of glow plug failure, the engine may be difficult to start and excessive smoke emissions may be oserved after starting.

The Mechatronic valve block is located in the bottom of the transmission and is covered by the fluid pan. The valve block houses the TM, electrical actuators, speed sensors and control valves which provide alelectro-hydraulic control for all transmission functions. The Mechatronic valve block comprises the following components:

TCM Pressure regulator solenoids   
Shift control solenoid   
Damper Hydraulic spool valves   
Sélector valve   
Temperature sensor   
Turbine speed sensor   
Output shaft speed sensor.

Diesel fuel is drwn from the tank by the intemal electric li pump.The fuel pressure regulator loated in the fuel pump module assembly regulates the delivery pressure at approimately .5 bar to the transfer pump housed in the High Pressure (HP) pump. A Volume Control Valve (VV) governs the amount of fuel supplied to the HP pump.

The transfer and high pressure pump are driven directly by the engine. Due to the storage volume of the common rail, the injection pressure will remain practically constant over thé complete duration of the injection process.

The HP pump has a returm pipe circuit which is separate from the injector retumn pipes.

This document defines the requirements for care and maintenance of battries, and the standard of battery care at dealers and retailers for new vehicles.

This applies to alltypes of 12 Volt Lead Acid Batteries used in Jaguar and Land Rover vehicles whether they are conventional flooded technology or Absorbed Glass Mat (AGM - also known as Valve Regulated Lead Acid (VRLA) technology and also applies t bt Primary, Sendary andAuxiliy Batteries.A attriesofferimproved eistance tcyclig asseeistp start applications.

n order to prevent damage to the battery and ensure a satisfactory service life, al processes detailed within this document nust be rigorously adhered to.

It is equally important therefore to note the following key points:

Allnew vehicles leave the factory with either a transit relay installed and/or have a transit mode programmed into the vehicle control modules.The transit relay must be removed and the transit mode disabled(where applicable) using an approved diagnostic system, NoT НПRу THAn 72 HouRs before the customer takes delivery.

ie battery can be discharged by the following mechanisms:

Self Discharge: - A lead acid battery will very slowly discharge itself due to its own intemal chemical processes whether it is connected to a vehicle or not.   
Quiescent Discharge: - The vehicle electrical systems when connected to the battery will draw charge from the battery

2 Volt Lead Acid Batteries rely on intemal chemical processes to create a voltage and deliver curent. These processes and :he intemal chemical structure of the battery can be damaged if the battery is allowed to discharge over a number of weeks nonths, or is left in a discharged state for a lengthy time period.

On vehicles with conventional ignition keys, these must not be left in the ignition lock barrel when the transit relay has been removed, otherwise quiescent current will increase and the battery will discharge more rapidly.   
For keyless vehicles, the Smart Key must be stored at least 5m (16 ft) away from the vehicle when the vehicle is parked or stored.   
•AGM Batteries are fully sealed and cannot have the electrolyte level topped up.

NOTE: Dealers and retailers involved in the storage /handing of vehicles and replacement batteries have a responsibility to ensure that only a fully charged battery may be processed through the distribution selling chain.

ehicles used as dealer demonstrator(s), in a showroom, must be connected to a JLR approved showroom conditioner capable of delivering 50 Amps. This will prevent'the battery from being damaged.

Due to the high electrical curent demand and high depth of dicharge that can occur during vehicle software reflash aivities orelaereeicad aeue a JLR approved power supply capable of delivering 50 Amps or more.

or any extended vehicle rework that results in consuming vehicle power, either the battery should be disconnected or a JR spproved power supply connected.

It is the dealer / retailers responsibility to make sure the battery is not allowed to discharge by following the instructions and processes defined in this manual.   
However, if cirumstances dictate that a new vehicle must be jump started due to a discharged battery whilst the veice in the dealer/ etailers care, the attery on this veicle must be replaced with a new one prior to delivery to the customer at the dealer / retailers liability.   
The vehicle should also undergo investigation as to why the battery became discharged.   
Do not conect the jump starting cable to the negativeterminal of the battery. Always connect to the reommended earth point. As defined in the owners handbook or service documentation for that vehicle.

WARNINGS:

BATTERY CELLS CONTAIN SULPHURIC ACID AND EXPLOSIVE MIXTURES OF HYDROGEN AND OXYGEN GASES. IT IS THEREFORE ESSENTIAL THAT THE FOLLOWING SAFETY PRECAUTIONS ARE OBSERVED.

Batteries emit highly explosive hydrogen at al times, particularly during charging.To prevent any potential form of gnition occurring when working in the vicinity of a battery:

Do not smoke when working near batteries.   
Avoid sparks, short circuits or other sources of ignition in the battery vicinity.   
Switch off current before making or breaking electrical connections.   
Ensure battery charging area is well ventilated.   
Ensure the charger is switched off when: a connecting to a battery; b disconnecting from the battery.   
•Always disconnect the ground cable from the battery terminal first and reconnect it last.

Batteries contain poisonous and highly corrosive acid. To prevent personal injury, or damage to clothing or the vehicle, teiacielectiiraiy carrying batteries:

Always wear suitable protective clothing (an apron or similar), safety glasses, a face mask and suitable gloves. If acid is spilled or splashed onto clothing or the body, it must be neutralized immediately and then rinsed with clean water. A solution of baking soda or household ammonia and water may be used as a neutralizer. In the event of contact with the skin, drench the affected area with water In the case of contact with the eyes, bathe the affected area with cool clean water for approximately 15 minutes and seek urgent medical attention. If battery acid is spilled or splashed on any urface of a vehicle, it should be neutralized and rinsed with clean wate. Heat is generated when acid is mixed with water If it becomes necessary to prepare electrolyte of a desired specific gravity, LowLY pour the concentrated acid into water (not water into acid), adding small amounts of acid while stimng.Allw the electrolyte to cool i noticable heat develops. With the ecption of lead or lead-lied containers, always use non-metallc receptacles or funnels. Do not store acid in excessively warm locations or in direct sunlight.

Due to their hazardous contents, the disposal of batteries is strictly controlled. When a battery is scrapped, ensure it is iooalycgit aeiomnaeat doutoaoa oi disposal facilities.

A selection of colored sleeves areavailable for maintaining the wiring hamess cable identification on the pre-teinated wiring hamess. Forexample, if the riginal wiringhamesscablecolor i pink with a black trace put the pink wiring hamess cable identifiation sleeve on the pre-terinated wiring hamessfirst followed by a black sleeve, and slide both along the wiring hamesscableto the electrical connector terminal.

The extraction hande, in cojution with the corct tip, is used to remove a terminal from anelectrical coector.Each tip is marked with an identifiation letter, A to K inclusive. Each tip has been specially designed to extract a particular type of electrical connector terminal. The use of any other tool is not recommended and is liable to cause damage to the lectrical connector. The tip is fastened to the handle by a screw which holds the tip firmly yet allows it to be easily replaced.

It must be noted that some electrical connector(s) have anti-backout devices which prevent the terminals from being removed from the electrical connector.Some examples of these are shown in following ilustrations.The anti-ackout device must be released before tmpting t remove the teminal from the electrical conector Some antiackout deviesequire aspei tip to release the device. Most can be released by carefully using a suitable small screwdriver.

Various types of electrical connector have seals installd intemally or extermallyto prevent moisture ingress.These nommally do not have to be removed but make sure that they are installed when the electrical connectors are connected.

The ilustrations show examples of each tip used on different types ofelectrical connectos There are a arge umberof different types oeletrical coecor usedon vehices therefore only one example using each tipis shownechnicians experience and judgement willdictate which type of tip should be ued for those electrical connctor(s) which are not shown. Care should be exercised to avoid further damage when removing the terminals from the electrical connector.

WARNINGS:

To avoid accidental deployment, the restraints control module backup power supply must be depleted. Wait at least one minute after disconnecting the battery ground cable(s) before commencing any repair or adjustment to the supplemental restraint system (SRS), or any component(s) adjacent to the SRS sensors. Failure to follow these instructions may result in persnal inury.

Prior to starting any weld procedure, the following safety precautions should always be implemented:

Disconnect the vehicle battery   
Disconnect the generator electrical connectors   
Remove any ECMs within 500mm of the weld area   
Remove the battery before carrying out welding work in its vicinity   
Utmost care must be taken when welding near the fuel tank or other components that contain fuel. If the tank filer neck or a fuel line must be detached to allow access for welding work, then the fuel tank must be drained and removed   
Adjacent vehicle parts and adjacent vehicles must be shielded against flying sparks and heat

It is essential that all tos and equipment are maintained in good condition and the correct safety equipment is used where required.

Never use tools orequipment for any purpose other than that for which they were designed. Never over- loadequipment such as hoists, jacks, axle and chassis stands or liftig slings. Damage caused by overloading is not always immediately apparent and may result in a fatal failure the next time that the equipment is used.

Do not use damaged or defective tools or equipment, particularly high speed equipment such as grinding whees. A damage grinding wheel can disintegrate without warning and cause serious injury.

Wear suitable eye protection when using grinding, chiselling or sand blasting equipment.

Wear a suitable breathing mask when using abrasive blasting equipment, working with asbestos-based materials or using spraying equipment.

Ensure adequate ventilation to control dusts, mists and fumes.

The following safety precautions must be observed when raising the vehicle to carry out service operations:

Never rely on a jack alone to support a vehicle. Always use suitable vehicle stands to provide rigid support.   
When working beneath a vehicle, whenever possble use a vehicle hoist instead of a jack and vehicle stands.   
Make sure that the vehicle is standing on firm, level ground before using a jack.   
Do not rely on the parking brake alone; chock the wheels and put the automatic transmission into Park if possible.   
Check that any lifting equipment used has adequate capacity for the load being lifted and i in corect working order.

Gear noise is typicall a howling or whining due to gear damage or incorect bearing preload It can occur at various speeds and driving conditions, or it can be continuous Chuckle is a particular ratting noise that sounds like a stick against the spokes of a spinning bicycle wheel. It occurs while decelerating from approximately 64 km/h (40 miles/h) and can usuall be heard allthe way to a stop. The frequency varies with vehicle speed Knock is very similar to chuckle, though it may be louder and occurs on accleration or deceleration. The tear down wil disclose what has to be corrected

check and rule out tires, exhaust and trim items before disassembling the transmission to diagnose and corect gear noise.

The noises described under Road Test usually have specific causes that can be diagnosed by observation as the unit is disassembled. The initial clues are the type of noise heard on the road test and the driving conditions.

The double wishbone type rear suspension is a full independent design assembled on a steel subframe. Large diameter bushes isolate the subframe from the vehicle's body.

Toe links, installed between the wheel knuckles and the subframe, are used to adjust the toe angle of the rear wheels.

The wheel knuckles are attached to the upper and lower control arms. A spring and damper assembly is located between ea lower control arm and the vehicle body.

The spring and damper assemblies incorporate air springs controlled by the air suspension system.

The cast aluminum upper control am locates to the subframe via one cross-axis joint and one plain rubber bush, and links to the wheel knuckle via an integral ball joint.

The aluminum lower arm locates to the subframe via one cross-axis joint and one plain rubber bush, and to the wheel knuckle via a second plain rubber bush.

he rear of the control arm has mounting points for the damper and the stabilizer link.

### Principles of Operation


Tire pressure sensors are not fitted to the space saver spare wheel and therefore the spare wheel is not monitored.

The TMS uses active tire pressure sensors which are located o each wheel, inside the tire caity. The sensor ioorates the tire alve and iseured in the wheel by  nut on the outside of the wheel. The sensor contains  Printed Ciruit oard which houses a PTC (positive temperature coffient) sensor, a Piezo pressuresensor aradio reciver and trasmitter and a lithium battery.

The tire pressure sensors use the P sensor and the Piezo sensor to periodicall measure the pressure and temperature of the ir inside the tire. The data is transmitted by RF data signals at either 315 MHz or 433 Hz dependant on market requirements.

The RF transmission from the sensor contains a unique identification code  its transmission data. This allows the TPMS to ientify the wheel n the veice. the sensoirplaed o a whee he ew sensordentifiati willeeat tough the learn and location process.

Factory installed tires and wheels are designed to operate satisfactory when inflated to the recommended inflation pressures; refer to the Specifications sub-section. The recommended pressures apply to vehicle loads up to and including full-rated load capacity

Correct tire pressures and driving technique have an important influence on tire life. Heavy comering, excessively rapid acceleration' and unnecessary sharp braking increase tire wear

Replacement tires should follow the recommended:

size   
speed rating   
load range   
radial construction type

The use of any other size or type may seriously affect:

safety   
ride   
handling   
speedometer and odometer calibration   
vehicle ground clearance   
tire clearance between body and chassis   
wheel bearing life   
brake cooling

Wheels need to be renewed when:

impact damaged   
heavily corroded   
porous   
wheel stud holes or seats become damaged   
they have excessive radial or lateral runout

WARNINGS:

Do not mix different types of tires on the same vehicle. Handing may be seriously affected resulting in loss of control. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury.

When using winter tires, observe the direction of the sidewall moulded indicators; correct tire rotational direction is critical. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury.

A tire and wheel must always be correctly matched. Wider or narower tires than recommended could cause danger through sudden deflation. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury.

When using the temporary spare wheel, maximum speed must not exceed 80 km/h (50 mile/h). Drive with caution anc replace with the specified wheel and tire assembly as soon as possile. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury.

Traction control (if available) must not be engaged with a temporary spare wheel fitted. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury.

When changing a wheel, make sure that the vehicle cannot move. Always apply the parking brake and select the ransmission park position.Failureto follow these nstructions ay resut in personal injury.

Never run the engine with one wheel off the ground, for example, when changing the wheel. The whee resting on the ground may cause the vehicle to move.Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury.

Tighten the wheel nuts to specification. Too tight may cause damage, too loose may allow the wheel to become detached. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury.

Use only wheels and wheel nuts supplied by Jaguar. Aftemarket wheels or wheelnuts may not fit or function correctly and could cause injury or damage. Failure to follow these instructions may result in personal injury.

The speed at which the vibration occurs   
What type of vibration occurs in each speed range - 'Mechanical or audible   
How the vibration is affected by changes in the following: - Engine torque -Vehicle speed -Engine speed   
Type of vibration-sensitivity: torque sensitive, vehicle speed sensitive or engine speed sensitive

Any special tols and equipment required to perform a maintenance procedure, are shown at the beginning of each procedure.   
When possible, illustrations are given to assist in identifying the tool needed.

To prevent ingress of dirt, accumulations of loose dirt and greasy deposits should be removed before disconnecting or dismantling components or assemblies.

Components should be thoroughly cleaned before inspection prior to reassembly.

Cleaning Methods:

Dry Cleaning   
Removal of loose dirt with soft or wire brushes Scraping dirt off with a piece of metal or wood Wiping off with a rag

•Blowing dirt off with compressed air (Eye protection should be worm when using this method)   
Removalof dry dust using vacuum equipment. This method should alwaysbe used to remove friction lining materia dust (asbestos particles)   
Seam Cleaning

wARNING: Failure to comply may result in personal injury or damage to components.

Air Bags - Do's

Do store in an air bag safe when not installed to the vehicle.   
Do store modules in an upright position   
Do keep modules dry   
Do carry modules with the cover side pointing away from the body   
Do place modules with their cover side upwards   
Do carefully inspect modules for damage   
Do stand to one side when connecting modules   
Do make sure all test equipment is properly calibrated and maintained   
Do wash you hands aer handling deploye air ba   
Do wear safety glasses when carrying out repairs to the SRS or when handling an air bag module   
Only carry out' a system test with 'the air bag modules fully installed   
Do inspect the condition of the impact sensor mounting bracket and sensor flylead if the vehicle has been in an impact. Replace if damaged, even if there has been no deployment.

Air Bags - Do Nots

Do not store highly flammable material together with modules or gas generators Do not store gas generators at temperatures exceeding 80°

Do not store modules upside down   
• Do not attempt to open a gas generator housing   
Do not expose gas generators to open flame or sources of heat   
• Do not place anything on top of a module cover   
• Do not use damaged modules   
Do not handle a deployed device or gas generator for at least 20 minutes   
Do not probe air bag module electrical connectors or any other SRS component

Solders are a mixture of metals such that the melting point of the mixture is below that of the constituent metals (normall lead and tin). Solder application does not nomally give rise to toxic lead fumes, provided a gas/air flame is used. Oxy-acetylene flames should not be used, as they are much hotter and will cause lead fumes to be produced.

Some fumes may be produced by the application of any flame to surfaces coated with grease etc. and inhalation of these should be avoidéd.

Removal of excess soldershould be undertaken with care, to make sure that fine lead dust is not produced, which can give toxic effects if inhaled. Respiratory protection may be necessary.

Solder spillage and filings should be collected and removed promptly to prevent general air contamination by lead.

ligh standards of personal hygiene are necessary in order to avoid igestion of lead or inhalation of solder dust from clothing

rief exposure to high concentrations of vapors or mists will cause eye and throat iritation, dowsiness, dizziness headaches and, in the worst circumstances, unconsciousness.

In common with many other manufacturers' vehicles, some components installd to the Jaguar range have 'O' rings, seals or gaskets which contain a material known as 'Viton'.

Viton isflurlastomer, thatis a synthetic rubbertype which contains Fluorine. t iscommonly used for''rings, gasket and seals of alltypes. Although Viton is the most weli known fluoroelastomer, there are others, including Fluorel and Tecmoflon.

When used under design conditions fluoroelastomers are perfectly safe. f however, they are exposed to temperatures in excess of 400 C, the material will not burm, but willdecompose, and one of the products formed is hydrofluoric acid.

This acid is extremely corrosive and may be absorbed directly, through contact, into the body.

'O' rings, seals or gaskets which have been exposed to very high temperatures willappear charred or as a black sticky substance.

DO NOT, under any circumstances touch them or the attached components.

Equiriesshould be made to deterine whether Vito o ay the rlstmerhasbeenused ithefftedigeal oakeaoatauiiethereoaa dueindsme at the ala e Viton or any fluoroelastomer.

Viton or any other fluorolastomers have been used, the affeted area should be decontaminated before the commencement of work.

Disposable heavy duty plastic gloves should be wom at alltimes, and the affected area washed down using wire wool and a limewater (calcium hydroxide) olution to neutralize the acid before disposing of the decomposed Viton residue and final cleaning of the area.'After use, the plastic gloves should be discarded carefully and safely.

Description and Operation

Joise, vibration and harshness(NVH) is becoming more important as vehicles become more sophisticated and passenger :omfort levels increase. This section is designed to aid in the diagnosis, testing and repair of NVH concerns.

Noise is defined as sounds not associated with the operation of passenger compartment equipment that interface with customer satisfaction.   
Vibration is defined as impulses felt by the customer that are not caused by road surface changes.   
Harshness is a ride quality issue where the customer feels that the vehicle response to the road surface is sharply transmitted to the customer.

Diagnosis is more than just follwing a series of interlated steps in ordert find the solution to the speific condition. t s way of looking at systems that are not functioning the way they should and finding out why. Also itis knowing how the syster should work and whether it is working correctly.

here are basic rules for dianosis. If these rules are followed, the cause of the condition is usuall found the first time hrough the system.

Know how the parts go together.   
Know how the system operates as well as its limits and what happens when the system goes wrong.   
Sometimes this means checking the system against one that is known to be working correctly.

A clue in any one of these areas may save time:

•How old or new is the system?   
What kind of treatment has it had?   
Has it been repaired in the past in such a manner that might relate to the present condition?   
What is the repair history?

Did it start suddenly or appear gradually? Was it related to some other occurrence such as a collision or previous part renewal? Know how the condition made itself known; it may be an important clue to the cause.

Charts are a simple way of expressing the relationship between basic logic and a physical system of components. They help ioehe ecieameicar mi aariaiieiai

probability of certain things occurring in a system speed of checking certain components or functions before others simplicity of carrying out certain tests before others elimination of checking huge portions of a system by carrying out simple tests certainty of narrowing down the search to a'small portion'before carrying out in-depth testing The fastest way to find a condition is to work with the tools that are available. This means working with proven diagnostic charts and the correct special equipment for the system.

Make notes throughout the diagnosis routine. Make sure to write down even the smallest piece of information, because

it may turn out to be the most important.

Do not touch anything until a rad test and a thorough visual inspection of the vehicle have been caried out. Leave the tire pressures and vehicle load just where they were when the condition was first observed. Adjusting tire pressures, vehicle load or making other adjustments may reduce the conditions intensity to a point where it cannot be identified clearly. It may also inject something new into the system, preventing correct diagnosis.

Make a visual inspection as part of the preliminary diagnosis routine, writing down anything that does not look right Note tire pressures, but do not adjust them yet. Note leaking fluids, loose nuts and bolts, or bright spots where components may be rubbing against each other. Check the luggage compartment for unusual loads.

Road test the vehicle and define the condition by reproducing it several times during the road test.

Cary out the Road Test Quick Checks as soon as the condition is reproduced. This willidentify the correct diagnostic procedure. Cary out the Road Test Quick Checks more than once to verify they are providing a valid result. Remember, the Road Test Quick Checks may not tell where the concern is, but they will tell where it is not.

If a customer complains of a noise or vibration on a particular rad and only on a particular road, the source of the concem may be the road surface. If possible, try to test the vehicle on the same type of road.

The waring indications to the driver are common on al vehicles fitted with T. The driver is alerted to system wamings by a low tire pressure waring indicator in the instrument cluster and an applicable text message in the message centre.

he CB passes system status information to the instrument cluster on the medium speed CAN bus. The instrument cluster onverts this data into illumination of the warming indicator and the display of an appropriate message.

When the ignition is switched on, the warning indicator is illuminated for 3 seconds for a bulb check.

NOTE: If the vehicle is not fitted with the TPMS, the warning indicator will not illuminate.

The instrument cluster checks, within the  seond bulb check period, for a CAN bus message from theMs. During this time the TPMS performs internal tests and CAN bus initialization. The waring indicator will be extinguished if the  des not issue a fault message or tire pressure waring message.

a TS fault waring message is detected by the instrument cluster at ignition on, the waming indicator wil flash for 72 :econds after the 3 second bulb check period and then remain permanently illuminated.

fatre pressure waming message is detected by the instrument cluster at ignition on, the waring indicator wilextinguish oriefly after the 3 second bulb check period, before re-illuminating to indicate a tire pressure warning.

(A) Check Tire Pressure Warnings. A low tire pressure warning wil continuously illuminate the low tire pressure warning lamp. This warning may be accompanied by a text message such as CHECK TIRE PRESSURE (refer to owner literature). The manufacturer approved diagnostic system does NOT need to be used. Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs are not generated with this type of waming. To extinguish this waming it is essential that, with the ignition 'n' al vehicle tires including the spare are to be set to the correct pressure as stated in the vehicle handbook or as indicated on the placard label in the passenger/driver door aperture.

NOTES:

The tire pressures should be set by:

Using a calibrated tire pressure gauge   
With 'cold' tires (vehicle parked in the ambient temperature for at least one hour, not in a garage with an artificial ambient temperature)

f the tire pressure waring does not clear within two minutes, it is likely that the gauge is not correctly calibrated or the tires are 'warm'. Cary out the following steps until the warning has cleared:

Rotate wheels approximately 180 degrees   
Increase the tire pressures by 3psi   
Wait a further two minutes When the tires are at ambient temperature and a calibrated gauge is available, reset the tire pressures to the correct pressure.

Tire pressure adjustments are part of routine owner maintenance. Tire pressure adjustments that are required due to a lack of owner maintenance are not to be claimed under vehicle warranty.

(B) System Fault Warnings. When a system fault is detected, the low tire pressure warning lamp willflash for approximately 75 seconds prior to being continuously illuminated. Visually inspect wheel arch Tire Pressure Monitoring System Antennas and check for system DTs. Extemal visual damage to the tire low pressure sensors and air leks will not cause system fault warnings (note: nut and seal system should be replaced at each tyre change using the available service kit). Check for the presence of tire low pressure sensors on all four wheels (note: a tire low pressure sensor has a metal valve stem rather than a rubber one).

Check for Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) and refer to the DTC Index.

The pump consistof a shaft cotaining a umber of slots into which vanes are nserted and these vanes run within a cam ring ithepump body.The ctrne f the shaft s ot coentri ith thatof the bre othe odand thiscreatesthe eandig and contracting cavities that form the pumping action.

The vanes rotate witin the cam ring and are driven by the shaft As the vanes rotate, the cam ring causesthe space between the vanes to increase.This causes a depression between the vanes and fluid is drawn from the reservoir via the uction hose into the space between the vanes. As the shaft rotates, the inlet port is closed to the vanes which have drawn in fluid, trapping the fluid between the vanes. The cam ring causes the space between the vanes to reduce and consequentially compresses and pressurizes the hydrauli fluid traped between them. Further rotation of the shaft moves the vanes to the outet port As the vanes pass the port plate the pressuried fuid passes from the pump utlet port into the pressure hoseto the steering gear.

The aming in the pump body ca moveitin the alve body. y moving the cam ing  ipossleto vary the etricity of the shaft and the vanes in reltion to the cam ring.As the ecetricity is decreased the volume of hydraulifluid trapped between the vanes decreases, maintaining the flow in response to pump speed. This reduces the load required to tum the pump and therefor improves engine output and economy. This allows the flow rate to be matched to the system demands and increased flow rate is only required when the steering wheel is turned.

The pump has an itemal regulating valve which controls the ecentricity of the cam ring and therefore varies the flow rate according to demand. The reulating relief valve limits the maximum pressure supplied to the steering gear to 110 bar (1595 f in  4 bar (58f in2) and also limits the maximum flw to 8.5 /min (1.86 gl/min) ± 0.5 /min (0.1 gal/min) egardless of engine speed.'

The connecting rods are manufactured from sinterforged stee and have fracture-split bearing caps. The bearing caps are produced by fracturing the opposing sides of the conecting rod at the bearing horizntal centre-line. As wella being easier to manufacture, when reassembled the fractured surfaces interlock to form a strong seamless joint. The cylinder position is etched on adjoining sides of the joint to identify matching connecting rods and bering caps. The selective connecting rod bearings are lumium/tin split plain bearings. The conecting d bearing is 'sputtr coated', which is a manufacturing process that layers the bearing material to produce a higher load capacity for improved durability.

JOTE: The connecting rods are not selective.

The lightweight valve gear provides good economy and noise levels. Valve head diameters are 31 mm (1.220 in) for the exhaust and 35 mm (1.378 in) for the intake. All alves have 5 mm (0.197 in) diameter stems supported in sintered metal seats and guide insets. Colts, valve collars and spring seat locate single valve springs on both intake and exhaust valves. Valve stem seals are integrated into the spring seats.

The thermostat is closed at temperatures below approximately 82°C (179°F). When the coolant temperature reaches approximately 82 the thermostat starts to open and is fully open at approximately 96°(204n this condition the full flow of coont isdirected through the adiator The thermostat is exposed to 90% hot coolant from the engine on one side and 10% cold coolant retming from the radiator bottom hose on the other side. Hot coolant from the engine passesfrom the by-pass pipe through four sening holes in the flow valve into a tube surounding 90% of the thermostat ensitive area.Cold coolant returming from the engine, cooled by the radiator, conducts through 10% of the sensitive area.

n cold ambient temperatures, the engine temperature is raised by approximately 10° (50°F) to compensate for the heat loss if 10% exposure to the cold coolant returning from the bottom hose.

The by-pass flow valve is held closed by a light spring. It operates to further aid heater warm-up. When the main valve is closed and the engine speed is at ile, the coolant pump des not produce sufiient flow and pressure to open the valve. In this condition the valve prevents coolant circulating through the by-pass circuit and forces the coolant through the heater matrix only. This provides a higher flow of coolant through the heater matrix to improve passenger comfort in cold conditions. When the engine speeincreaes above idle, the coolant pump produces a greater flow and pressure than the heater circuit cantakehe pressure act nthe byassw ale andvercomeshe alvesring pressure opening the alve and miig the pressure in the heater circuit. The valve modulates to provide maximum coolnt flow through the heater core and yet allowing excess coolant to flow into the by-pass circuit to provide the engine's cooling needs at higherengine speeds.

A pressurized expansion tank system is used which continuously separates the air from the cooling system and replenishes the system through a hose connected between the expansion tank and the heater retum hose. A continuous vent into the expansion tank, through a hose connected to the engine's coolant outlet conector, prevents air locks from forming in the cooling system.

Service fill Coolant expansion during warm-up •Air separation during operation System pressurization by the filler cap

![](images/_MISSING_3236148c7a50278f47afea7c08e4e6947ea3ee598189f5f6098b2f13b75f88cd.jpg)

The HP pump is a2 piston radial plunger pump.The pump has the ability to produce a maximum pressure of 2000 bar (29007 Ibf/in2).'The housing is cast from iron, the flange is cast from aluminum.

The HP pump is driven from the cylinder bank exhaust camshaft via a toothed belt.The drive from the belt rotates a cam wiinthem ich eaeu iieac pumpigelemnt.proue andse too areeqreopum belt replacement to time the pump.

e highpressure pump comprises 2 high pressure pumping elements, a volume control valve, an intemal transfer pump and a uel temperature sensor.

The fuel idelivered to the itemal transfer pump vi the exteal fuel fiterandanlectrifuel pump which is located in the uel tank.

The volume control valve is mounted on the high-pressure pump, ad located i the feed port between the high pressure pum elements and the ntemal transfer pump. The volume control valve i a variable poition solenoid-operated valve thatis controlled by the .The vlume control valve detemines the amount of fuel that  delivered from the intemal trnsfer pump to the P pumping elements. When there i no signal to the vlume control valve, the valveis closed and there isno fuel delivery.

The fuel from the intemal transfer pump is passed to the HP pumping elements at a constant pressure known as transfer pressure.The transfer pressure is controlled by an ntemal pressure relief valve.Once the fuel enters each of the HP pump elements the pressure rises rapidy, with each element providing a P suppy to one of the fuel ils.The high pressureis controlled by the high pressure regulator valve and the fuel rail pressure sensor.

A controlledamount of fuel is allowed to leak-ofrom the intemal transfer pump. This fuel is delivered to the pump intemal components to provide cooling and lubrication and is passed back the fuel filter via the LP feed line.

The pressure cotrol alve i loated ione ofthe fuel il.The fuel pressure is monited by a pressure sensor located in the other fuel ail.The EM controls the pressure control valve using the recived signals from the pressure sensor Reducing the pressure  thefuel ail via the pressure control alveresult fuel ting fom the fuel ails to the fuel et  the fuel filter.

The fuel temperature sensor is locatedon the rearof theP pump. It measures the fuel temperature in the low-pressuresid ofthe pump. The  coiall monitors this sigal to deteine the fuel tmperature t prevent ereatig of thefu system. The EM will also make fine adjustments to fuel injection quantity to adjust for fuel temperature.

![](images/_MISSING_04008aadae05993848ade45d75c32fec6bc662cccfaeef8f405a490bb5e47644.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_155b5873dc9bf21498f455b80c448e12bcf7062b9ed20106373f8edb8dbe79bb.jpg)
he fuel ails are steel fabrications and are similar in their construction. wo fuel rails are used with each rail supplying high ressure fuel to 3 fuel injectors.

Each rail has 5 threaded connections which provide for the attahment of the high pressure fuel supply from the HP pump, th balance pipe and connections for the 3 injectors supplied with fuel from that rail.

The fuel pressure in the rails is detected by a fuel pressure sensor which is located in the end of the RH rail.The LH rail houses a pressure control valve. The ECM controls the pressure control valve using signals from the pressure sensor.

The fuel rail pressure sensor i a piezo-resistive type sensor containing an actuating daphragm. Deflection of the diaphragm provides a proportional signal (output) voltage to the ECM, dependant on the fuel pressure within the fuel rail.

Both rails are connected together with a balance pipe which ensures the pressure in both rail is equal, even though each ril is supplied from a different pumping element in the HP pump.

ix fuel injectors are used in the fuel system. Apiezo actuator in each injector is electronicall controlled by the ECMt operate the injector in response to engine speed and load conditions.

Each injector has an electrical conector which connects the injectorto the engine hamess. A fuel coection on the top of the injector providesfor the high pressure fuel inlet rom the pump. A seond fuel conectio allws fuel akage within the injector to return to the HP pump.

The injector can operate up to 5 times during one combustion cycle depending on engine speed and load. The injection sequence can occur as follows:

![](images/_MISSING_646361031903c4b500eecf39a1aedf0307b7ccdbc8e2ee7979ce0f7f29ffcff6.jpg)

E107577

1. Pilot injection - occurs before the main injection and improves fuel and air mixing   
2. Pre-injection- shortens the main injection's ignition delay and therefore reduces the generation of nitrous oxides 3. Main injection - delivers the required engine torque   
After injection - occurs after the Main injection and assists the re-burm of any remaining particulate matter 5. Post injection - helps manage the temperature of the exhaust gas for more effective exhaust-gas after-treatment Injection delay 0.4 ms.

Each injectori calirated to the EM andapplicble the ylinder to which it i fitted.Therefore, if an injecto removed it must be refitted to the linder from which it was removed. If a new ijector is fitted, a caliration rutine using a Jaguar approved diagnostic system must be performed to calibrate the injector unique code to the ECM.

The perating voltage of the injector is between 110 and 163 volts depending on engine speed and load and care must be :akenwhen orking  the viinity of the jectors.The voltag icrasesinaly from 200 to 2000 bar (2900  2900in

Each injector has an electrical resistance value of between 150 - 250 kOhms.

The by-pass valve is a vacuum operated valve which directs the flow of exhaust gasses either through the EGr cooler or by-passes the cooler and directs the gasses directly to the intake manifold.

A vacuum actuator is located on a bracket attached to each EGR cooler The actuator receives a vacum which is produced by eam leaeaeeiehe amaacoteass aeieya housing by a connecting rod.

The vacuum supply to the actuator is controlled by the ECM (engine control module). When by-pass control is required, the ECM energizes a vacuum solenoid valve which applies vacuum to the vacuum actuators. The vacuum causes the actuators to move the connecting rods in a linear direction. The linear movement of the rod is transferred to rotary movement of the by-pass valve within the by-pass housing.

By-Pass Valve Closed

![](images/_MISSING_2d41a94dddb342d8ffa289e9982dc25ddae39ac622252ab46b89268f8eb2fbd7.jpg)

E112407

When the by-pass valve is closed, exhaust gasses are directed through the cooler before being passed to the intake manifold. By-Pass Valve Open

![](images/_MISSING_df5be339c7685959a4a443e85fa930f718ed3b623c2f34851c042a06d14731bf.jpg)

E112408

When the by-pass valve is open, exhaust gasses are passed directly through the by-pass housing into the intake manifold with no cooling applied to the gases.

The EGR valve motor is located on the by-passhousing. A 5 pin connector provides the power, ground and ECM signal and feedback connections for the motor.

The motor is secured to the by-pass housing with 4 tor screws. A pinion gear on the motor spindle drives a geared rack which

www.JagDocs.com

is connected to the EGR valve in the by-pass housing.

The motor is controlled by the ECM which provides power supply to operate the motor as required. A 5 Volt fedback signal is passed to the ECM which is used to establish motor position for precise control.

The EGR valve motors each receive a 12 volt supply and ground from the ECM.

The 12 volt power upply from the EM operates the GR valve motor. Threefurther wires connect the EGR valve to the ECMa 5 volt reference voltage, a ground and a position signal feedback.

The valve is used to direct a calculated proportion of exhaust gas back into the combustion chamber.

Ifa vehiclerequires recovery/transportation, the emergency park release mechanism is used to manul disengage the park lock and engage the transmission in neutral.

The emergency park release mechanism consists of an operating lever that is connected to a park interlock lever on the :ransmission by an upper and lower cable assembly.

eperating lever installenthefooconsoleundertrim panelthe ubby ox.The park teck leversattached t :he transmision selector shaft.

ne end of the perating leveris attached to a base by a hinge pin. A locking cylinderi installed in the other end of the perating lever to secure the perating lever to the aseThe peratng lever is raised by puling on astra.

When operated, the emergency park release mechanism turns the transmission selector shaft.

To disengage the park lock:

Open the cubby box lid.   
Remove the trim panel from left side of the cubby box.   
Rotate the locking cylinder of the emergency park release lever 90 degrees counterclockwise.   
Apply the footbrake, pull the operating lever upwards and ensure it locks in the vertical position.

aising the operating lever causes the emergency park release cable to rotate the park interlock lever on the transmission, hich disengages the parking pawl and engages neutral. This allows the vehicle to freewheel.

To re-engage the park lock:

Hold the strap on the operating lever, release the latch and lower the operating lever to the horizontal position.

Lock the operating lever by turning the locking cylinder 90 degrees clockwise.   
Install the trim panel.   
Close the cubby box lid.

Two processes are used to regenerate the DPF; passive and active.

The DPF requires constant monitoring to ensure that it is operating at it optimum efficiency and does not become blocked. The EM contains DPF software which controls the moitorig and operation of the DPF system and also monitors other vehi data to determine regeneration periods and service intervals.

The DPF software can be divided into three separate control software modules; a DPF supervisor module, a DPF fuel management module and a DPF air management module.

These three modules are controlled by a fourth software module known as the DPF co-ordinator module. The co-ordinator module manages the operation of the other modules when an active regeneration is requested.

The DPF fuel management module controls the following functions:

Timing and quantity of the four split injections per stroke (pilot, main and two post injections).   
Injection pressure ánd the transition between the three different calibration levels of injection.

The above functions are dependant on the condition of the catalytic converter and the DPF.

The controlled ijection dtemines the required ijection level in aitiont measuring the activity of the catalyti coverte and the Dp. The fuel management calculates the quantity and timing for the four split ijections, for each of the three calibration levels for injection pressure, and also manages the transition between the levels.

The two post jections are equiredto separate the fuctioality of increasing in-clinder gastemperatures and the productio ofhydrocarons.The first post injection is used to generate the higher in-clinder gas temperature while simultaneously retaining the same engine torque output produced during normal (non-regeneration) engine operation. The second post injection is used to generate hydrocarbons by allwing unbumt fuel into the catalytic converter without producing increased eñgine torque.

The following section details some side effects caused by the active regeneration process.

During the active regeneration process of the DPF, there will be an increase in fuel consumption.

However, because active regeneration occurs infrequently, the overalleffect on fuel consumption is approximately 2%. The aditional fuel used during the active regeeration processis accounted for in the instantaneous and average fuel cosumption displays in the instrument cluster.

Recent years have seen the introduction of 'DPF cleaning fluids' to (non JLR approved aftemarket sales. These products claim to reduce the temperature that the soot reaction takes place. It should be stressed that, during the vehicle development activity, every effort is made to generate DPF regeneration temperatures whilst maintaining safe levels for allother vehicle components. Unauthorized use of the aftermarket fluids produces a significant risk to soot bum rates and DPF peak temperatures real world driving conditions. These fluids are not authorised for JLR use.

CAUTIONS:

The regeneration procedure produces high temperatures in the diesel particulate filter. Heat can be felt radiating from beneath the vehicle, which is normal and not a cause for concem, However the vehice should not be parked overcombustible material, particularly during dry weather. The heat generated could be suficient to start a fire when in close proximity to combustible material such as long dry grass, paper etc

At alltimes during this procedure you should observe all relevant speed limits, laws, and regulations

The ideal speed and conditions for regeneration are 100 km/h (62 mph )  120 km/h (75 mph), in Drive. Keeping a constant speed enables the diesel particulte filter to regenerate more eficintly. It is therefore reommended that ruise control is used to achieve this, if possible

When driving off-road during the regeneration process, greater accelerator pedal use may be required

Drive the vehicle until the engine reaches normal operating temperature. The engine should Not be left idling to achieve working temperature   
Drive the vehicle for a further twenty minutes, keeping the vehicle at a constant speed between 75 km/h (45 mph) and 120 km/h (75 mph)   
If regeneration is successful the waming message wil be extinguished, once the messae is extinguished please keep driving for 10 minutes to ensure that the diesel particulate filter is completely clean

The fuel filter is a disposable canister type.

To prevent diesel waxing in cold conditions and to aid warm-up, a temperature sensitive regulating valve incorporated in the fuel filter housing, diverts a portion of the warm fuel returning from the engine into the fuel filter.

The regulating valve commences closing at 30°  (86° F and fully closes at 50°  (122° F When the valve is closed the retuming fuel is diverted to the fuel filter via the under vehicle fuel cooler to maintain an optimum fuel temperature.

The filter has an air bleed retumn to the fuel tank which returns excess air and fuel to the tank.
