The A/C compressor circulates refrigerant around the system by compressing low pressure, low temperature vapor from the evaporator and discharging the resültant high pressure, high témperature vapor to the condenser.

he A/C compressor is a variable displacement unit driven by the engine accessory drive belt.

•Up to 2013 MY: petrol vehicles, the A/C compressor is driven directly from the pulley.   
2013 MY Onwards: petrol vehicles, the A/C compressor is driven via an electro-magnetic clutch.   
On 3.ol diesel vehicles theA/ compressor is driven via an electro-magnetic clutch.

While the ignition is on, the clutch is permanently engaged by a power feed from the ignition relay in the EJB protect the system from excessive pressure, a pressure rlief valve is installed in the outlet side of the  compressor.The ressure relief valve vents excess pressure into the engine compartment.

The solenoid valve enables the flow of refrigerant through the A/C compressor to be adjusted to match the cooling load. Operation of the solenoid valve is controlled by the ATC module using a hardwired drive current of diffring values. By controlling the flow of refrigerant through the compressor, the solenoid valve controls the A/ system pressure and the evaporator operating temprature.

![](images/_MISSING_2e2bf53bd3d6f8e6699157bbe570c5ecb2077f6f094fb4d06b0bde92f2fc4c29.jpg)

E127738   
![](images/_MISSING_540861de09f860fa7513e23fec044383a7fbcb62d6f688ee332dea2c96a80cb0.jpg)
The condenser transfers heat from the refrigerant to the surounding air to convert the high pressure vapor from the compresoitiqudThe cesestallemedtlifontthedatooracket oachndtakatah the condenser to the end tanks of the radiator.

The condenser is classfied as a sub-cooling condenser and consists of a fin and tube heat exchanger core installed betweer two end tanks. Divisions in the end tanks separate the heat exchangerinto a four pass upper(condenser) section and atw pass lower (sub-cooler) section.

The LH end tank provides the connections to the high pressure line from the A/ compressor and the high pressure liquid lin to the evaporator.

The RH end tank provides the connections to the receiver drier.

The receiver drieris connected to the RH end tank of the condenser It removes solid impurities and moisture from the refrigeant and provieseseo liquid efeant t accmoate changs oheat a at theeratheeve drier is part of the condenser assembly and is not serviceable separately.

The refrigerant lines consist of a combination of rigid pipes and flexible hoses that connect the thermostatic expansion valve on the evaporator to the A compressor and the condenser. To maintain similar flow velocities around the A/ system, the diameter of the refrigerant lines varies to suit the two pressure/temperature regimes. Larger diameter pipes are installed in the low pressure/temperature regime and smallr diameter pipes are installed in the high pressure/temperature regime.

Low and high pressure servicing connections are incorporated into the refrigerant lines for system servicing.

When the system is in the automati mode, the ATC module determines the blower speed required from a comfort algorithm. When the system is in the anual mode, the AT module perates the blower at the speed selected using the rotary control switch on the .The AT module also djust blower speed to compensate for theam effect n inet air produced by forwar movement of the vehicle. As vehicle speed and ram effect increases, blower motor speed is reduced, and vice versa.

On vehicles fitted with the four zone system, the system cannot be tured on using the rotary blower control on the rear limate control panel. This is to encourage the use of the AUTO mode. Provided th rear climate control panel is unlocked, pressing a rear AUTO button on the rear climate control panel will reactivate the system if previously off.

The ATC module transmits refrigerant pressure and A/ compressor current values to the ECM over the medium speed then high speed CAN bus, using the  as a gateway.The M uses these lues to calulate the torque being ued to drive theA compressor.The M compares the calculated vale with i llwable value and, i necessary, forcestheAT module to iiit the  compressor by transmitting the AClutchhiitCAN messageThis forces the AT module to reduce the rive curent to the A/ compressor solenoid valve, which reduces refrigerant flow. This i turm reduces the torque required to drive theA/ compressor.

By reducing the maximum A/ compressor torque, the ECM is able to reduce the load on the engine when it needs to maintain vehicle performance or cooling system integrity.

The programmed defrost DEF switch is located on the IP. When the switch is pressed, the ATC module instigates the orogrammed defrost function. When selected, the ATC module configures the system as follows:

•Automatic mode off.   
A/Con.   
Selected temperature unchanged.   
Air inlet set to fresh air.   
•Air distribution set to windshield.   
Blower speed set to level 6.

he ATC module also sends a medium speed CAN message to the B to activate the windshield heater where fitted and rea vindow heater.

On vehicles fitted with the four zone system, the rear limate control panel shows a defrost symbol to indicate that the system is in defrost and no air flow wili be available to the rear vents.

The programmed defrost function can be cancelled by one of the following:

•A second press of the DEF switch.   
Selecting any air distribution switch on the TSD.   
Pressing the driver side AUTO switch on the ICP.   
•Switching the ignition OFF.

he AFS control module is located on the bulkhead in the passenger compartment, behind the glove compartment.

The AFS control module is a dual functionality unit which als incorporates software to control the dynamic headamp leveling. The AFS control module is coected to the high speed CAN bus and receivesinputs from other vehicle systems on the status of the following parameters:

Steering angle Vehicle speed Headlamp status •  Engine running • Reverse gear selected Automatic lighting on.

The AFS willoy operate when the AFS control module receives an engine runing signal on the CAN bus. When the engine running signal is received the AFS control module performs an initializtion routine.

### CAN Harness 'Spur' Type Configuration Circuits


Control modules are coected t the CN hamessither in aloop' or 'spur coiguation. In the ooptype cfiguratin the CAN hamesslops into the module via two connector pins) and then loops out of the module via another two connecto pins. In the 'spur' type cofiguation, a hamess spur is spliced into the main 'ackbone' of theCAN hamess and the module is connected to the harness spur via two connector pins.

fa control module is suspected of non-communication, the Network Integrity test application available on the manufacturer

approved diagnostic system can be used to confim if communication is possible between the control modules on the vehicle ante manufacurerapprovediostystevi the9ioscnecThe eultom te test cabe se to determine if either a' single modüle or multiple modules are failing to communicate.

If the Network tegrity test indicates that one or more module on one of the CAN networks (HS or MS) are failing to communicate, there are several checks that can be madeThe first step i to identify if both of the CA teminating modules on each individual CAN Bus are communicating. If both CAN terminating modules for each individual CAN Bus are communicating (identified via the Network Integrity test), then it can be cofirmed that the main backbone' of the CAN harnessis complete. The main 'backbone'o the CN hamess consists of al the modules connected to the CAN harmess via a 'loop' configuration and also includes the two terminating modules.

Communication with both CAN terminating modules via the Network Integrity test confims the physical integrity of the main 'backbone' of the CAN hamess (and the hamess spur to the J1962 diagnostic connector. This means that there i no requirement to check the resistance of the N Network. This is because the standard check for  ms across the AN High andCa Low ies willot provieany aia ifoatin earding the hysical coditiof the  hamess, beod what has already been determined from the Network Integrity test.

If a Network Integrity test reveals a terminating module is failing to communicate it can indicate a break in the main backbone' of the CAn hamess. The first checks should always be to confim the power and ground supplies to the non-communicating moduleare corect.Providing these are corect, the resistance between the CAN High and CAN Low lines at te  coeco ca be checked to detemie he terit o he mai ackone he  hamesAfer doctg the battery a reading of 10 ohms would indicate an opencircuit in the main backbone' of the CAN hamess. Alteratively, a reading of 60 ohms would indicate that there is no open circuit fault with the main 'backone' of the CAN hamess.

It is worth noting that even if one of the terminating modules is disconnected from the CAN hamess, communications betweer the modules stillconnected may stillbe possible.Therefore communication between the manufacturer approved diagnostic system and the connected modúles may also be possible.

In the case where multiple modules, including a terminating module, are failing to communicate, having fist confirmed the power and ground supplies are corect, the approximate location of the open circuit can be identified from analysis of the Network Integrity test esults and reference t the relevant CAN network circuit dagrams. Forexample, if an open circuit existed in a certin position on the CAN hamess any module positioned on the Network between the J1962 connector and the open circuit should retum a response during the Network Integrity test. No responses would be retumed from any modules past the open circuit fault in the Network.

terthe initial checks (Network Integrity test using the manufacturer aproved diagnostic system, and power and ground supplies to the module have been checked and confirmed as corect), a module that is connected to the CAN hamess via a 'spur type configuration is suspected of not communicating, then thé physical integrity of the CAN haness'spur can be checked.

This is most easily undertaken by individually checking the continuity of the CAN High and CAN Low lines between the non-communicating module connector (with the module disconnected) and the J1962 diagnostic connector.

As well as the methods described so far in this document, which can be used to determine the location of an open circuit ir :he CAN hamess, 'Lost Communications' DTCs can also be used for this purpose. Lost communication DTCs mean that a module is not receiving CAN information from another module.

For example if a global DC read were to be carred out, only DTs stored in the modules that the manufacturer approved diagnostic system could communicate with would be displayed. If there was an open ciruit fault in a certain position on the CAN hamess, the modules that could display Ds wouldal be priorto the open circuit on the Network, and these modules should display 'Lost Communications' DTs with al the modules located on the Network past the open circuit fault.

The purpose of this document i to promote quick and eficint minor repairto hamess connectors or cables using approved methods. Repairs may only be made to cables and conectors which have been mechanically notelectricallydamaged It also applies where the whole extent of the damage can be clearly identified and rectified.

Care and neatness are essential requirements in making a perfect repair.

This harness repair guide, does not approve repairs to any of the following circuits:

1.Any media orientated system transport network harnesses.   
Supplement restraint system (SRS) firing circuits (Air bags).   
Link lead assembles, which are unique to safety critical circuits such as anti-lock brake system (AS) and thermocouple circuits. An example of this is the ABS wheel speed sensors with moulded connectors.   
4Screened cables, leads and wiring haress(s).

If any harness(s) with defective electrical connector terminals or wires from the above circuits are a concern, new components müst be installed.

### Multifunction Electronic Modules -


Jpon receiving the'start button pressed' hardwired signal, the  sends a message via the medium speed CAN (controller area network) bus to the KVM initiating the vehicle starting process.

The KM then energizes the low frequency antennas within the vehicle cabin which transmit a 125KHz signal to the Jaguar ar eeoeaeaai ia the authorisation code to the RF receiver.

The RFreciver relays the code, via a serial communication line, to the  which then checks and approves the code as valid The  will only respond to a valid Jaguar Smart Key.

The KVM continues the passive start processby communicating a Jaguar Smart Key valid' signal to the CJ via the medium speed CAN bus, Once the B receives the Jaguar Smart Key authorisation it confis the reponse matches with an intema calculation.

Before the B sends a mobilisation signal to the ECM, via the high speed CAN bus, it will exchange encrypted data with follwing components:

The instrument cluster via the high speed CAN bus,   
The steering column lock via the high speed CAN bus, to authorise unocking the steering column. The steering colum unlocking function is powered by the CiB and grounded via the instrument cluster

When the  receives a hardwired Park/Neutral signal from the JaguarDrive Selector, a high speed CANbus message from the ABS module and a simultaneous star/stop switch ignal it interprets this as an engine crank request.Before the engine crank request is proessed, the  vifieshe brake pressure sial ecivedrom the S module. f theigal is gratr than the stored threshold value, a crank request signal is sent to the ECM on the high speed CAN bus.

Five Low Frequency (LF) antennae for the passive start system are positioned in specific locations within the vehicle.

The KM transmits an LF signal via the antennas which is received by the Smart Key. The Smart Key then responds by :ransmitting a RF signal which is received by the RF receiver and passed to the KVM for authorization.

Depending on the weight of the occupant and the severity of the collision, the mechanisms begin to operate at a relative impact speed of between aproximately 8.7 and11.2 mph (13.9 and 17.9 km/h). At the point f a rear pact, the foward energy of the impact and the inertia of the occupant combineto push the backrest aginst the occupant's back. That causes the s mechanism to begin a controlled sequence of movements. First, while remaining in an upright position, the backrest moves rearwards by approximately 50 mm. Next, the backrest reclines through an angle ependant upon the direction and relative speed of the collision, up to a maximum of approximately 15 degrees.

The combined effect of these movements i to absor some of the energy of the impact and reduce therelative accleration of nead and body, thereby helping to reduce the possibility of whiplash injury.

CAUTIONS:

Make sure that the vehicle is clean and dry prior to commencing this procedure.

Make sure that the vehicle is kept in a dry environment and is not washed within 24 hours of completing this procedure, failure to follow this instruction will prevent the slip coat from curing correctly.

NOTE: The lubricant used in this procedure (LIP Ac612/21) is part of the Squeaks & Rattes Kit. For more formatio on the Squaks & Rattes it safety data sheets and detail o how to order the kit or part thereof please visit (www.squeaksandrattles.info).

Open the roof opening panel glass to the full tilt position Insert a suitable applicator card in to the position shown at the left hand front cormer of the rear glass roof panel.

![](images/_MISSING_8641af0f9d7fc3019c9804aec10529dadae669ceb0e51dc792d3b44803fcdcdb.jpg)

![](images/_MISSING_aeaa2a7885e7e8202ee77646d2e2c91c22edf9a2a62d6e0702ff0d983231fcf4.jpg)  
E142600

3. CAUTION: Make sure that the two areas that are cleaned with the applicator card overlap at the centre of the veiclle.

Starting at position 1 in the left hand front corner of the rear glass roof panel, carefully slide the applicator card around the rear gláss roof panel through position 2 and past the centre point of the vehicle.   
Remove and clean the applicator card.   
Starting at position 3 in the right hand front comner of the rear glass roof panel, carefully slide the applicator card around the rear glass roof panel through position 4 and past the centre point of the vehicle.   
Remove and clean the applicator card.

![](images/_MISSING_1835a53e74b951a2a523db1e3a5e9bb06f8d70d22e492aeea3ab28ba28d43f4c.jpg)

4. CAUTION: Make sure that the bottle is well shaken before applying the fluid to the applicator card.

Insert a suitable applicator card in to the position shown at the left hand front corner of the rear glass roof panel. Spray a sufficient amount of LIP AC612/21 fluid on to the applicator card until the fluid runs between the rear glass fixed panel and the seal.

![](images/_MISSING_76fcdd0c2b2b3a383dff634ceb6f090ac214cca9945d0c40fcaba4f166130109.jpg)  
E142600

5. CAUTION: Make sure that the applicator card does not slip from under the rear glass roof panel as the card is rotated around the corners.

Carefully slide the applicator card along the edge of the rear fixed glass panel to position 2.   
Slide the applicator card backwards and forwards from position 1 to 2 to make sure that a sufficient amount of fluid is applied to the rear fixed glass panel.   
If required, apply more fluid to the applicator card and repeat the above step.

6. CAUTION: Make sure that the applicator card does not slip from under the rear glass roof panel as the card is rotated around the corners.

At the position 2, spray a sufficient amount of LIP AC612/21 fluid on to the applicator card until the fluid rúns between the rear glass fixed panel and the seal. Rotate the applicator card backwards and forwards 5 times at the corner of the rear fixed glass panel.

E142603

![](images/_MISSING_ff97f18d19666757ed274845ebe15bbe3ab4905a5452192102b94f5265c49b13.jpg)

E142600

7. CAUTION: Make sure that the applicator card does not slip from under the rear glass roof panel as the card is rotated around the corners.

Carefully slide the applicator card along the edge of the rear fixed glass panel from position 2 past the centre of the vehicle.   
If required, apply more fluid to the applicator card   
and repeat the above step.   
Remove and clean the applicator card.

Repeat steps 4 to 7 for the other side of the vehicle.

Wipe away any excess fluid.

The SRS (supplemental restraint system) provides additional protection for vehicle occupants in certain impact conditions by selective activation of twin stage driver and passengerair bags, side ir bagside ir curtains and front safety belt pretensioners. Operation of the system is controlled by a RCM (restraints control module).

The RCM receives inputs from various sensors around the vehicle to detemine which devices i any, should be activated durin anacident.The inputs include those from an occupant monitoring system for the front passengerseat front and side impact sensors and side pressure sensors.

In all markets except NAS, a PAD (passenger air bag deactivation) switch is a dealerfit ption that allows the passenger il bag to be disabled.'

The activation status of the passengerir bag is given by an indicator on the veread console.The status of the SRS i iven by an air bag warning indicator in the instrument luster.

When the RCM outputs any of the fire signals it also outputs a crash signal to the  and the ECM on the high speed CAN. he crash signal is also hardwired to the M and the .On receipt of the crash signal, the ECM cuts the power supply to he fuel pump relay and the ClB goes into crash mode. In the crash'mode, the CJB:

Activates all of the unlock signals of the vehicle locking system, even if the vehicle is already unlocked.   
Ignores allocking/superlocking inputs until it receives an'unlock input, when it retums the lócking system to normal operation. Activates the interior lamps. The interior lamps remain on permanently until they are manuallyswitched offat the lamp unit, or the ClB crash mode is switched off and they return to normal operation. Disables the rear window child lock input until the crash mode is switched off. Activates the hazard flashers. The hazard flashers remain on unti cancelled by the hazard waming switch or the crash mode is switched off.

CJB crash mode is switched off by a valid locking and unlocking cycle of the locking system.

The buckle of each front safety belt incorporates a switch that provides a safety belt status signal to the RCM. The RCM broadcasts the status on the high speed CAN bus for use by the safety belt reminder and beltminder systems in the instrument cluster.

In the event of a front impact, the RCM willdeploy the pretensioners provided the safety belt buckles are fastened. The pretensioners have a lower deployment threshold than the air bags. Hence it is possible during a minor collision, which exceeds the deployment threshold, that only the pretensioners will deploy.

There are two types of occupant monitoring:

In all markets except NAS and Australia, vehicles have an occupant detection system.   
•In NAS markets, vehicles have an occupant classification system.

The pedestrian protection system is designed to mitigate injuries in a pedestrian colision with the vehicle. It does this by utiliing a pair of pyrotechnic actuators to lift the hood awa from the engine, creating a cushioned impact between the pedestrian and the 'vehicle.

The pedestrian protection system is controlled by the RCM (restraints control module), but operates independently of the SRS (supplemental restraint system).   
Refer to: Air Bag and Safety Belt Pretensioner Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) (501-20 Supplemental Restraint System, Description and Operation).

edestrian protection is also provided by passve protection integrated into the bumper system and the structure of the hood.

The pedestrian protection system is operational when the vehicle is traveling at speeds between approximately 20 and 45 <m/h (12.4 and 28 mph). A vehicle speed signal is received by the RCM over the high speed CAN bus.

The system is able to determine if contact is made with a pedestrian or anotherbject, such as a traffic cone, using sigal from the pedestrian impact sensors. When the system determines contact is made with a pedestrian, i fres the hood actuators to lift the rear of the hood approximately 130 mm (5.2 in.) within 35 ms of the fire' signal.

When an impact condition is registered, the RCM outputs an impact signal on the high speed CAN bus. This signal is used by the  t initiate the haard waing amps.  thi ccurs, the hazard waming amp switch is diabled for the remainder of the current ignition cycle.

If the RCM detects a fault with the system, it outputs a message on the high speed CAN bus to the instrument cluster message center. On receipt of this, the message center will display the mesage Check Pedestrian System.

When the vehicle is delivered from the factory the pedestrian protection system i in a safe'plant' mode. Normal operating u ceiaaproed digeprdlieiecritdeliv to the customer.

Galvanic corosion is the cross-contamination of dissimilar metals, in this case aluminium and steel. Avoidance of galvanic corrosion is an important issue to be considered in the repair of aluminium bodied vehicles. Precautions to prevent the contamination of exposed bare aluminium surfaces should be taken. Good housekeeping and cleanliness should be adopted throughout repairs and especiall prior to welding, pre-treatment and adhesive bonding. The repair environment requires control and protection from dust and debris from conventional stee body repairs.Aleuipment must be clearly identified and used solely on aluminium. Tools should be kept clean and in good order. Stee fastenings are coated to prevent galvanic corosion. Fastenings should be examined during repairs and where damaged or suspect must be renewed. The use of graphite penetrating oil, or copper based anti-seize compounds upon the steel fixings is not recommended.

test weld using identical coupons from waste panels should take place prior to working on the vehicle. The test piece is then isually checked and destructively tested to make sure all settings are corect and an acceptable weld has been achieved.

Prior to starting, the following should be checked:

Gas - Correct for the type of job Filler Wire - Correct for the type of material to be welded

An effective weld should demonstrate the following qualities:

All visible weld surfaces shall be clean, bright and of a uniform profile The weld seam should show uniform height and width over its entire length There shall be complete fusion between the surfaces of the work piece and the weld metal deposit

Correct level of penetration will be visible at the rear of the coupon as a fine continuous line.

Weld inspections take the form of a visual examination, non-destructive and destructive testing.

Galvanic corrosion is the cross-contamination of dissmilar metals, in this case aluminium and steel.Avoidance of galvanic corrosion is an important issue to be considered in the repair of aluminium bodied vehicles.

Precautions to prevent the contamination of exposed bare aluminium surfaces should be taken. Good housekeeping and cleanliness should be adopted throughout repairs and especially prior to welding, pre-treatment, (Pyrosil), and adhesive bonding.

The repair environment requires control and protection from dust and debris from conventional stee body repairs. All equipment must be clearly identified and used solely on aluminium.

Tools should be kept clean and in good order Steel fastenings are coated to prevent galvanic corosion. Fastenings should be examined during repairs and where damaged or suspect must be renewed.

The use of graphite, penetrating oil, or copper based anti-seize compounds upon the steel fixings is not recommended.

Some leaks originate here, or only occur here.   
The relevant passenger compartment should be checked using a torch during the wash procedure.

If no leaks are located during the tests above, road tests should be carried out on wet roads. Road tests under various conditions:

- At various speeds.   
- On various road surfaces (asphalt to cobbles).   
- With loaded or unloaded vehicle.   
- Driving through puddles (splash water).

Increasing mileage has an effect on the problem of leaks in a vehicle. Possible influencing factors are:

Servicing and maintenance of seals: - No maintenance, lack of maintenance or incorrect maintenance - Using an incorrect agent   
Damaged seals: - As a result of aging, wear or incorrect handling/assembly.   
Heavy soiling of the vehicle: '- Heavy soiling of a vehicle can seriously impair the function of water drainage channels in particular, and also of rubber seals.   
Age-related factors: Environmental factors - UV radiation -Extreme climatic conditions   
Corrosion can have a serious impact on bodywork, in particular as a result of: - Lightly or heavily rusted'seal carriers - Rusted body seal welds Perforation corrosion

If a vehicle develops water leaks, then areas into which water is routed or drained should be checked first.

he five most important sources of non-axle noise are exhaust, tires, roo racks, trim and mouldings, and transmission.

herefore, make sure that none of the follwing conditions are the cause of the noise before proceeding with a driveline te lown and diagnosis.

Under certain conditions, the pitch of the exhaust may sound very much like gear noise. At other times, it can be mistaken for a wheel bearing rumble Tires,especially snow tires, can have a high pitched tread whine or roar, similar to gear noise. Radial tires, to some degree, have this characteristic. Also, any non-standard tire with an unusual tread construction may emit a roar or whine type noise Trim and mouldings can also cause whistling or a whining noise Clunk may be a metallic noise heard when the automati transmission is engaged in reverse or drive, or it may occur when the throttle is applied or released. It is caused by backlash somewhere in the driveline Bearing rumble sounds like marbles being tumbled. This condition is usually caused by a damaged wheel bearing

OPEN REAR DIFFERENTIAL - V8 5.0L PETROL AND TDV6 3.0L DIESEL VEHICLES

![](images/_MISSING_ae012d6723b9195d2c403899cdfb993b663744ada293dbae2883894ff9bdc4a1.jpg)

The rear differential has two functions:

to convert the 'angle of drive' through  and distribute drive, via the rear drive halfshafts, to the rear wheels.   
to compensatefor differences in the rotational spees of the vehicle's rear wheels during coerig.

Two types of rear differential are installed:

an open rear differential on V8 5.OL Petrol AND TDV6 3.0L Diesel vehicles an electric rear differential on V8 S/C 5.0L Petrol vehicles.

Both types ofear differential are attached to the rearubframe at fourmounting points.Each mounting point incoporates rubber bush to reduce NVH (noise, vibration and harshness). The bushes in the forward mounting points are installed in the differential. The bushes in the rear mounting points are installed in the rear subframe.

The pendifeential are almostdentical in their desig and differ ony in the final drive rati and a heavier input flage which ifittet .isel ices.The ial riveatisorte e and the ectriardiffnt re asfollws

•V8 S/C 5.0L Petrol, V8 5.0L Petrol - 2.56:1 TDV6 3.0L Diesel - 2.44:1.

Rotational iput from the drive shaft is passed via the iput flange to the pinion shaft and pinion gear.The angles of the oinion gear to the crown wheel drive gear moves the rotational direction through 90°.

The transferred rotational motion is now passed to the crown wheel drive gear which in tum rotates the diffrential casing. The cross-shaft, which is secured to the casing, also rotates at the same speed as the casing.The planet gears, which ar mounted on the shaft also rotate with the caing. In tum, the planet gears transfer their rationa motion to the left and right hand sun gears, 'rotating the drive halfshafts.

When the vehiceis moving in a fowar direction the torque applied trough the diferential to each sun gear iequal. th condition both drive halfshafts rotate at the same speed and the planet gears do not rotate.

If the vehicle ituming the outerwheel willbe fored to rotate faster thanthe ier whel by having a greater distance to travel. The iffentiasenses the torque diffrence between the sun gears. The planet gears rotate n theiraxes to allow the outer wheel to rotate faster than the inner one.

The multiplate clutch prevents excessie diffential lip and therefore maximizes the traction perfomance of the vehicle.This is fundamentall different from braked' traction control systems, which can only counteract diffrential slip when it occurs.

Acertain amount of differential slip i required to allw the vehicle to tum comers and to remain stable under control of the ABS(anti-lock brake system).The system i completely automatic and does not require any special driver input.

The multiplate clutch actively controls the torque flow through the differential and optimizes the torque distriution in the driveline.The clutch biasesthe torque from the differential to the wheel with the higher grip and prevents the whee with the lower grip from spinning.

The instrument cluster is connected to the TM via the high speed CAN bus. Transmission status is transmited by the TCM and displayed to the driver in the instrument cluster. Refer to: Instrument Cluster (413-01 Instrument Cluster, Description and Operation).

The transmission status display is located in the tachometer.The display shows the JaguarDrive selector position. When the transmission is in the Jaguar sequential shift mode the current gear is displayed in the information window.

When the transmission is in the Jaguar sequential shift mode, the appearance of the instrument cluster changes to the dynamic mode and the current gear is displayed in the informátion window.

The TM outputs signals to control the shift control solenoid valve and the EPRs (electronic pressure regulating solenoid to control the hydraulic operation of the transmission.

The TCM processes signals from the transmission speed and temperature sensors, the ECM and other vehicle systems. From the recived sial iputs and preprogrammed data the module calulates the corrct gear torque converter cutch seting and optimum pressure settings for gear shift and lock-up clutch control.

The ECM supplies the engine management data over the high speed CAN bus. The TCM requires engine data to efficiently control the transmission peration, forexample; fywheetqueenginespeed, accelerat pedaangle engne emperature. The steing angle sensor and the AS(anti-lok brake system) module also supply data to the M o the high speed CN bus. The M uses data from these systems to suspend gear changes when the vehicle is comering and/or the ABS module i controlling braking or traction control.'

Using the signal inputs and the memorized data, the TCM control program computes the corect gear and torque converter lock-p clutch setting and the optimum pressure setings for gearshift and lock-up clutch contro Special output-side modules (power output stages, curent regulator circuits), allw the M to control the solenoid valves and pressure regulators and consequently precisely control the hydraulics of the automatic transmission. In addition, the amount and duration of engine interventions are supplied to the engine management by way of the CAN bus.

The transmission has a full electronic JaguarDrive selector with no Bowden cable connection to the transmission. The transmission selections are made using a rotay JaguarDrive selector which rises from the floor console once the engie s runing. Rotati of the JrDrive selectort any of the five positinsis sesed by the  vithe high speed C bus. The M then reacts according to the selected position.The '(sport) position selection allows the M to operate the transmission using the semi-automatic 'Jaguar Sequential Shift'."

Gear selections are sensed by the TM when the driver operates the steering wheel paddle switches. Once the JaguarDrive selector position is confirmed, the TCM outputs appropriate information on the high speed CaN bus.

fthe JaguarDrive selecto  n' aguar Sequential Shift i permanent and can only be cancelled by pressing and holding he + paddle for approximately 2 seconds or by moving the JaguarDrive selector to thé 'D' position.

The TCM can be reprogrammed using a Jaguar approved diagnostic system using a flash code. The TCM processor has a 440k intemaash memory. f this capacity, approximately  are used by the basic transmission program. The remainder approximately 70 kb is used to store vehicle-specific application data.

he fluid pump i an integral part of the transmission. The fluid pump is used to supply hydrulic pressure for the peration of :he control valves and clutches, to pass the fluid through the transmission cooler and to lubricate the gears and shafts.

The Z HP8 fluid pump is a crescent type pump and is located between the intermediate plate and the torque converter. The pump has a delivery rate of 16 cm3 per revolution.

The pump comprises a housing, a crescent spacer an impllrand aring gear The housing has inlet and outlet pots todirec low and is located inthe intemediate plate y a centring pin. The pump action is achieed by the mpeller ig gearand crescent spacer.

The crescent spacer i fixed n its position by a pin and is located between the ring gearand the impelle. The mpeller s driven by drive from the torque coverterhub which i located on a needle roller baring in the pump housing.The impeller teeth mesh with those of the ring gear When the impelle i rtated the motion is trasferred to the ring gar which rotates in the same direction.

The rotational motion of the ring garand the mpeller collets fluid from the ntake port n the spaces between the teeth. When the teeth reach the crescent spacer the il is traped in the spaces between the teeth and icarred with the rtation of the gearsThe spacertapers nearthe utlet port.This reducesthe space between the gearteth causing build up of fluid pressure as the oil aches the outlet port. When the teeth passthe end of the spacer the pressurized fluid is rleased into the outlet port.

The fluid emerging from the outlet port is passed through the fluid pressure control valve. At high operating speeds the pressure control valve maintains the output pressure to the gearbox at a predetermined maximum level. Excess fluid is relieved from the pressure control valve and is directed, via the main pressure valve in the valve block, back to the pump inlet port. This provides a pressurized feed to the pump inlet which prevents cavitation and reduces pump noise.

The temperature sensor is also located in the Mechatronic valve block. The TCM uses the temperature sensor signals to deterine the temperature of the transmission fluid. The planetary gear trains used on the ZF 6HP28 transmission comprise a single web planetary gear train and a double web planetary geartrain. These geartrains are known as Lepelltier type gear trins and together produce the six foward gears and the one reverse gear.

### Automatic Transmission/Transaxle - Transmission Fluid Level Check


The M is an integral part of the Mechatronic valve block which is located at the bottom of the transmission, within the fluic an. The TCM is the main controlling component of the transmission.

The TCM processes signals from the transmission speed and temperature sensors, ECM and other vehicle systems. From the received signal inputs and pre-programmed data, the module calulates the corect gear, torque converter clutch setting an optimum pressure settings for gear shift and lock-up clutch control.

CAUTION: The vehicle should not be driven if the fuid level is low as intemal failure can result.

NOTE: The transmission fluid temperature must not be allowed to exceed 50°C (122F) whilst checking level. Should the .emperature rise above this figure, abort the check and allow the transmission fluid to cool to below 30°C (86°F).

This vehicle is not equipped with a fluid level indicator. An incorrect level may affect the transmission operation and could esult in transmission damage. To correctly check and add fluid to the transmission.

Afluid level that is too high may cause the fluid to become rated due to the chuing action of the tating itemal parts. A low fluid level could result in poor transmission engagement, slipping, or damage. This could also indicate a leak in oneo :he transmission seals or gaskets.

which in any way may result in the productión of sparks

Ensure that adequate ventilation is provided when volatile degreasing agents are being used.

Keep oils and solvents away from naked fames and othersoures oitionDo not apply heat in an attempt to ree seizedut o fitting; a wellas causig damage to protective coating, there irisk f amage from stray heat to electron equipment and brake lines.Do not leave tools, equipment, spilt oil etc. around the work area. Message center - Displays system information to the driver.

The information and messages which can be displayed in the instrument cluster are mainly generated from other system control modules. When a system control module detects a change or a fault which is tagged to generate a message, an electronic signal is sent vi the medium or high speed CAN (controller area network) bues to the instrument cluster which displays the message. I more than one message i requested the instrument cluster displays them in order of priority.

In the combined mode, the sensors emit a series of ultrasonic impulses and thenswitch to receiver mode to receive the echo reflected by an ostace within the detection range.The recived echo signals are amplified and converted from an analoue signal to a digital signal by the sensor. The digitl signal is passed to the parking aid module and compared with pre-progammed data stored  an EERom(lectricaly erasable progammable read ony memory) within the module.The module receives this data via the sigal line from the sensor and calculates the distance from the oject using the elapsed time between the transmitted and reived impulse. The duration of the impulse duration is determined by the module, with the sensor controlling the frequency of the impulse output.

n receiver mode, the sensor receives impulses that were emitted by adjacent sensors. The module uses this information to orecisely determine the position and distance of the object.

If no objects are detected there are no further waming tones. I an object is detected, repeated audible tones are emitted from either the front or rear audio speakers as appropriate. The time delay between the tones decreases as the distance between the object and the vehicle decreases, until at approximately 300 mm (12 inches), the audible tone becomes continuous.

After the itial detection of an oject ithere i no dereasein the distance between an oject and the central sensors, the time delay between the audible wamings remains constant. If an object is detected by one of the comer sensors only, the audible warings stop after approimately  seconds if there is no change in the distance between an object and the comer sensor.

When approaching several objects within detection range, the control module recognises the distance from the vehicle to the

nearest object.

The PC module wil pririise the bjects detected, the earest bject detected willtake priority and the coresponding audio outputs willbe emittedForexampl if  bject are detected one front one rear the nearest detected bject wil take priority and relevant audible tone will be heard.

If o objects are detected at equal distance one front ne rear the audible tones willalteate between the front and rear speakers.

Ifreverse  ithe firt arleted after theiition iihedon, both thefront if fttedand rearparking id sensor will become perational. f a foward drive gear isubsequently selected, the front and ear parking aidsensors wil remain operational until vehicle spee increases above 16 km/h (10 mph), park (P) is selected or the PDC control switch is pressed.

Ifdrive  is the first gear selected after the ignition i switched on the parking aid system will have to be activated by pressing the PDC control switch.

The components of the audio/fotainment system are allconnected on the Media Orientated Systems Transport MoST ring. The MoSTring i afire optic communiatios bus for multimedia applications.Audi and control ifomation ipassedaround the MoST ing and can be picked up by any of the systems unit.For example, radio sation tuning/selection iput by the vhice uset the Touch Sreen Dispa ent log the oSTigand collee y the teteAudi odule (IAM) which then selects the requested radio station.

MOST technology uses a plastic optical fibre which forms a network connecting the audio and multimedia system components. Each component in the ring is connected to the plasti optical fibre through adevice known as a Fiber Optial Transceiver (OEach FoT has two optical conections; one conection is sensitive to light and i the nput, the seond conection foms the light soure and ithe output.The system perates by coecting the utput rom one Ft to the iput of another FOT

The light signals are sent in one direction only and are formed in the following way:

Electrical signals are converted into an electrical current   
The current then drives an LED (light emitting diode) in the FOT to produce a high intensity red light The LEd transmits the light through a fiber optic cable   
A photo diode in the FOT at the opposite end of the fiber optic cable detects the light.

The following components may be connected to the MOST ring dependant on the vehicle equipment level:

Satellite Digital Audio Radio Service (SDARS) (NAS only - if fitted) Power audio amplifier   
Instrument cluster   
Telephone control module (if fitted)   
Navigation computer (if fitted)   
Televison (TV) tuner (if fitted).

Diagnosis:

Ingress of water into A-pilla area or instrument cluster area and rocker panel area.

Cause:

- Breaks in adhesive beads.   
- The breaks in adhesive beads can be located from inside by using compressed air. The leak can be identified   
from outside by the escaping air.   
- The second test method is by means of a water test. The outer trims must be raised careful using a plastic wedge. The leak should be lócated from inside by a second assistant.

Corrective action:

- Remove the windscreen. Remove the existing adhesive bead and reapply using the correct bonding procedure.

he forward alert and Advanced EBA system response to an imminent rear-end collsion with another moving vehicle reacts r he following order:

1st stage precharge - If a colision is judged to be credible and the driver takes no action then Advanced EBA will prepare the brake system by requesting a fixed precharge brake pressure (approximately 3 bar). In a collion, the sudden deceleration or acceleratio is measured by the impact sensors and the accelerometers in the RCM. The RCM evaluates the readings to determine the impact point on the vehice and whether the deceleration/accleration radingexceed theimit for firig any of thei bag and preteiners.During a colion heoniesthe i ba and pretensioners if the safing functio cofis that the data from the impact sensor(s indicates an impact limit has been exceeded.

The RCM incorporates the following impact thresholds to cater for different accident scenarios:

Front impact, pretensioners.   
Front impact, driver and passenger air bags stage 1, belt unfastened.   
Front impact, driver and passenger air bas stae 1, belt fastened.   
Front impact, driver and passenger air bags stage 2, belt unfastened.   
Front impact, driver and passenger air bags stage , belt fastened.   
Rear impact.   
Driver side impact.   
Passenger side impact.

For markets that have an occupant classification system, this provides the RCM with the occupancy status of the front passengerseat.The restraint control module uses this and theseat bucke status in the elation ofthe firing strategy fo the passenger air bag, the passenger side air bag and the front passenger safety belt pretensioner.

he occupant classification system can determine if the front passenger seat is unoccupied, occupied by a small person, or ccupied by a large person. The occupant classification system consists of:

A pressure pad, installed under the cushion of the front passenger seat, which is connected to a pressure senso A safety beit ténsion sensor, integrated into the anchor point of the front passenger safety belt. An occupant classification module, installed under the front passenger seat.

'he pressure pad is a silicone filled bladder. Any load on the pressure pad is detected by the pressure sensor.

The safety belt tension sensor is a strain gauge that measures the load appied by the safety belt anchor to the anchor bolt.   
The sensor is located in the lower safety belt anchor point.

The occupant classification module supplies a rference voltage to the pressure sensor and the safety belt tension sensorand, from the retumed signals, measures the loads acting on the pressure pad and the safety belt tension sensorThe load measurement from the safety belt tension sensor is used to produce a corection factor for the load measurement from the pressure adThe itess of the aet belt affet the lad acing on the pressue pad so witout the corction fache occupant classification module cannot derive an accurate occupancy status.

The occupant classication module traslates the lad readings into a seat occupancy status and transmits the result to the RCM, on a dedicated high speed CAN bus link. The occupant classfication module incorporates two load limits for the seat ushion: When the loadexceeds the lower imit, but i lessthan the upperimit, the ccupant is classied assmall; when the upper limit is exceeded, the occupant is classified as large.
